title: Coby Bryant, Braxton Jones, Montez Sweat on Day 2 of veteran minicamp | Press Conference
text: What have you learned about the intensity of your head coach? >> Yeah, I I love it. Honestly, I love it. He's filled with fire, honestly. Um, just obviously he's offensive guy as well, too. But we have a lot of similarities. Hence, that's why I'm here as well. He's a true competitor. Every day he competes. He likes likes us talking, you know, junk to him and vice versa. He talks junk to us, too. And, um, so I match his energy every day and vice versa. So, it's it's been a special offseason for sure. >> Your similarities, are you as intense as? >> Absolutely. Absolutely. I'm I'm a true competitor. I don't care if it's walking down the street. I want to walk faster than somebody else. So, I don't care what it is. >> What do you interception? >> Just me being me, honestly, and you know, the guys up front doing their job and um you know, just everyone playing together and me just making a play. >> Yesterday, Khif Raymond was talking about how he was very impressed with the makeup of the roster. as a newcomer, what's been your read of of just the guys that you've been working around for >> Definitely. Um, a ton of a great group of guys, honestly. You know, obviously I'm still getting to know everyone, but just being here this short amount of time has been special, honestly. We laugh. Uh, we put in a lot of work and guys are willing to work, like I said, and it it's been fun. It's going to be a great year for sure. >> Dylan, you've been where sorry, Kobe, you've been where Dylan is now. Um, uh, what are the challenges that he's going to face and how can you help him through that? >> Yeah. Um, honestly, just the biggest thing is just taking care of his body and um, just being coachable, which he is. He's very, very smart, intelligent. Obviously, the tape speaks for itself as well, too. But it's going to be a long year for him, you know, just coming from the combine and just all the meetings and everything. So, just taking care of his body and taking it one week at a time. And, uh, any questions? I'm always there for him. >> What have you seen from him so far, particularly with speed and how he moves on the field? >> Yeah, well, first things first, uh, me being a year five guy, he's a rookie, so he wants to go full speed and everything. So, uh, during individual drills, we have to tell him, you know, slow down cuz I'm not running that fast. Um, I'm 27, he's 21. So, but just the speed, um, he's he's very coachable, like I said. Um, he's exciting to watch, man. He makes plays every day, so it's been special. >> How do you see the speed translate? How does it how does it become football functional when you're out here? >> Yeah. For him or just in general? >> For him? Yeah. >> Um, obviously, you know, he he's, like I said, like I said, he's a great football player. when he sees something, he recognizes he makes a play right away. Um, that's the biggest thing, especially playing safety in this defense as well. And, um, like I said, he has he has had a great spring and I know he'll continue to grow. >> You have guys who ask you about the Super Bowl or kind of the things that it took to get there. >> Yeah. Um, they they they ask, you know, the biggest thing is I tell them, you know, just take it one day at a time, one play at a time, one game at a time. You know, I try not to use, you know, my past, what I did in Seattle, you know, with these guys. The biggest thing I came here to do is be a leader and um you know direct these guys and lead these guys and vice versa. I need to be led as well too um other leaders. So that's the biggest thing. Are >> you starting to kind of figure out your own leadership style here and kind of what is that? >> Yeah, for sure. Um just who I am um and not to, you know, blow smoke up for myself, but just, you know, a lot of guys respect me and um how I go about myself and you know, how I practice. Um you know, DA, uh Ben, a lot of guys have, you know, commended me on that as well too. and you know, I just go out and be the example. So, >> you're a Super Bowl champion >> and recognition. How tough a skill is that? What do you see in him? Especially for somebody who that's he's a rookie, >> right? Uh that's a special trait. You can't teach that honestly. Um that's just knowing football and trusting in his ability and um like I said, he's been doing a great job and he continues to make plays. >> You're Super Bowl champion. Do you see how people kind of regard you a little bit differently in the locker room? >> Honestly, no. Um, I'm just, you know, the same as them, honestly. Obviously, I won the Super Bowl, but like I said, I'm here now. Um, I'm a bear even, you know, all the way, honestly. Um, it's whatever questions they have, like I said, I answer them, but like I said, I just try to be here present where my feet are and, um, be that leader to get there again. >> Now that you're competing against Caleb on a daily b basis, what what what's left an impression on you about what he is, >> man? And like I said from day one, um he's elite, honestly. And that's why, like I said, he's a cover of Madden. And that's always exciting as well, too. I got his back no matter what. Um great player. Um just elite. He shows me something different every day, honestly. Um you know me and just being a leader. I try to give him a different look. Um honestly, and and challenge him and he challenged me for sure. He's he's a special talent, honestly. >> You were able to get him today. What What happened on the on the pick play? >> Yeah. Um you know, that's just me, like I said, just making a play. you know, I had to get him before, you know, the off seasonason started as well, too. So, feel good about that. I know he didn't like that. I seen his demeanor on that one. But, um, like I said, true competitor. Comes out every day willing to work, and, you know, I can't speak enough about him. He's honestly too too talented for sure. >> Are you starting to get a sense of Are you starting to get a sense of how DA best wants to use your skill set and how it fits you? >> Well, it's it's still early right now. Obviously, there's a lot of more things we need to put in and and do, but as right now, I'm definitely uh getting a feel for it. And like I said, whatever he needs me to do, I'm willing to do. So, honestly, >> guys had conversations with you about what to expect from training camp under Ben. >> Yeah. Uh I actually just had a couple conversations with it being especially today. You know, it was very hot out there. I haven't experienced anything like that since college. So, um but I know we're going to go out there and compete and um the weather's going to be hot, but ultimately we got a great the great group of guys and it'll be it'll be fun for sure. I've noticed you're building a connection with Jaylen Johnson. What have you like learned about him and how you guys kind of >> Yeah. Uh first he I didn't know he was the same age as me. Honestly, I thought he was older. So, that was a good thing about that. But, um we he knows somebody I I used to play with in Seattle as well too. And like I said, he's like me as well too. A true competitor. He puts in a ton of work before and after. Um obviously great talent. Um and and you know, we've been connecting very well for sure. >> Did you tell him you thought he was older? >> Yeah. Yeah, honestly when like the first day he got here, I'm like I definitely thought you were like 29, but he's same age as me. So that was that was pretty cool. >> Ben said this off season, I think it was like right after your guys' first meeting when you were here as a free on your free agent visit. He's like he's one of those guys that if you take football away from him, I don't I don't know >> if you didn't have football. Do you have like what else do you think you would do? >> Yeah, absolutely. Um ton of stuff honestly. I did graduate college um you know with my communication degree as well. um started my masters, want to go back and finish that as well in sports administration. Um so there's a ton of stuff I I can get into. Honestly, football is doesn't define me as a person, just what I you know do well and uh just one of the things I do well and um honestly there's a ton of things lined up for me after football as well. >> What do you think communications degree that can go a long way? >> Yeah. Uh be a sports analyst um somewhere in that field, work on ESPN, things like that. Broadcaster, whatever the case may be. Yeah. >> What do you do? What do you do for the What do you do for the next six weeks? after tomorrow >> spent time with the family and then put in a ton of work honestly take care of my body. I know that this offseason is going to be very important just with it my earlier was a little shorter just because we played in the Super Bowl obviously. So just put in a ton of work and spend time with the family and you know just get away honestly when they start to you know be overwhelming then I was so >> you when you're on an elite defense at what point in training camp last year did you feel that? Honestly, it wasn't until the season, middle of the season where I knew we were elite because obviously the training camp is where you put in a ton of work. There's going to be ups and downs. Um, that's just part of it. But I just knew in middle of the season that how special we were. >> Oh, I hear a phone. >> Uh, a lot. Um, you know, he's obviously he has a a good career of, you know, great stats and everything he's done. Um, but it was it was great just uh having one-on-one time, working with other uh tackles and and stuff like that. Just uh getting the base right again. Um, repetition, doing it over and over again. and then his knowledge and like kind of putting that confidence after coming back from injury or dealing what you know however last last year went and kind of building that confidence back in me and just cuz you know I know I can do it. It's just it's just one of those things you got to you know continuously do. So, he's he was great with that. And then his continued um just love, you know, off the record whenever he's talking about me is just great. And, you know, I I'll be there probably again and working with him again. And, you know, I just I I can't get enough of that truly. >> How do you describe the difference confidence-wise of where you are today versus where you were for much of last year? >> Yeah. No, for sure. I think uh a big piece of it is simply uh feeling right from the lower half and from the injuries. It that's like even last year I was still in a good place, but I just didn't trust it. I didn't trust um the positions I was putting myself in. And when you don't trust that, you're you're never going to, you know, put a good outcome out there. So, um, just continuing to trust that what's what's happened, the the procedures I've had is is fine, and everything's good, everything's strong, and and that's what really what it is, and continue to put myself in those great positions and trusting myself in those great positions. >> How different does it feel that you have a full off season where you're not having to rehab? >> Uh, night and day. Um this was like yeah the the first one since uh I think my second rookie year where truly got that full off season not dealing with anything after and it you know it it means everything to me to be able to get the reps during this OTAAS's um know what we want as a team you know from Ben to my to my coach knowing what we all want is just huge for me and and being able to go out there and and just rep it over and over again and have such a great coach like Dan, you know, just on me about the small details. It's it's it's unbelievable and I'm just blessed to be out there and be able to do OTAAS and stuff. >> What's the mental and emotional track been like for you coming out of last season with the injury, new system, new staff, and then you ended last season I remember we talked in the locker room at the end of last season and there was some legitimate uncertainty about what was next for you. Um and then you come back here and now you're healthy and you know in the competition. What what's that been like for you mentally and emotionally that whole roller coaster? >> Yeah, you know, I'll be front up uh straight up. It's obviously a lot and it can go up and down. Um I will say everything I have, you know, gone through up until this point is happened for a reason, just to get me where I'm at now and building that confidence again. So yeah, it's up and down. It's life. That's what life is. And you know, not getting too low, not getting too high in those moments. And that's what I've constantly learned. And then, you know, with the regime we have now and and Ben, it's just you just see it from top to down like everything that we're doing. So, you can't you really can't live in those lows and highs. Like, you just got to keep on moving, keep on pushing, and that's what we're all trying to do. So, you know, obviously it was up and down, but I can't I'm so grateful for everything that's happened genuinely. >> What were the conversation like when you realized that they they were going to offer you back here? Uh I mean shoot there was a lot of conversation here and there you know obviously it just was trying to get back to a place where you know I had an opportunity to start and um show show my talent and that's that's really what it was you know from conversation with them and as well as with myself and um you know I'm just glad to be in a position where I have the opportunity to start and give my best every day. Braxton, when you're when you're hurt, when you're hurt and not playing, is it more tempting to worry about the future than like like when you were when you were out last year, is that when your mind wandered toward, well, what's going to happen with this contract? Where am I going to be next year? Or or are they unrelated? >> Honestly, you know, looking back on it, I naturally as a human, I would say so. Yes. Like what's going to happen? But honestly, I was genuinely just, you know, trying to be present and do anything I could to help, you know, our team win later in that season and having the opportunity to get back on the field, too, um, later in that season was was was great, too. But naturally, obviously, you know, you think about, you know, the future a little bit, but I wouldn't say I was weighing too heavy on it. I think I really started to realize obviously when, you know, that last game come came to an end with LA here and then I was like, wow. like I started to think about it, but I try to stay present for the most part and help exactly where I could be, you know, for our team. >> You said you're feeling good. You're feeling confident. So, when it comes to the left tackle competition, do you look like the start you look at it like the starting job is yours to lose? >> I mean, I I wouldn't I wouldn't uh I wouldn't say that necessarily. Um, you know, I think we're all competing to win. I wouldn't say it's mine to lose, but I mean, I don't know. The way you worded that just kind of set me up for regardless, but you know, I'm out there competing. Um, you know, I think it's at the end of the day, you know, if you're competing for a job and competing for a starting job, whoever it is, we're all, you know, you don't you don't want to lose that job. So, we're all working to win that job. >> Reframe that question. What can you do when the P when the pads come on in August and the competition get reals? what can you do to to leave no doubt that you were the guy and what what do you feel like you can put on on on the tape that wasn't there last year? >> Yeah, I think uh a big thing for me last year was just uh you know um second half production I'll say um I for the most part um was pretty decent in the first half. I just think with the ankle and injuries like I really um didn't have much coming out in the second half and I think that's the biggest thing is just reps getting as many reps as I can obviously um got to be better in certain areas pass pro run game efficiency all of that is going to come together but I think the amount of reps I can get and just you know turning the body making sure everything's rolling and taking as many reps as I possibly can is going to be the biggest thing to set set me you know apart and and you know everything will come after that. >> Now that you have time, now that you've had like distance from week four of last year, how do you look back at that moment? Like is that something that was a good thing that happened? Was it a reset that was needed or is that motivation now to not have losing your job come be happen again? >> Um I you know there's a a lot that goes into that. um when it comes with that, like I just first of all, I just don't think I was at my best with um uh my injury and and mentally it can be a lot. Um but, you know, I'm grateful for those for that. Um to be able to look back and see that and realize that, you know, I was right there. I just need to trust what I was in and that's simply all it is. So, you know, going back looking at that, I'm very grateful um that it all happened the way I needed just because it kind of, you know, punched me in the face a little bit too as well and made me wake up a little bit like I I genuinely, you know, got to do a lot of things to get better, especially with the injury, you know, I was coming back from. So, you know, I'm just I'm blessed to have that situation and be able to look a more positive light, you know, coming out on it. >> At what point did you get that full trust back in your lower half? Um, I would say like each and every day it's getting it's getting better. But, um, I'd really say working with uh, Terron was was big and um, just trusting those positions, you know, obviously a lot, you know, in pass pro, bore rush, trusting that position with my left leg back. Um, it it helped a lot with him and and trusting those positions, constantly getting in those positions again. And then once I, you know, came here, obviously bullets are flying a little bit faster. You start going against men. So getting that flow and getting back into it. So, you know, it's constantly getting better. But I would say like truly, you know, um, trusting it. I definitely got that with Toron. I'm curious how you've observed Caleb Williams and not only how he handles the small details of like coming out of huddle and those things the responsibility of the quarterback but the big picture things like his overall responsibilities the growing attention and expectations. >> Well, sorry the first part of the question was the >> first part is the details of the game, how he manages that and then the big picture stuff like how he handles general. Yeah, I mean, um, you know, for somebody as as young as he is and the way he comes into the building each and every day, the consistency he has and, you know, we're all human. Um, there's going to be up and down days and the way he just responds is just, you know, exactly where you want someone like him to be. And, you know, I'm very proud of him, how he continues to stay day in and day out doing extra. you know, I always see his car here after when I'm leaving and he's doing doing more stuff, I'm sure, going and and just getting that extra work. So, just the broad picture of it all is going to continue to come together uh like a young guy like that and, you know, I'm just blessed to have him back there and somebody that's constantly working at it. >> Thanks, guys. >> Thank you, guys. God bless. Have a good one. Mont. >> And so Ben was saying that uh he thought he had the best year of his career after watching the self scalper. What did you see for yourself? >> Um uh just a year of uh first year learning uh DA DA's defense DA's defense, getting comfortable, just uh honing back on who who I am, who I am as a player. DA said earlier this offseason he felt like he focused too much on scheme last year and like not enough on fundamentals. How has that been a switch this off season? >> Yeah. Um he's uh toned the um the output a little bit. Uh it's less plays more more fundamentals more worrying about us. You know what I'm saying? And how how we can uh get better with whether that's our get off hand placement striking a block. Not ne not necessarily worrying about the scheme, but just working on uh being the guy in front of us. >> There a fundamental you feel like you pumped in on a lot. >> I mean all all of them like So we just been kind of working all the all the fundamentals from the run technique to pass rush to just everything. So >> have you noticed like a difference? Jon said it feels like night and day from a year ago. Have you noticed a difference with what you guys are doing just because of that focus on fundamentals? >> Um not really. It's to me it's just it's just all football. We are honing in a little bit more on the uh on the fundamentals but uh I mean it's the same defense stuff. >> The outside conversation has been that like your position group as a whole might be the weakness of the team coming into this season. Obviously the front office didn't make heavy investments into your group. What do you think you guys are? Do you hear that conversation? What's your perception? >> Yeah, we hear the chatter. Um it is what it is. I mean, everybody has an opinion. It's our job to go out there and do what we got to do. I hear you. >> What are some of your personal goals this season? Um, I just want to be better than the year before. Like, uh, yeah, he was honing in just, um, being better in my in my fundamentals and, uh, just, >> yeah, >> out there and Ben said earlier that that, you know, uh, they were thrilled that he came back as quickly as he did. What's it like to, you know, after watching him kind of rehab, what's it like to see him back out there? Oh, it's encouraging uh to have a uh a guy out there that was um just a guy that that's another plug in on our um on our defensive line. So, yeah, it's great seeing him out there. >> Sounds like they're expecting more from Austin Booker. What is the key for him to getting better? What advice would you be giving him? >> Yeah, he's he's just scratching the surface. Uh I think he's shown a lot of flashes of of the type of player that he could be. uh he's still young and and still uh just learning the in the ins and outs of being of being a pro. Uh but this guy's a limit. Because obviously the team success last year was more than you'd experienced previously. When you got distance from the season, what do you think brought that all to life here last year? >> Um Ben, >> what specifically struck a chord with you about the way he led? >> I mean, he just uh he worked out us. Uh, we just was all on one accord. Everybody was on the same page and everything was just really about winning. It wasn't about winning, then it was nonexistent. >> Sounds like a mindset. How does that influence what you guys do? >> Oh, that's your question. >> It's like just an attitude, a mindset, you know, an ability to just think on winning on winning terms. >> Yeah. I mean, when we just know Ben is all is all about winning. He don't really care about nothing else. So, I don't care about nothing else but winning. So, everybody just kind of honed in on winning. >> Can you think of a moment early last year when it was clear that he didn't care about something? I mean, was he dismissive of something that that maybe other coaches would have been okay with or was there some moment when you went, "Oh, man. This guy's not messing around." Uh, I probably could attest to maybe towards the end of the year when we didn't have any heaters outside in the cold trying to get he was getting us ready for the uh getting us ready for the winter. So, yeah, that was that was a little different. >> How you getting used? >> When you come back this spring, does Ben feel the same as he did last year? >> Uh, it seems like a little bit. Uh, he's pretty much the same. >> Yeah. >> How new voices on the defense, especially up the middle? Are you getting used to or do you have to get used to like the new voices, the new Kings, whatever it may be? >> Yeah, and I mean those new guys like uh Bush and uh Kobe, they're they're learning defense for the first time just just like I was last year and it's it's going to take some time. That's we've been repping that through uh OTAAS and they're going to rip it again during camp. So, but uh those guys are tremendous leaders. You kind of you see it out there on the field even through OTAA. So, I'm going to I have no uh doubt in my mind that they'll be tremendous communicators. >> With DA bringing so many different like like pressures yesterday, y'all brought a couple corner pressures, safety. You have to like work on like spacing and timing with those guys. A lot of time they coming off the edge. >> Yeah. Um I mean, it's just getting a feel for for your blister. Uh depending on what on who they blissing and really just uh that's kind of just going back to those those fundamentals. If you know what I'm saying, if you're running it the right way, the way the way that they teaching us to run it, then nine times out of 10, eight times out of ten, it should hit. >> The next time we'll see is is when camp arrives, knowing what you experienced last year, what are you anticipating this camp going to be like in July and August? >> Oh, yeah. I'm expecting the worst. Uh, >> be prepared. I guess it it probably hopefully it'll be a little bit more easier this time since I've been through it already. But yeah, live days, hard hitting, long drives, playing preseason games. I'm I'm ready for it. >> I know pads on yet, but anything you've seen from Darnell just facing him a little bit just to see that he's continuing to take those next steps. >> Yeah, he's a uh we was uh talking we was joking today and um I'm keep that to myself. >> Yeah, he's doing good.

title: Ben Johnson on player development during OTAs | Press Conference
text: Good weather again this week, so nice and warm for us and and the guys are powering through, but we're at a good spot right now. So, I'll go ahead and open it up. >> Jaylen said that he's going to need a full off season to recover from muscle surgery. What have you seen from him out there? Do you feel like he's back to himself? Does he see himself to go? >> Um, I don't know that I ever saw himself, so I I it's hard for me to gauge that. Um, particularly this time of year, but uh I I think he had a good day yesterday out there. Um, he's he's been able to stack a few of those throughout the OTAAS and I think uh I think his mind's probably getting more confident in terms of the movements he's making. Um, and so yeah, he's he's a vital part of what we want to do. You know, he's he's been a pro pro bowl caliber player in the past and and hopefully we can get that out of him again this year. match up with him, the match up with him and Luther. How do you think that can benefit each other with Jaylen going against a quick tit quick twitch receiver and then also Luther going up against a strong physical corner? >> Yeah, I mean all of our guys are matched up on them um over the course of of the spring and and throughout training camp. You know, Rome's got length and and more size and and Luther's got a good combination of speed and quickness and then uh Khalif is is a little bit smaller, but he's got a different level of quickness to him. So, um I think it's been good. We've been cycling guys inside and outside and so Jaylen's seen seen the whole gamut of receivers at this point through OTAAS and all of our corners have. It'll be fun once we get to camp and we're able to do one-on- ones as well. I feel like that that uh shines a lot of light on what they can do as well. >> Appeal of Star Rising, you know, with Madden probably his inclusion the NFL top 100. Do you have to talk to him about staying focused or do you have to get involved with managing like this going demand forward, Caleb? >> No, I I'm focused on coaching him. Um, our discussions are always about football. He This is a guy that's grown up in this. Um, he's been a five-star recruit. He's one Heisman. I think he knows how to handle attention and uh, you know, you come to a big city like Chicago, a team that loves their sports and u place that loves their sports and loves the Bears. Um, I think this is kind of what he's built for. So, I I think it's a good good match. >> Ben, what are you looking for from >> yesterday? Uh, and people were asking us who's who's 81 and the speed. When do you see it in person? Is he actually maybe even faster than you thought of what you were getting just seeing the ability of what you could do with him? >> I I don't know if he's faster, but it's uh it's what he showed at LSU and Mississippi State before then. I mean, he he's he's got a long highlight reel in terms of showcasing that speed in the SEC and um he he tends to make a play almost every single day right now that that says, "Okay, if we can harness all this energy and and make sure that we can trust him and that he's going to align where he needs to and run the route the way we need him to, that um we really could could use him and he could be a big weapon for us this year. But that's what we're trying to to harness right now. I think coach L and uh and Isaiah Ford are doing a phenomenal job with him and the rest of the room and getting him up to speed and challenging him. Um and I think he's he's developing the work ethic that we expect uh not only from a receiver but from anyone on offense or or the team >> without pads. What has Braxton been able to show you this spring that gives you some confidence that when you get to pads in the summer, things will look uh like you guys needed to? >> Yeah. Um I don't know that you can say at this point. So um but all all those guys right now, they're doing a phenomenal job in the drill work um taking the coaching from from the coaches there and looking to apply it um as much as we can, as much as the rules allow. But once again, it's it's hard to say uh who's up, who's down, who's trending sideways. You really can't say a whole lot right now. But um I I do think he he would probably tell you. Same as Jaylen, he he's a lot more comfortable in what's being asked of him. And hopefully the game continues to slow down. >> Is Jedric dealing with an injury or will he be out there today? >> Jedric. >> Yeah, Jedric Wells. >> Uh he may be out there today. >> Jaylen, what are you looking for from him beyond just his play as >> Jaylen Johnson? Yeah. >> Uh, beyond just his play on the field like as one of your more established prominent guys, what are you looking for from him >> just beyond the white lines? >> Well, I'm looking for him to be a good teammate. Uh, good strong work ethic. Uh, prepared. I think he's he's done that uh when he's been in the springtime and I think that'll carry over to training camp as well. But, uh, it's like anything we we expect from any of our guys. Any leadership qualities are are gravy on top of that. But um you know we want to get him healthy and we got want to get him available. >> How much of a sense do you have from him from LA given how limited you guys how limited his availability was last year? Like how much of a Ben Johnson guy he is? How on board he is with your culture? >> He's doing everything that we ask of him. So I'm very pleased with where he's at right now. >> Qualities are you already seeing in Kobe and how he is connecting with Dylan? It's easy to see their speed even this time of year. >> Yeah. Well, he's one of those guys. He knows what good football and bad football looks like. He just came from a Super Bowl winning team. And I I think that you there there is a there's a premium on that experience. I mean, I think that easily resonates with all the guys in the locker room. Um I think there's an instant amount of respect that he's garnered because of that. And uh when you watch him on the practice field, he really comes to life. title: Dave Canales evaluates Day 2 of mandatory minicamp | Carolina Panthers
text: Uh great response by the players today. Uh challenging we can go another level. We can go harder. Um again within the confines of what this uh time of the season is with our phase three, but um the finish and the effort, the speed was there. Uh ordered up another hot one for them and and the guys handled it uh really well, I thought. Finished with a nice team period, some move the ball things. Um but really pleased with the group as a whole. Um just how they're taking the coaching, they're applying it. Um and above all, it's just the play style, right? And it's the it's the finish and the effort that we're looking for that I was really proud of today. >> Uh today X dropped a pass and then two plays later Bryce came back to him and he made a pretty impressive grab falling to the ground. How have you seen the trust kind of grow between those two? >> Yeah, a lot of trust there. Um I'm I'm excited for Xavier where he's at right now. Bryce really trusts him. Again, I think we talked about this yesterday, but just uh just Xavier's ability to grasp the entirety of the concepts in the offense, you know, in all the different situations, the nuances, the guys that are new to our program, they look to guys like Xavier, like Deemo, even T-Mac, who played a lot last year, you know, and Coker. So, we have a group of guys that um that have built a chemistry that other guys can kind of look at and say, "Hey, this is how we want this to feel and look." So, um, love that. You know, they just continue to work on different routes, different concepts, and, uh, getting their timing. >> Yesterday, you kind of jokingly said you didn't really want to watch the video from Mullen, South Carolina, but what do you think it meant for Bryce to go down there uh, to X's hometown and spend that kind of time with him? >> It's great. Uh I I believe that's what great teams are made of is being able to connect not just on the field but also off the field and understanding that we all got each other's back and uh you know we're all pulling in this together and and you know was Bryce hosted an event earlier in the offseason and brought all the guys over to his house and had a good time and Xavier you know just he comes from a different place Mullen South Carolina. I've driven through there a couple times and it looked like a lot of fun. Um just you know the guys are out there you know getting dirty and and uh you know a lot of smiles. So, from what I saw, um, but those are the types of things that we need. You got to have high ground for hard days. And when you talk about these guys putting in that time together, it matters. As you get deeper and deeper into the season, the relationship matters. >> Dave, Cory Gorton, uh, had a pick today, but it looked like just in general, he was having a really strong day. What are you seeing from him in his second OTAAS? >> All the work that he's put in in his first year is paying off for him. Um, his being conscientious of the schemes, how to play different techniques. Um he's had exposure outside at the nickel at the safety spot. A lot of trust with Corey. Uh especially coming off the injury. He attacked the rehab, came back out here and has looked great, more and more comfortable. And I love seeing him make plays because he works so hard at it. He's the first guy on the field and he's out here working on his craft going through his stance, his footwork, and all those things. So when guys work like that, I expect good things to come. Um and so I'm just really glad that he's continued to grow and progress. There were a couple of guys who didn't practice. Was it that day for T-Mac and JC and Teemo? >> Yeah, just a part of the plan was just to get them two out of three really good days. Um, keep their high speed up when they're out there and, you know, just be smart about that and so that was kind of the plan all along. We expected be for them to be back out there tomorrow. >> From your perspective, what are some of the bigger challenges for a center adjusting to a new quarterback and how have you? Well, it's the cadence first. Getting used to the rhythm of how Bryce calls his cadences, when he checks protections, when he alerts, different things like that. You know, as you can imagine, the center doesn't know what's going on behind him most of the time. So, just getting that chemistry going and then understanding like if you for the center position, if you just give a good clean declaration early on, the quarterback can fix it if he needs to, but it allows us to play fast. and Luke's got a ton of experience and so he's able to hop in there uh get everybody lined up where they need to get a good starting point and then he and Bryce talking through things in between. >> Dave, after we talked to you yesterday, excuse me, Bryce and uh Jaylen both came in and described kind of their little trash talking from yesterday, which you know, I know it was somewhat joking, but but not entirely. And you've talked about wanting to get that energy level up. How important is it to see those two guys who are pretty big names on either side of the ball raise the level of the energy by doing that? >> I it's the heart of competition and while I really don't know what they're saying, we got loud music playing and all that. their words are exchanged, but if you look at the exchanges that are happening, it's in the spirit of competition and uh none of it's personal, none of it's degrading each other, but it's just kind of like, you know, they're going back and forth. And I can see the confidence of both groups really growing and the connection that they have. it brings those things out in us and it gets harder and harder to have success in one way or another, you know, and um whether it's picking up an exotic blitz or whether it's a new pass concept we're trying to get done, um the more the tighter they get on both sides of the ball, the margin continues to just shrink, you know, for for finding that win on that certain play. And and that's what's going to help us play really good ball as we go into the season is making sure that the competition is right in practice. It's got to be hard in practice. This has to be the most physically challenging uh platform that we perform on so that when we get to the game, you have your mind about you. You have that focus and and the bottom line is whatever whatever they're saying and however they say it. They got to be ready to be locked in for the next time they go out there. >> Do you like the trash? >> I don't mind it. For me, it's like it's what it looks like out there. It's all in good fun and it's just the spirit of competition. I was never that way as a player. >> I was never that way. I just played hard, everything I had all the time and but I had teammates that were and you know I appreciated them too because they bring a little swag, they bring a little confidence. I don't think it's a prerequisite to being good. Um but if that's just the personality of the group, that's what it is. >> One more day with this these guys before the break. What do you want to see tomorrow? >> A great finish. Um we're going to throw some different situations at them. We're not going to be on a script, so we'll call it from the sideline. I want to see the players, especially the newer guys, operate quickly, get the communication out, know what they're doing, get a line quickly, um, and go to the next play, be able to do it when you're a little tired. Um, it's kind of like the final exam for the spring. So, we'll be able to put them in those settings and see how guys respond. And that'll tell us, you know, we're we're not um we're just trying to gather information about our players and who we have, especially the new guys, whether they're free agents, whether they're rookies, um to just see how they respond to those situations so we know how to address it, how to help them take the next step and develop >> more control like a true scrimmage. >> Not really. It'll be it'll be more controlled, but um it'll be as close to a move the ball as you can, but it's kind of on my judgment and I'll be able to, you know, put the DNDs in different second and ones, second and twelves. They all happen in games in different ways. So, just making sure that our guys are ready to respond, the play callers are ready to respond with those calls. >> Dave Stone uh was the first and second team right tackle with Taylor out. Um are you in favor of having one guy back up one side and one guy back up the other? or is that just how this kind of shift? >> Honestly, the guy's got to be ready to do both. You know, Wal Teemo, as we know, he's the right tackle. He's our right tackle. Um, but anybody that's not going to be a starter has to be able to learn how to play both because typically on game day, you're the swing tackle and you have to be able to pop in there on either side. So, it's really important for them to get that exposure. I love that Joe and Goodie do that with our players. It's uncomfortable. You ever tried brushing your teeth with your left hand? You had to, I'm sure, right when you were recovering from from your arm, bro. So, >> hey. Oh, you're a lefty. Okay. So, that that was a cheat code for you. But for these guys, you know, if you're naturally left tackle, you go on the right, you're having a punch with your right. It's different. It's good to get that exposure. >> Thank you very much. >> What has uh Willie shown you to give him like very meaningful reps um with the with the first team? >> Yeah, we're asking him a lot. Um, first and foremost, to have the confidence to step in there with the veterans and to know that everybody knows what they're doing, I better know what I'm doing. He's done a great job so far. Um, taking the coaching and the individuals, just the technique coaching from coach Culie. Um, he's really progressed that way. And again, he sits there and he sees JC and Mike and these are two of the best. He gets to watch them every day, how they operate, how they work, and that's been a great influence on him right now. >> All right. Thank you, coach. All right. Thank you. We got T-Mac for y'all.

Concerned about these guys all reporting on July 22nd. Really more concerned about the next 40 days and and what these guys are doing to you know, continue. Like, you can't take steps backwards. That's not the quarterback, that's all these guys. So, literally, my only focus right now is that. We don't play again till September. It is June, whatever it is right now, 10th or what or whatnot. So, not worried about that right now. >> All right. So, is do you expect Jacoby to show at camp with a new contract? >> Uh conversations will uh will be ongoing like they have been. That's all I can give you guys on that and we'll see where it goes. >> [snorts] >> Do you expect that competition to ramp up as soon as you guys get back in the building in July? >> Shoot, I think it's been ramped up. I mean, every single day is a day to compete. Whether it's OTA like it's the intensity should not change from OTAs to training camp. The only thing that happens is naturally physically the intensity picks up because they have pads on. You can actually play football. But no, I hope I hope nothing ramps up there. >> Might be too early question. When would you like to maybe start? >> Yeah, it it would be too early right now cuz we'll let this thing play out and figure out who the best 22 that we're going to put out there plus the specialist to give ourselves the best chance to win on Sundays. >> You were obviously part of one of the more successful franchises the past decade or so in Los Angeles and now you come to a franchise that's struggled over the past couple years. What have you learned about the gap between those two things? Like what what what does this franchise need to do to obtain that sort of success in the long run? >> Yeah, it's it's a good question. Um think these guys um they know how to work. You know, there's not as crazy as it sounds and I know I might get a chuckle but there's not as big of a gap between teams in this league as you would think. Um you got to play the right way. You got to play good football. You can't play bad football. You got to play tough and you got to show up and find a way within the three and a half hour window to win every Sunday. Um I do believe there's just like in any other sport um when you're confident and you take the feel confident. I don't know if they didn't last year. I have no idea. I wasn't here. Um but I do believe this team is going to work to in in in build belief and with belief comes confidence. And um you know, so um yeah, I'll leave it at that. >> You kind of alluded to it earlier but where where are you with health with some of the the longer term guys? Are they all in good spots or is there anybody you're seriously concerned about heading into >> You're saying from an injury standpoint? No, I even the guys that weren't out there for OTAs you feel really good about, you know, just unless there's a setback but had that meeting today with Drew and in the staff and we feel really good about where where all those guys that that weren't out there practicing that they'll be available, you know, right when training camp starts barring setback. That would have we got great news on Garrett. That will not happen for him to be back right in July but when I first got here I I mean maybe I miss speaking here but I mean it was like in October November thing and now it's talking about getting in training camp getting him going. So he's he's put so much good work in what a what a special human being that is and you know, again what a what a really good player that that this defense missed last year when he went down. >> He'll have a chance for week one for sure. Yeah, I'll I'll get away a little bit. Um I'll be with the family a lot. I mean there's almost every single day I'll at least have my wife and kids with us. I'm going to take her up to to Sedona just her. That's going to be our little little quick trip for two days but yeah, we'll get away try to keep the feet up a little bit and with the access and and with the you know, the iPads and computers and all that I mean you always have access to what you need to so I'll pick and choose my spots. I'll be in Wisconsin for a couple weeks with Matt and I'm sure we'll we'll have some pretty good dialogue there about a lot of different things. >> I I can do a pretty good job for the first part because you know, training camp's not starting for 40 days but naturally all of us you just you know, once you're getting a little bit closer you're thinking about it and then it gets you gets you kind of right right. So you're not just showing up and going uh cuz that's not good for anybody. So, uh what's different is this is obviously, you know, a different seat. So, it'll be interesting to see if it does truly turn off because I've already been told at home uh when I'm home, when I think it's turned off, she says it's not. You're not hearing me. And I said, "I heard everything." She says, "Repeat it." I have to I have to ask for forgiveness, so we'll see how this one goes. But no, it'll be it'll be good. So. >> What [snorts] have you seen from Nick and this defensive staff from when you got in this building to now? What type of uh changes, growth have you seen from that? >> Well, Nick, like I've said, um you talk about turning it off, Nick doesn't turn it off at all. Nick probably needs to turn it off. Uh I tell I said, "Do you do anything besides lift and think about football for the 40 days?" And he didn't really have much of an answer for me right there. So, um but uh no, he's um he puts so much work into this thing and uh he's always trying to not just improve the scheme, but improve these players individually, their techniques. They're always, you know, really every week or every 2 weeks going through each guy's individualized plan in terms of what they need to improve on, what we thought going back to to February and and March and then when they got here in April, uh and and how do we have to, you know, kind of um tweak that and stuff. So, um he's been phenomenal to work with. Again, he's just he's just all about it. >> When you're you're designing an offense when you first get here, I imagine you kind of have a vision for what it's going to look like. When the guys first get get out on the field for for practice, has that looked like your vision? Have things shifted at all? Kind of where is the state of of this offense compared to kind of how you might have imagined it when you were building it in your office here? >> Yeah, it's it's a it's a good question because you um you sit there and you you you study these guys, right? And and again, being in this division, you knew some of these guys a little bit more than you'd say if if you're with Buffalo or something like that because obviously they're in the division, you see the crossovers and all that kind of stuff. So, you you you you like you had a pretty good idea, but you don't really know until you get on the grass with these guys, how they think, how they're interpreting the information you're giving them. So, when you give them the foundational aspects, you're trying to spread spread the wealth a little bit. Hey, can he do this? Can he not? Like I don't I don't know if he can, so let's give him an opportunity. And and us as coaches, we I mean that's that's part of our job is to say he can or cannot do this. And that's okay. Like not every guy is is Superman out there that's able to do every single aspect. And and that's why you build the plans as such. He does this well, let's give him the ball this way. He does this well, let's give him the ball this way. So, that's what this was more about, just kind of figuring out a little bit more. As we got a little bit further in OTAs, particularly, you know, yesterday and the week before, like we didn't do much with Trey yesterday. I saw a lot from Trey, you know, from Trey through those first nine practices. But again, we still we still weren't game planning, right? We weren't overly game planning our defense. We just want to make sure we weren't in dead plays cuz no one wants that. And this defense can do that to you. So, kind of a little bit long-winded right there, but yeah, I mean that's that's kind of where we're at. >> I think >> I guess like building when you're building your offense, how how much of it is it your own philosophies and then how much does have to be tailored around like I I imagine there's going to be more stuff for the tight end here than there was last year in LA. Like how much of it is kind of view that part that shifts with >> Yeah, I know it's I know what you're saying. I mean it's you have the foundations, right? The tried and true, you know, we're going to spread out the field, we're going to, you know, make sure that guys aren't overlapping and doing all the things that we need to do on offense where we're distributing the field the right way in the pass game. Same thing with the run game, how are we hitting our combinations? With that being said, now we're going to tailor to those players. And again, as we kind of got a little bit further in the OTAs, we were doing a little bit more with Trey that we knew what we know we're going to do come late August and then obviously into the season. So, you're always going to tailor to your guys. That's why you see Arizona and San Francisco and LA and Green Bay. That's why yeah, there's foundational aspects that you could watch from, you know, the bird's eye and say there's similarities there, but it's always going to be tailored to their guys, for sure. >> You said the other day that he has been game planning already. He's not necessarily in order of schedule, just teams here and there. Is that something that that you do, and if so, what does that look like for you guys? >> Yeah, um kind of started dabbling into it in this last week, uh just cuz part of the you know, what we're just saying. I mean, you have a better feel for what these guys can do, and you know, like I told the staff today, it's again, we gave guys a lot of opportunities. That's stuff that, you know, can they do it, can they not? We we as coaches have to decide uh without saying, "Hey, it's an absolute." Guys are going to go work on some of their weaknesses, but we as a staff have to say, "Okay, now we have to go get good at something, right?" And so, we need to tailor this a little bit more to the skill sets of these guys. So, as you do that, then you can start kind of looking at some of those first opponents and whatnot. You know, the you think about the first opponent that we got, coordinator was at Western Michigan a year ago. Now, with that being said, he was with the Chargers the you know, the year before that. So, um we'll see what they end up doing. It could be what, you know, Jesse was doing, or could be something completely different. I don't know. Um so, you got to just kind of take it a little bit at a time right there. Those first four weeks, in my opinion, are more about your foundations and what you do well, and then figuring out after that, cuz now you're figuring out what the defenses are doing, cuz they got enough tape. And then after that, okay, what are our complement plays that we can still handle that are going to play off of some of first three, four games, like I was saying. >> Do you have any kind of a parting message for the guys today? >> Uh that'll be at about 2:00 today. >> Is Caleb [snorts] Proctor injured? >> Yeah, he is, yeah. So, that's uh just throwing it out. That's the one that's uh it sucks as that's the only injury we we had some, you know, bumps and bruises, I guess you could say, but everyone's leaving healthy. Uh Caleb Proctor um had a a men- meniscus tear. Uh so, he'll miss, you know, quite a bit of time, if if not I don't want to say absolute but if not the the whole year. >> Coach, this [snorts] is the last day for players to is there more or do you have more for the coaches here in the next few days or weeks? >> Yeah, so it's the last day for us as a 90. Our rookies are still here. Uh, rookies don't have rules for the most part. Uh, and it's actually toned down. It used to they really didn't have rules. It was great. But, um, so now we'll we'll let these guys out here in a little bit. Rookies will be here Thursday, Friday. Coaches will be with them tomorrow. And then Friday they'll just be with the strength staff. And then next week the rookies will be here with the strength staff and and doing some of their success program and stuff like that. >> I mean >> that's me uh turn it off a little bit. When you're around your brother, how how tough is it not to talk football? >> He just wants to be on the boat the whole time. So, it's uh no, it's um you know, before this year like we would talk but like it is nice to not talk about it either. And I think we both know kind of what's going on. There's there's constant um family and friends that are kind of ripping through his his place up there at his lake house in Wisconsin. So, you naturally get breaks right there. But, uh I I have a feeling I got I got a couple questions or a laundry list of stuff uh that you know, I'd like to talk with him about. But, again I talk to him every day. So, it's not like it's you know, I don't I don't have the access to it. >> What coach do you think of Max's Nick Wilson mentality that yesterday he tweeted like Arizona against the world after he said that also LA Rams have to deal with us? Um, what do you think about that as a leader for Max? >> I love it because that's who Max is and that's what Max believes and that's how Max um practices and that's how Max prepares and that's how Max carries himself in the building. Um, Max always viewed himself as an underdog. And I mean let's let's not throw it out there. I mean like you know, you got a pretty tough division right now where you can make a case right now before anyone's played that shoot a lot of these teams everyone's saying they're going to go to the Bowl and all that. And I understand. Rosters are great. And so I think this is right where Mack wants to be. I think this is where he feels most comfortable. You know, and if he says it, he means it. >> We haven't seen a ton of Carson Shushire. Is that how you say his name? On the on the field during during camp. How how's he doing and then what's kind of >> Yeah, so he had a he had a hammy and that's what that's what kept him out of there. And it was substantial to be strong but for lack of a better term, but he'll he'll be another guy. I mean seriously, there's he'll be good to go come the 22nd. >> You said you had great news >> But he's he's looking good. >> You said you had great news on Garrett Williams. Is there optimism that Walter Nover might be able to be ready for >> Yeah, Walter Walter's going to be again and he's I mean there there could be setbacks, but right now all this is is trending great for for the 22nd for all these guys where we feel really good. It was a very I was very happy this morning with the meeting we had. So. Yep. >> You mentioned earlier having that extra week in training camp and with that comes the Hall of Fame game. How do you approach that as a I'm sure it's a welcome thing for a first-year head coach. Not just for on-field evaluation, but maybe operationally with the >> Yeah, no totally. >> What do you what do you think about having that extra opportunity? >> I think that's great. I think having the the first-year head coach being in the Hall of Fame game getting that extra week like I think that that is absolutely a net positive for us to be able to one get the preparation, get those pads on a little bit earlier. You know, our acclimation period like I was just saying, guys are still going to be on vacation around this league and rightfully so. I mean that's the way the the calendar falls. So and then be able to get to that that Hall of Fame game and and like you just said work that operation like I I apologize guys, but you're not going to see me with headsets and stuff like that on the practice field. Like I just I've never seen it. I've never done it. I know other people do. I respect that, but you know, we've been in this long enough to to know how to operate, but it is a new staff and that's what the preseason's for. So to get one extra crack at it, I think is a is a great thing for all of us, players and coaches.

title: OL Paris Johnson Jr. Minicamp Press Conference 06-09-26 | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: How's the new offense coming together? >> Oh, great. I would say it's this the accumulation this off season. I would say the guys are really on the same page with the with the offense and the guys are starting to fall in love with it. >> Through the limitations, what have you been able to learn about the type of player that Isaac is next to you? >> I love playing next to Isaac, you know, he doesn't really talk much. You know, I'll be up there. I'll make them on calls and I'll look at him and he'll start to grunt. I'll look at him and I'm like, that's [snorts] all I need. Like if if I hear the grunt and I know we're on the same page. >> [laughter] >> When you've got a new offensive lineman in the room like like Chase, I know he plays on the inside, but do you still kind of lend your advice or do you kind of let the the guards and centers kind of handle >> Yeah, I mean within the O line room, going to continue to lend a hand to Chase even though he plays on the right side. However, on the field, I kind of let that be with Elijah since potentially, you know, Elijah can talk to him whoever the right tackle right now like with Josh or the two of them on the right side like between Josh and Elijah, I kind of let those guys kind of talk because there's a connection between the way you set within the way you set in protection or the way you want your combinations in the run game like me and Chase aren't in in combinations. So unless he wants my advice on how he should play a certain thing um based on my experience of playing, that's one thing, but on the field, you know, my communication solely relies right now with Isaac with how we want things to work together, you know. >> How have you seen Chase? I mean, I know he as you said up up season on the line, but how have you seen him come along over this past month? >> Yeah, I mean, I would say how he's been able to show the confidence on the field has been something that's starting to jump off the tape. You know, just confidence. You know, like I told him regardless of the role he has on the field year one, you know, I want to see him play as if he's coming in to compete for a spot. Cuz ultimately you draft in the second round, you know, you have high goals, high expectations. So, whether that role is play now or to play next year, in 2 years, whatever God has for him, front office has for him, you know, I just want to see him grow as fast as possible. You know, I think God I had the ability to play year one and I would love to see other guys be able to to to see what that looks like whether it's a game or a whole season, you know, whatever it is. You know, I want to see him shine when opportunity comes. >> You just mentioned playing in year one for you. Now that you go into year four, like how different of a player is Paris and kind of where do you see your game right now as you head into this fourth year? >> I'll say the difference between year one and year four, I mean it's just the ownership that I have over my game, how I play and how I execute my technique. I would say it's just the the difference. You know, like I know on the field exactly how I'm going to play, how I'm going to show up, and what exactly I need to do to win. More so than seeing how my college game is about to translate, you know, game one versus Washington, you know, 2023, you know? >> How are you doing with the play calls and terminology in the huddle and translating that to the line of scrimmage? >> And all that terminology stuff was able to be translated pretty fast. I like the way that we did the installs in the meetings and it definitely helped having Coach Fry here in the building too for year two here with us able to translate our terminology within the room from last year to this year made that all the more simple. >> What do you What do you hope to see out of your running back room as a whole if guys get healthy come on the other side? >> Yeah, we have a lot of talent and um, back there. So, again, I feel like that just put some more on us up front to make sure we do our jobs because I trust everybody from 6 to 4 to 20 to 37 um, thought the running back room is endless right now. You know, so but you know, I trust all those guys. Um, that the way you know, when when they when they get the ball in their hands the way those guys take off and I can't forget um, 22. Algier, almost forgot to name him too, but all those guys um, the way that they practice and you can tell that these guys are ex- excited to take the reps that they get and these guys are running full speed in practice. So, you can just see the excitement. I think all these guys are healthy, they're ready to go. >> Go- going into your fourth year, you're obviously now eligible for for an extension, but you got the the fifth-year option. Are you still looking to get that done this off-season or with the option are you happy to push that off till next off-season? >> I feel like right now my goal is just be the best version of me today. Um, that's the only thing on my mind. I know the contract stuff will work itself out in the timing, you know, it always does. You know, especially in the tackle market. You know, it happens when it happens and it's usually right, you know. Um, but I'm not really worried about that right now cuz it's not going to help me block anybody in front of me right now, you know what I mean? So, right now I'm just thinking about how I can be the best version of myself for the guys on the on the on the team right now. >> Was that more on your mind before you got the fifth-year option exercised? >> No, cuz it wasn't going to help me prepare in the off-season whatsoever, you know, I was training up in Cleveland Ohio in the cold every day. The only thing on my mind was was making my time up there be worthwhile. You know, and I was trying to to take advantage of the days and the training and um, so that way I can come to OTAs and be sharp, you know. The la- it's kind of like when I was in college, like my last year in college I heard rumblings about what league and all that kind of pushed all that to the side because that wasn't going to help me in block anybody. And I was like put the blinders on kind of mindset and in fact that's the same kind of approach to this year and putting the blinders on. Things are going to happen. What's going to happen, but right now I'm just saying what talking to you guys, you know. >> Speaking of Cleveland, you get the privilege of seeing Miles Garrett twice a year after he was traded to the Browns. What was your initial reaction to that? >> Yeah, I mean I think it's awesome that we get to bring that great um talent to put the division. Again, it just makes these games even more exciting and the games are more even more important up front, so to have the privilege to go against even more guys like that, especially in the NFC alone. Um on the town, I think it's looks like the SEC right now. You know, which is awesome. You know, so I'm definitely excited that you know, getting to see him two times a year. But again, I think, you know, the guys that we have here, too. You know, I know exciting for um like those guys have to see the guys that we have here, too. So, to be able to have the guys back and guys like Sweat back in the building, you know, today was exciting, too. You know, cuz those are guys that we have that those guys are going to see, too, twice a year, too. >> How good is it to see Jacoby back in the What kind of presence does he bring to the locker room just in the team in general? >> Yeah, I mean the guys are like super excited to see Jacoby back. You know, it was great. I mean we all you know, knew he was going to come back today. Um but you know, that's our guy through and through, you know. We're behind him 100%, so and it was it was it was it was good to see him. >> Where do you train in Cleveland? >> Oh, man. I train I train wherever my old line coach is at. So, sometimes I'll be 4 minutes down the street. Sometimes I'll be in Cleveland. I don't ever stay in Cleveland. I stay in Columbus at my mom's house. I just drive the 2 hours up every day cuz I don't want to stay the night in Cleveland. >> I think it's just cuz I'm from Cincinnati, you know, there's just Cincinnati in me. And Columbus has my heart since I went to school there, but I just I do the drive up and back. It's too close to the state up north, you know, so I drive all the back, you know, where I know. >> Given your individual workouts in the off-season, are you still training left and right side? Are you at the point where you're really just focused on left? >> No, I only train left side. That's all I do. Um the only time I may get in a right stance is just to more so work the brain and hand something on the left. But you know, I'm not I'm not taking a set on the on the right side at all. >> Even with your focus and you can, you know, focus on your four and what you're preparing for, people talking about you sticking around long-term, your foundation is doing a charity event and all that stuff. Like does it feel good to be able to kind of really establish these roots and further that kind of going forward? >> Yeah, you know, I I I love being here in the valley. Um I love I love the community. I love being able to serve the community. When um you know, we have the free time like this. Off-season's a great time to be able to do that. Um personally I love to be here. You know, you know, right now it's all up to the way I continue to play, the way I continue to show up, you know, on the field and off the field, continue to be, you know, that star guy. And then it's up to, you know, the guys above us right now, you know. >> Paris, you go back with Marvin a long way. Um he he came in with great excitement being the fourth pick of the draft, a successful Hall of Famer. Uh and then last year he had some unfortunate luck just with the injury, the appendix situation. How how do you think he's dealt with just the expectations, the ups and downs of pro football, where he is right now? >> Yeah, I know him well, and I'm sitting next to him every day. I talk to him every day. And I would say the one thing right now that he's doing is continuing to fight right now. You know, I believe that Marv is um the kind of guy since college that, you know, he's never compared himself to his dad. His dad had an an awesome career and he, you know, he's a by all rights, he's a legend, a Hall of Fame. I believe that Marv sees himself as his own person. And by all means, he wants to, you know, be his dad in every single way. Not just cuz he's a son, but because this is his own career. You know, so right now he's starting to he's in a mode right now where he wants to fight for everything that he wants to achieve. And right now he's not looking at the past couple years. He's looking at how can he fight to get what he wants right now. Then this time next year, how can he fight to get it again? You know, even if he's done everything everyone here wants to see, again, you have to fight to do it again. You can't just do it one time and just start to sit back and to reminisce on that too much. You know what I mean? So, he's he's just a fighter right now, keeping his head on. He's still just as quiet, but he's smiling. Um, just cuz he's dialed in and he's focused. You know, cuz you know he knows why he's here. He knows what the fans want to see. He knows what, you know, the team knows he can do and I've seen him do it since he was like 18. So, I'm excited again for another opportunity for people to see the version of Marv that, you know, I've always known is truly him, you know. >> Larry, do you have any summer plans? >> Summer plans, um, just going to be training. Training the usual, Cleveland. I mean, I'll be back in Cleveland again. If you want to call that if you want to call that a vacation, you know, it'll be a little warmer this time, though. It'll be a little warmer, so I don't need to bring a coat, but I'll be back in Cleveland. But it feels like a vacation, um, just because, again, um, any day I'm up there I'm getting better. I'm up there with a purpose. So, I feel like I'm Rocky old, but although I haven't seen the full Rocky movies, but I've seen enough clips to feel like I feel like I'm Rocky. You know, he's a Philly cold with the hoodie on. Like, anytime in Cleveland, I'm there with a purpose. I'm not there for fun. There's nothing fun up there. You know what I mean? But that work. So, um, so, you know, I'm there with a purpose, so it feels like it, you know. >> You're just not staying the night. >> No, back to back to Columbus I go. >> Are you going to be running the streets and dogging up and down hills and >> Um no, it felt like I remember the first day I landed in Columbus and I walk outside my mom's house and I didn't walk outside with a coat and that cold breeze hit me and I was like, "Dang, I'm really back here." Like, I'm really back in the mix. That's why I was like have went back out a hoodie and I was like, "I feel like Rocky, man." Like, I'm in that mode cuz what am I doing out in Ohio? I play for the Cardinals. You know what I mean? And my trainer has me there for 2 weeks. I'm like, "Shoot, I'm in that mode." So, obviously I'm going to put those 2 weeks again this year and then I mean this all I mean this summer and then again before that training here being Cleveland and then I'll be back for the last 10 days before training camp which is training 4 minutes down the road. >> Which one is your favorite Rocky movie? >> Um favorite Rocky clips? I mean, probably cuz I haven't watched the full I haven't I I haven't sat down and watched the full one. Um shoot. The one where he's uh he goes against the Russian guy. I mean, that's Rocky 4. >> Yeah. >> Come on now. Seen enough clips. You know? >> So, how hard is it going to be to have to stay in Cleveland for the Hall of Fame game? >> What's that? >> How hard is it going to be to have to stay in Cleveland overnight for the Hall of Fame game? >> Oh yeah, I guess I will be overnight in Cleveland for that day. But, you know, again, I'm there with purpose. You know what I mean? It's all about the purpose. I can be anywhere I can be anywhere with purpose. You know, have you guys seen the video of um things like a UFC fighter and he's like every off season he goes like the middle of like Eastern Europe. It's like Bull Stack of Stan or something. You guys you know what I'm talking about? Like that one guy, you know? That's like my you know, you know, whatever Stan. That's like my that's my Eastern Europe out there. So, it's like I'm just going back to work, you know what I mean? And it's for a preseason game. So, whether I'm playing or not, I'm out there for the work. So, I I like it. You know, I'll be dialed in. >> Who's the Who's the coach that you work with in Cleveland? >> I work with Willie Charles Bentley. Up in Cleveland and out here in his team out here. >> Thanks, Barry. >> Thanks. Thank you.

title: LB Mack Wilson Sr. Minicamp Press Conference 06-09-26 | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: Yeah, I got it as a gift yesterday. It's pretty nice. >> How do you think things are going now you got the new coaching staff here? Not everybody, but a lot of new guys here coaching wise, how's it going? >> Yeah, I think I think it's been fun, honestly. I did it my sophomore year in college and my junior in college, but that was the last time I did it. So, it was new to me and um obviously, there was a lot of nerves there going into games. Have you been able to see benefits of having kind of those experienced coaches on the defensive side? >> Yeah, it's been benefiting us a lot, honestly. Uh been around some of the best guys ever do it and uh kind of just pick his brain and kind of see the type of backers he've came across and you know, how I kind of fit in that in that criteria and what he think of me and how do he feel I can be better and things like that.
