Obviously, a guy who's won three Super Bowls, then been playing ball at the highest level. Uh coach Nick Bolton, one of the one of the good backers I would say in this league and things like that. So, it's been dope, honestly. It's been fun. Um I'm just excited to to continue to build this thing with the guys. >> Does it feel like you have kind of more voices that you can lean on this year? You know, with those guys you're talking about? >> Yeah, definitely. I would say that and I mean, at the end of the day they all are coaches. They serve us at the end of the day, so feel like if I need anything from any of the coaches, I'm able to to go ask any of them. I feel like. >> What was the injury and how long did it take you to get back to 100%? >> Yeah, it was tough, honestly. It was some of the one of the toughest things I had to deal with, I feel like throughout my whole career and um uh coming back, it was like I didn't know what was going to happen. I'm I'm a maniac. I tried to come back a week after to play against the 49ers or whatever and uh God had other plans, obviously, and um yeah, it was it was it was pretty tough. It was a pretty pretty long recovery. Um and now I'm I feel like I'm 100% obviously. This offseason I feel like I've been 100% and been able to hit those strides and things like that, get all my wind back and stuff, but I would say it was it was tough. It was tough. >> How severe was the injury? >> Uh it was severe enough to put me out the rest of the year. So, I would say I mean, I had two two fractured ribs, so that what it was, honestly. >> You're going against a lot of running backs, obviously, right? But Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah, can you tell much yet? What What can you tell? What has stood out? >> He got it. He blessed. I would say he blessed, honestly. Uh just seeing him from the sidelines move, catch the ball. Like, it's a run play I had against him uh we had against him, I think, last week. And I was getting over the top, and I thought he was about to press the gap, but like he's so patient, and I feel like he feel like he been here before, honestly. Uh and I know I'm talking highly of a rookie right now, but he got game, man. I'm just excited to to share the field with him and and see where his career go. >> I know you didn't get to play with Walter a lot last year, but you did get to play with him a little bit. Like, what when he's healthy, what does he >> [clears throat] >> give to this defense? >> He's a difference maker, I feel like. And that's something that I've been telling him uh since he stepped foot in this in this building, honestly. You don't want to put too much pressure on a rookie, but sometimes it's like that. And, you know, once you see a potential in some of these guys, you got to let them know, like, hey, like, you got it. Like, whatever you got to do to get yourself mentally prepared to go out there and execute, like, do that. Because you got guys like me and Buddha pulling for you. We see the potential. We know what you can add to this defense, so it's just all about him just just uh I think taking care of the mental battle of it, the mental aspects that come with the game, and just honing on honing in on being a beast. You know, everybody know that he a beast, and that's something I have to continue to tell him, like, like, you got it. Like, keep keep balling, keep grinding out, you know, keep recovering and things like that. You know, the sky's the limit for him. >> How was it to have Sione back in the building? >> Great. I love Sione. I was so excited to see him today. Obviously, he's a big part of what we trying to build here, big part of this defense. Uh Great dude, great energy. Yeah, I was I missed him for this whole offseason, honestly. So, having him back today was was super dope, super dope. >> What is difference maker? What is Josh Sweat when he's smelling blood? >> Shh. He a bad dude. Honestly, I've I've shared the field with had a blessing to share the field with Myles Garrett in Cleveland. But, I mean, Sweaty Sweaty's a good pass rusher as well, and he do it just as as good as the rest of the best of them. And, like I said, he's he's a key part of what we doing on defense. So. >> Thank you. >> Myles joining the Rams. >> Hm? >> How do you feel about Myles joining the >> They got to got to deal with us. At the end of the day, they got to deal with us.

title: Jesse Minter's Parting Message to Players After Minicamp | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: The Ravens wrapped up their off-season program today. The two-day mini-camp concluded this afternoon, and now it's time for summer break. The Ravens have a few weeks off before reporting back here to Baltimore for training camp in late July. Now, it has been a very busy off-season program for the Ravens with the new coaching staff led by head coach Jesse Minter. There's been the work on the field and in the classroom learning the systems, building the camaraderie, building the foundation of this team that they're going to take into the upcoming season. Now, as practice concluded today, coach Minter, as well as owner Steve Bisciotti, both talked with the team, and Jesse talked about the message for the team going into this break. >> Yeah, I think it's it's simple in a sense like, you know, when you're not here, like you own your career. You're the owner of your career, and everything that you do, you know, it puts you in position when you come back to be in position, you know, and really just put yourself in position so that when you return, you're able to, you know, we're able to kind of roll into this thing instead of starting back from ground zero. >> Now, I can tell you this, and being in the building, vibes are high for this team. There's a lot of good energy coming off this practice field and out of this locker room, and both Lamar Jackson and Kyle Hamilton talked about what they're taking from this off-season program. >> Just the chemistry, building chemistry with our guys, you know, trying to learn guys, you know, as we going along in our season before this break. That's it. >> There's there's no gray area, and I feel like that's huge, especially in a sport like this, and I felt like you know, if you go out there and you got any sort of uncertainty about what the guy next to me is doing, then, you know, it's not going to look good on either side of the ball or special teams. So, um just being connected, they always preach that. It's on our wall in the meeting rooms, and being connected and communicating is first first and foremost, for sure. >> And maybe the best part of this off-season program is that the Ravens made it all the way through healthy, and Minter expects a roster at full go once they get to training [music] camp next month. That's it for me on Final Drive. Thanks for watching. We'll see you again tomorrow.

title: Deshaun Watson Press Conference | June 10th, 2026
text: So, Deshawn, can you um what do you make of this opportunity that you have to come back out here and and win this starting job after everything that's transpired here so far? >> Uh I mean, it's it's a blessing. It's great. It's anytime you get the opportunity to play in the National Football League is uh is a is an honor. So, you know, I don't take it for granted. So, um I'm in a great space. >> What was the last year and a half like for you since that injury in the in that Bengals game? >> Um I mean, it was a lot of ups and downs. You know, I learned a lot about myself. Um learned that uh you know, you just got to be patient. Just keep working, keep pushing, keep pushing forward. But uh you know I've always kind of had that mentality since I was a kid you know growing up. So it wasn't anything you know new for me. Um the situation and environment was probably new just been with the type of injuries that I had but outside of that you know just keep pushing keep pushing forward. That's how life go. Life is going to continue to go on. So um yeah it's been it's been tough but at the same time you know I was able to grow and learn. >> Desan was there ever a thought I mean you talk about the ups and downs. Was there ever a fear in the back of your minds like am I going to ever be able to get back out there and get an opportunity to to play this game? >> No. No, never was a thought. >> Desan, can you The last time we saw you on the field, uh you were rupturing your Achilles and you got some booze from some fans. Uh how do you and and now there still are some fans that don't necessarily seem to be in your corner. How as you move forward and maybe become the starting quarterback of the Cleveland Browns, how do you reconcile or grapple with the notion that, you know, maybe you don't have all the support that that you would hope that you would have from Cleveland Browns fans? >> Um, you know, at the end of the day, I can't control what, you know, people support. You know, I think that's their own opinions. You know, I think that all I can do is just put out the best person I am. um showcase who I am as a person, as a player, as a teammate, and uh what I represent as an individual. So outside of that, you know, I can't focus on, you know, what the outside is saying or what they, you know, I have no control over that other than just putting out the best um you know, product that I can put out as a person and as a player. Sean, >> do you have any emotions with that? Obviously, like like I know a lot of your teammates kind of spoke out about how frustrated they were. I mean, and kind of a real love moment for you. You haven't strong emotions without that kind of some of that kind of energy. >> I mean, yeah, I had emotions at the time, but you know, you grow, you grow out of it. >> Yesterday, Todd Mon said this competition is too close to call. Do you feel that way? >> I just come show up every day, you know. So, I can't control, you know, coaches, he's the head coach. He's the he's the one calling the plays and, you know, he got to decide who he wants out wants out there on the field. So at the end of the day, I got to just show up each and every day and be ready, you know, wait for my numbers. >> Sean, coming off the Achilles, >> how important is it to you to get a chance to start again at this time? >> Um, I mean, it's very important, I think, each and every person that walks into this the the locker room should have that mindset that you want to start in this league. That's that's why we show up each and every day is to be able to go out there and be able to perform on Sundays or whenever that that day is. So, um, yeah, it's a it's a definitely the main focus of why, you know, I work hard to be able to come back the way I do. >> How does this system fit you versus the last few installments? >> Um, you know, it's a lot of responsibility on the quarterbacks in the system and I think that uh that's what I had in Houston when I was with Bill O'Brien. It was, you know, pretty much that Tom Brady tree and everything relied on the quarterback operation. So, uh, with with Monk, he's given a lot of responsibility to us and, um, you know, you got to own up to the responsibilities and and the situations and what you decide to do on the field. And, uh, I think that's that's something that I'm very comfortable with. >> It's been a while since you've been on the field competing. So, how are you doing? >> I'm doing well. I'm doing great. When you look at um the way that your first three seasons here went, if you get back out onto the field as the starting quarterback for Cleveland Browns, do you think that you will have a better opportunity to be successful at it given everything around you, given the time of the system, given the support you pass? Do you think that this will be a chance to show who the real Deshun Watson is here? >> Um, of course. And I only reason I really say that is because, you know, it's the next opportunity. I can't look in the in the past. I can't look in the river mirror. You know, obviously, you know, those situations and know you have those experiences, but at the same time, you got to keep pushing forward. So, my mentality is one day at a time. Um, and for love and I think you guys seen it on social media, focus on only on victories every day. And so, that's all I'm focused on is just being able to keep pushing forward and keep stepping forward. And if I keep, you know, stepping forward and standing, you know, 10 toes down, then I'll be good. Des, I know you said that you didn't have any doubts in your mind that oh, you worried about never playing again, but I guess were there any doubts about if you would get another chance in Cleveland to be the starting quarterback? >> Um, no. And that's just from internal conversations. >> Have you thought about what you want to do since it is last year contract? What do you want to be doing in 2027? >> I don't I don't know. I'm trying to play a full season, man. I'm just trying to be healthy so I can play all 17 plus games. So I I don't know what happen is going to happen in at that time. >> Do you think that you're there yet to be to play like a full season? Like do you feel ready for all of that? Oh, >> most definitely. I do, you know, so I feel good. >> Even though you've only been able to play 19 games, you're the longest tenur offensive player on the team. >> Does that feel strange to you at all? >> Yeah, it's a lot. It was a lot of new faces walking in. How he deals with quarterbacks? Um, I think what makes him unique is that he he's worked with so many different guys. So, it's not just a a dual threat guy or a pocket passer, whatever, you know, you want to categorize, you know, the quarterback. I think he's just open to being able to relate to the players. And I think that's been a plus for this locker room and team, especially the young guys. >> Let's do Tony Spencer. And then I think Kelsey got one in Daniel. And then last one from Jeff. >> Can't turn back time. But given given all you've been, are you in a better place now than when you first arrived to Cleveland before the incident? >> Of course. Of course. There was a lot going on. So, uh, yeah, I'm in I'm in a a way better space. Um, and I've matured and and mentally I'm in a great position and again like I I'm I'm in a great space. I'm happy. So I'm enjoying life. >> Desawn, we didn't get a chance to talk to you obviously last year, but we've heard about some of your impact behind the scenes now you're in a direct competition with with just what's your relationship been what been like sort of with him from last year when he got here to now and now that you guys are out there. >> I mean it's been good. I think from the the time he got drafted, the the relationship and conversations has been growing even during pre-draft. Uh and I I've known the Sanders family. I've known his brother all the way back when he was at SMU when coach Chad Morris, he was the coach there. I used to go out there and you know, I used to hang out with with the team and uh his brother was one of the players. How helpful has that been, not only learning the new offense, the offensive staff, but also getting the chance to be on the field and get those reps? >> Oh, it's been awesome. It's been great, especially being off the field for the last year and a half, two years. anytime you get the opportunity to go out there and just compete and just cut it loose has been it's been awesome. So, you know, I think the biggest thing for me is just being out there going out there and just reacting, cutting it loose. Don't don't get too worried into making mistakes. That's that's part of the game. That's part of this this period uh where we're in. So, um again, I'm having fun. I'm enjoying the the guys. I'm enjoying the locker room. I'm hanging out with with the guys outside the building. It's been uh it's been a good nine 10 weeks for sure. text: juice today with the fans here. >> Yeah, it was good to get them out here. Um seemed like it was pretty packed early on. Um weather kind of held off for us. Um you know, and try to give the fans what they want, get the ball down the field a little bit and uh we appreciate the you know, the whole fan base and community coming out to support us. >> You like that being? >> Yeah, it's fun, man. It it it helps bring some some life to the to the joint and um I know the players really appreciate it. I know all of us feel it and it makes it just a little bit more competitive. It's just natural the the fact that uh you've got people that you know care about what we're doing out here taking the time to watch us practice. Um that's something that I I really appreciate as the coach and also feed off of when we're out here. It's when we're at the call it periods and you hear the fans roar when the guys make a play. Well, I want to throw it down the field again. And you know, you want to continue to do it because momentum is a a hell of a drug. >> Well, you talked about >> you talked about BTJ before, but what he's stacking here, what does that do for him or can do for him confidence-wise? >> Huge for for uh the confidence as you said number one to always, you know, I mean, you hear all it's hard to not hear everything, right? and to also for himself I know there was you know standards in which he wanted to improve upon and so the fact that he's just come out here and work his ass off uh having a great attitude like after every play communication with either myself or Trevor or Eie or Grant whatever it is um and then making the plays like that is something that you cannot simulate in routes on air you cannot simulate that type of confidence until you do it in practice. Like it's just there's nobody that I've known as a player that just can only turn it on in a game. Like there the whole gamer thing like I I don't fully believe in that. I believe in guys elevate their play to go play in a game. Absolutely. But the confidence of the connection and chemistry that they're building, uh that's real. a continuation to their points. You have the opportunity to string together a series of successful seasons for the first time in quite some time for this franchise. Was having the crowd's energy here a reminder of the expectations for this group? >> Yeah, I mean, look, we we try not to feed too much into the expectation world. We try to just live in the in the day in the process of getting better each and every day. And so as much as we understand that um there's been peaks and valleys in the past, we're not living in that past. We're living in the in the moment we're living in today. And having the fans out here today was a great representation of guys continuing to elevate their play, elevate the standard of how we practice and and operate on a day-to-day basis. But um you know, you want expectations to be high and and you want cuz it's more of a standard of creating a standard of hey, this is just how we play. This is how we operate. Coach, there's no such thing as having too many guys that can make plays, but with guys that have individual goals and a desire to help the team, how do you balance that out, letting them know that you're going to get your chance? >> Yeah, I think that the cream always rises. the guys that um you know operate as professionals that know what they're doing in the playbook that know how to come out here and practice and put it on tape. Those guys are going to be the ones that are always going to get the more o the most opportunities, excuse me. And you want every player and I tell them in meetings like, "Guys, your individual goals are important to us." Like, we go over those in your three better, three best and what your goals are individually because every player that's has success, I mean, that's only going to help our team, right? And you want players to go and achieve those goals, to go get paid, to get bonuses. Like, we want that. like absolutely want that for each and every player, but it's got to be a team first mentality. Is it truly what's best for the team? Um, and and that's what we're doing with personnel. I mean, the best players will always play. I don't care if you're a rookie, if you're a vet, it does not matter. The best players will play and the best players will get the the touches and targets. >> Rodriguez when he does get back, how much does his familiarity with you uh help him catch up? It helps for sure. Um the onboarding process of more so the run game and protections, right? That that's more the most that running backs have to know is their their track, what's the concept of run, whether it's outside zone, mid zone, tight zone, whatever those are. Knowing what those tracks and uh footworks are, and then the blitz pickup and protections. Other than that, I mean, you're talking about checkdowns and routes that they learn through concepts. and we've been running a lot of the concepts that we're running now when I was at Kentucky in 21. I mean, there's so much that we're doing that may be different verbiage from what it was then, but very similar conceptually. So, I'm really I'm not worried about him at all from a can he is he going to be ready mentally to go when we hit training camp. Not worried about him, not one bit. >> Last off season was your first season obviously and introducing everything to the guys. Yeah, there was a lot of cross positional uh you know flexibility within the offensive line. Any plans on the new guys or even the veterans grabbing that same thing this year? >> Yeah, next week when we hit uh kind of those last three days of what we'll call OTAAS, we're going to and now we won't be doing much team work like against each other. But within the positional drills, within the group, separate OD drills, we are going to be mixing up the offensive line a little bit and just getting some some of those guys individual work at different positions. And that's kind of our way to as we head towards the end, we're not doing anything where com like chemistry would get maybe in the way there or any issues uh with communication. We'll have some of those guys bounce around at different positions throughout individual and through group work next week. >> Uh using any week one stuff this week? >> Uh this week, no. Next week, that's what it's all for. Uh so we're going to use next week, what we're going to call it essentially a pass camp where everything that we're doing on Monday through Wednesday is really hyperfocused on the pass game. Not just obviously we'll do some seven on seven, but pass rush, it's all the D line's going to be in all pass rush drills the entire day. Offensive line, they're going to be in all pass protection drills, whether it's individually, pods of groups, halfline, full line, and then we'll do some blitz pickup, which will be a lot of it uh geared towards Cleveland in that way. >> UFFL experimenting with four points for a 60ard field goal or longer. any interest in that? >> Heck yeah, man. Let's go up the Annie a little bit. I mean, I think it's cool that I mean, you look at the dynamic kickoff and and the UFFL obviously having a lot to do with some of those things. And um I think the game so much of this game at this level, I mean, it's taken from high school, it's taken from college, it's taken from the UFO, from Canada, from arena. I mean there's so many different uh whether it's rules, scheme, concepts, fundamentals and techniques that we can take from everywhere. I think that would be a pretty cool uh rule proposal to come up on the docket here >> that would impact the way you might >> Absolutely. Yeah, there's definitely some more strategy involved when if it was worth four points. I think we have a little bit of an advantage with our guy having uh two of those long field goals last year and being able to attempt them. I mean, that would definitely change some of your strategy for sure. I think it's a cool conversation. >> It was a really big day for the secondary today. Like, what did you see from those guys today? Like, how do you how are you feeling walking out of this competition? >> Yeah, I've I feel like the secondary's improved drastically from uh where we were. I think the combination of Matt Rujo and and Anthony Perkins have done a phenomenal job in the secondary collaborating with what Campy's vision is back there. But what Matt has brought has been some swagger, some confidence, and we're trying to play a little bit stickier underneath. And look, make us throw make people throw the ball over your heads. the the percentages of completions of just a go ball versus a hitch or a curl, it's so much smaller. The margin for error is so much smaller to say, man, the ball has to get completed 45 yards down the field on the red line one-on-one, right? So, we're trying to just continue to take the air out of the coverage. Um, and that's not just in the secondary, that's in the at the linebacker position, and that only helps the rush, right? The rush and the coverage are always tied together. And if we can be a little bit more sticky, a little bit tighter coverage, even when we're in our zones, I think it's only going to help our cause. >> Um, I think he's improved a ton. Um, but just watching him, he's he's really been super detailed with his technique. I think that's one of the things that shows up. Very very deliberate like in the way that he's practicing. Um, and I think that that's uh created some takeaways for him and making some plays on the ball. He's just always seems to be near the action right now. So, he's uh he's really done a great job and improved a bunch this spring. >> Matthew off from your staff. Obviously, you have a background with him. What does he bring to the table? >> I I think he's he's an incredibly detailed guy. Uh he's really really smart young coach. Um but you know, he's a maniac out here out here on the field. Um I think you guys who've been around him, you've seen that he's just a great coach, super detailed. Um he's a tireless worker, you I mean, he going to puts in hours now. Um, we've known each other for a long, long time. Uh, we had coached together before at at Boston College when I was coaching DBs and he was coaching with me. Um, we just have a very, very similar philosophy and thought process on football. >> From your perspective, how different does Brian look this spring as opposed to last spring? Brian Thompson? >> Yeah, I mean, he's he looks great. He's done a heck of a job. I mean, honestly, last year I thought he was pretty good, too. Uh, sorry about that. >> Uh, yes. >> Good. >> Yeah. >> All right. >> Yeah, he's he's done a great job. Um, I thought he did a great job last year and and uh he's really had a great spring. I think you guys obviously have seen that. Um, but he's one of those guys. He's big, long guy that can really run and um, you know, there's not that many of those guy many of those guys walking around. So, he's tough to cover. What did you like about Zack Gury, you know, coming out and what have you seen from him so far? >> Really what we've seen out here, you know, that's what we liked about him. He practices super hard, plays hard all the time. Um, I think Zach's a really good pass rusher, but he's stouted the point of attack, so he can set a firm edge in a run game. Um, and he's just a big guy that's really, really athletic. You know, he's got some hybrid qualities in terms of being a defensive lineman that can do some linebacker jobs. So, we're always looking for guys with position, flexibility, and versatility. Um, and he was one of those guys that we thought he had those qualities and when you watched him play, he just played hard as hell. So, that's something I've been I certainly haven't been surprised by his effort in practice. That's what we expected. >> Hard to believe we're talking about Josh being bigger and stronger, but he looks bigger and stronger. >> Yeah, you like that. >> Yeah. Yeah, absolutely. I think he looks great. Uh, I said a couple weeks ago, I was talking about Eric Ciano and and his staff. I think they've done an incredible job with these guys. Josh isn't the only guy, but he looks great. I mean, he's put on good weight. you know, there's uh obviously you can put on weight, but it's got to be good weight and he still looks he's super strong at the point of attack and and he's got that first step and explosion that uh we love about him. >> What would that >> I just think it it benefits him in every which way, you know what I mean? Finishing the rush at the top of the rush, uh you know, when you're working speed to power, you can't tell me that that that's not something that's an advantage to you, you know, cuz his lower half uh is super strong and we talk about that in a run game. you know, your hands. Obviously, the guy who strikes first wins, but you know, the ass whooping's done with your legs, your hips, and low back. And, uh, you know, we got that. Got a bunch of guys with that lower body strength in the front, and that's what we're always looking for. >> Just said he thought the secondary was vastly improved. You agree? >> Yeah, I think we're getting there every day. It's a process. You know, this stuff in the spring is great, but, you know, uh, >> it don't really matter much what you do in your underwear. You know, it's about who's going out there and who's going to be physical uh, when we get out get back here in the summer. But this is always a good start and I think fundamentally our guys have improved a bunch since we started this spring. >> What do you think of a healthy armstead this year? >> What do we need from him? Um, we just need I I think the production that we were seeing before Eric got hurt and you know as he came back obviously he pushed through it uh pushed through an injury at the end of the year and Eric is a a huge guy inside. He creates great middle push. He's got elite pass rush value for us for us. So um you know we just need him to keep going the way he's been going. Besides your self scout during the offseason, which other teams got your attention like either the pressures they were at? >> Yeah, every year, every year you watch everybody and you kind of try, you know, you usually stay in the the top five, top 10 in different areas, uh, you know, that you're trying to improve upon. Um, but there's a bunch of teams and I I think it's a it's a little bit of a copycat league for sure, but you know, we've watched some teams and then I'll always watch the guys that, you know, I have familiarity with and similarities with in our system. So any of those teams, you know, uh any of those guys I work with, we're always watching each other's stuff. For sure. >> How important has Foyer been sort of just to lead the defense by example over over the last few years? >> Yeah, he's like having a coach on the field, you know what I mean? Um he's a great guy to coach. Just a great person and uh great leader. But the thing that's awesome about him is he's never going to ask anybody to do anything he isn't doing himself, you know. And it's not so much what you say, it's what people see. And they see him doing the right thing all the time. they see him being hard on himself, being critical of himself. Um, but he really is a great leader and a great teacher for some of the young guys, too. He's been awesome. >> Why do you think he doesn't get all the accolades and he's led the league against in solo tackles a couple times? I mean, >> yeah, I mean, I I think if if people don't think that guy's an elite player. I mean, they don't know a lot about football in my opinion. I mean, he is watching him when I was in Miami over the years. When he was in Atlanta, I remember watching him, I'm like, man, this kid is a great player. and coming here, getting a chance to coach him, he's everything that I thought he was and more, you know what I mean? Um, he's just a fun guy to coach. He's super detailed, super smart, like you know, and you uh I have such a great appreciation for everything that he tries to do out here every day. And the uh you know, the detail he puts into everything he does. So, yeah, he's he is in my opinion uh certainly at the top level at that position. >> Coaching your young linebackers outside of Foyer, are you satisfied with how they're tracking and with their progression? I think they're coming along. I think uh coach Lukaboo's done a great job with them. I mean, he's forever grinding and and uh you know, doing everything he can to bring those guys up to speed. Uh it's a lot. We've given them a lot this spring. Um we kind of kept pushing the install on them. So, when we get back in the summer, we're ready to go. We're not really leaving any stone unturned. We want to put that stuff on tape, give ourselves the opportunity to watch it, you know, tweak it and uh critique it. And then for them, they have some familiarity with doing it. So, that's hard for a young guy because, you know, it's not all like, "Hey, base install and here you go, buddy. Let's just see you run around and play." We've pushed him. Um, and they've done a great job even fundamentally in the drill work. Temp's all over him. And he does a great job. Uh, he's pretty innovative, too, man, with some of the stuff he's done with the drill work this spring, I think, has been great. Um, and I've been very, very impressed with them. >> How important are these reps for guys like Caleb and Jaylen, who, you know, weren't able to get them last year because of injuries? >> Yeah, I'm glad you asked that question. I don't think there's any substitute for repetition. I think that's the most important thing. Um, you know, people phys physiologically we're all kind of wired the same way. You know, you get better at doing things by doing them. You get better at football by playing football. And I used to work for a really smart guy. I used to say, you know, that less is more. That that's not true. More is more. You know, more is more. Somebody offer you less money or more money and I can say, "No, I want less." You know what I mean? It's it's uh that's just what it is. So, anytime you do more, uh, you're going to get better at it. And I think we've been doing a good job of giving these guys reps and they've been doing a good job of uh you know taking them to heart and trying to do the best they can. >> Thanks. >> Appreciate it guys. >> Just how important is that for you to get everybody out there donating blood and and sort of speak about that initi? >> I mean the bigger thing is it's not important to me much so important to those kids sitting in those uh hospital beds uh have by no choice. You know what I'm saying? they're they're stuck in there, have to do blood transplants, obviously firsthand experience, seeing sometimes where, you know, hey, we have to wait, you know, for treatment cuz we don't have any blood stock. So, just to be able to give back and help um kids in need or just anybody in need. Um I think that's kind of what we're doing. Um, and so for me, man, just to bring my awareness, bring the awareness to to all, use my platform, help you guys, you know, have you guys help me spread the wealth, not only for myself, but for the kids that really need it out there. So, thank you for asking. >> You've been a part of a number of successful Jaguar units over the years. What is it about this group in particular that separates them from the previous years of success? >> You said uh Jaguar what? >> Units. >> Units. Yeah. >> As a defensive unit or team? >> Uh, both. Go. Sure. >> I mean, as a team, um, you know, we have a lot of great coaches. Not saying we haven't had great coaches in the past, but we have a lot of great coaches on both sides of the ball. Um, coach camp has done a heck of a job on just being his authentic self. And when you can be your authentic self every single day and you can be a leader of men as well, uh, that just brings out the best into everybody. Uh, makes everybody want to compete at a high level. And, uh, if you don't perform at a high level, you're going to actually feel like you're not crap. And that's a feeling that nobody wants to have. Uh because we're dependent on each other because we are a family and that's the family unit that he wants to bring. And as a team, you talking about Liam, Liam brings both both sid both sides of the ball together. And um you know, it's not just offense versus defense. That's it. It's the Jaguars versus the Jaguars. Um for us to get better every single day. And that's the motto and that's the message. Um we want to protect each other and uh make sure that we're also getting good work because we want to be the best and we got to compete at the high level to be the best. >> Good question. I'm sorry. Two years ago, I think we you talked about gaining weight. Last year, losing weight, put a little bit more on this year. >> I'm still the same way. I just look good. >> Impressive. >> So, it's not a repeat of mass kicks ass. >> This guy. >> I mean, no, you do look good. How what how have you changed your body a little bit going in? >> I don't know. I work out good. Does it feel different? >> What feels different? >> Does it Does it Do you feel different? >> I feel great. >> I feel great. Um, running around out there looking. Y'all brought to practice. How' y'all think I looked for the first time seeing me practice? >> Always. Was there intentionality to big? >> Was there intentionality on your part? >> Getting bigger. I don't not bigger though. >> How big do you think I am? >> 265. >> Okay. How big do you think I am? >> I was probably going to say like 2 268 maybe. >> You're not 267. >> Not 27. >> There it is. >> Are we in the ballpark? >> Hey Josh, you didn't you didn't go you didn't go back to Arizona. Was there >> I did go back to Arizona. >> You did? Okay. So So do you feel like you're done there for this year? Are you >> Yeah, I only go I only go to Arizona um in the beginning now. If I'm not in OTAAS, I would be in Arizona. >> Okay. >> But I'm here in OTAAS. Was it intentional year two to to gain some continuity with this group? >> Um, yeah. I mean, you know, I mean, I think I think we have a good chance to win the whole thing. Um, and you know, talking to the coaches during the offseason, you know, the plan was, you know, we we had a different strategy coming to this, you know, attacking this program right here. And, um, you know, so far, you know, I think we've gotten better as a unit. Uh there's still steps that we need to take to become the defense that we need to become. Do I think we're there right now? I don't think so. But do I see the the growth and the mindset that everybody has to attack each and every day? Yes, I do. So that kind of gives me hope that to know that we are taking those steps and you know we come back training camp um you know put pads on you know obviously be a little bit more physical for both ends and uh I think that's when we can really try to test to see what the growth we really had cuz now you start putting physicality into assignment stuff if you really paying attention to one thing and the other. Um and that's kind of what we're well you know obviously I'm not going to say I'm waiting for it but you know I'm looking forward to that time comes. I know you guys push each other every year. >> I mean, obviously, you know, you step on the field, you want to be the best player in the National Football League. Um, you know, when you talk about duos in the National League, you know, every that's the new thing now. What's the duo? The dual this, duo that. Um, so you know, if that's what they're talking about, let's be a part of that conversation. Um, let's solidify ourselves as the best duo and, uh, you know, these aren't things that we talk about. These are the expectations that we have for each other. But, you know, if my level of play is at a high level and his levels of play, that comes naturally. Um, and that's kind of our mindset. You know, we want to be we Trey wants to break my record. I want to beat my record. I want to get Miles Garrett record. And, uh, you know, so these are the growths that we're taking. If we can both achieve those things, obviously we'll become the best duo. So, >> what have you seen from the two the two rookie defensive ends, Zack Derpy and Wesley Williams? >> I mean, you know, they're in the playbook, obviously. Um, you know, again, you know, we haven't did anything yet. You know what I mean? And, you know, and that's not a test.
