If he gives you something, are you going to go power? Are you going to go speed edge? Are you going to take the inside? Um, but instinctually, they're playing really fast, which is a good sign right now. But again, like, you know, ask me this question once we get into camp and then I can give you a better in-depth answer of how I really felt. But outside of that, man, they're great kids. They're great great young adults. They're I don't know. They're great. They're great men and uh they're very responsive for themselves and for the team. >> Seeing as you look and weigh exactly the same, where do you want to get better? >> Uh I mean, you know, you know, we have a good thing. You know, our coaching staff does a good job on, you know, find your three better, three best. And, you know, when you can sit back and you can analyze yourself, which is, you know, what I do. I look at my tape, where can I get better in, and I can write these things down. And then you go to your coaching staff and they say, "Hey, these are the areas." And when they can match together, uh, that's a good sign of we're we're all on the same page. And, you know, for me, it's just, you know, keying the ball a little bit better. You know, a lot of those sacks, I mean, a lot of those pressures, a lot of those hits can become sacks if I scoot up on the ball a little bit more by just a hair. You know, if I can get off, if I can, you know, anticipate the snap count a little bit better. These are all things that those pressures, those hits can become sacks, um, and force turnovers. So, you know, we're all on the same page of that. That's one thing that I've been trying to emphasize offseason, just the little details and, uh, and and and being on it, you know, every single play, not taking a play off on those details. Um, and that's kind of like my main focus just just OTAAS and we're doing good with it. >> Jaylen Mloud told me you're somebody he watches a lot just kind of picking up on the things you do. What have you kind of seen from him? Just his mindset, you know, second a guy going into his second year who kind of wants to make an impact. >> Yeah, I mean his first year obviously he didn't play. Um, so for him this is a show us who you are. Uh, prove yourself. And I think every day, you know, he he dang these dang nets. I'm sorry. Um, you know, he's attacking every day as a pro. Uh he's taking care of his body. Uh I'm not saying he's being me in the training room every morning, but he's right next to me. You know, working on something. Um you know, he's eating the right food. He's taking the right notes. He's asking the right questions. And uh you know, and it's translating out here on the field. You know, there's a couple good rushes that he had today. And I can't wait to look at him to kind of just see where he's at and to tell him, "Hey, next time, you know, once you set him up right here, what's your counter to that?" Cuz he know he's going to overset you. He's going to do this. and you know he's taking those steps and you know I like Jaylen and then you know he plays the run really well you know he's gonna continue to grow and get better for us >> like you said not a ton you can glean necessarily right now because there are no pads on but on the other side of the ball what have you seen from the offense in terms of taking the next step whether that's in the run game or the pass game or maybe >> sure >> couple players in particular that you feel like oh wow like I I'm now seeing the work of the offseason. Yeah, I mean we got a lot of obviously the O line, you know, I see those see those guys every day. Um, again, like when you talk about pass rush, I think, you know, Ton has got I think every guy has gotten better and I think we've gotten better as a whole. Um, but again, no pads is is kind of hard. The run game, you can't really get the run game going because like you don't want to hurt each other, but you also want to be in your right fit. So, there's a little competition there. Um, but you look at our skill guys, you know, BT's having a heck of a camp. Uh he had a heck of a day today which I don't like but it's good to see you know uh Jacobe you know true professional pros pro you know Parker you know Parker man Parker's been absolutely everywhere this offseason you look at our even our tight ends man um Tanner had a heck of a play right and he talks crap you know what I'm saying like he know he talks to talk so you know when you and Strange you know one of the most physical tight ends I've seen in a in a very long time um but can also run run good routes and then Trevor, >> you know, putting the ball where he needs where he needs to put it at. Um, but again, you know, how how good can we get each other better every single day and um, you know, that's our motto and we're going to stick with it. >> What would you rate >> Tanner? Yeah. >> I mean, he don't trash talk me yet. You know what I'm saying? I ain't put my hands on him yet. But, you know, just to see him make plays and to celebrate and not just like catch the ball, get a touchdown, and just turn back and get to the huddle. Like, I want to see you talk crap. I want to see you showbo. I want to see you. You can't touch me. You can't hold me. You know, I like I want to see that. Um and he does he does a good job at that. So, um big target, you know, can fast, you know, really fast, can move well. Um I think he's going to be a good asset for us. >> We have >> I was just saying BJ was your rookie last year. Um he started his foundation this year off the field. Just what type of a guy is he? >> Uh I love BJ, man. Um, you know, he's one of the funniest people I've been around in the football in this football world. Um, on the field, you know, he's very type A. Um, but off the field, man, he is he is he is a whole different person, man. And when he puts his mind to something, he does it. Like, you know, he went we went to London, he got the shopping, he's like, "Man, I like this fashion stuff. Now he's a model." You know what I mean? Like, it's he's he he's so funny, man. He's he's a great person, great teammate, uh great brother. He's accountable outside the building. When you need him to do something, when you need him to be somewhere, he's right there. Um and you know, he's been a he's been he was a good rook for me last year and he's a good he's about he's a good leader to the younger guys now. You know, he leads by example and uh his foundation um I'm not going to be able to make it to his foundation, but I know he's doing something for the kids to go watch the movies. Um, I wish I could make it uh to help him, but it's a good thing that he can do something to give back to the community. Man, it's always good to to not just think about yourself. >> Did I do what? >> You still drink those energy drinks? >> I'm not obligated to speak on that. >> I told him his teeth is what I'm worried about. >> Hey, you can pay to get those fixed. Thank you guys.

title: Quay Walker, Jalen Nailor, AJ Cole and Joe DeCamillis Presser - 6.10.26
text: All right. Uh, first I just want to say real quick, just really want to thank because I haven't been up here yet, but I really want to thank ownership, Coach Kubiaak, and Spy for bringing me in. It's been unbelievable. It's been a great few months. Can't wait to uh can't wait to get this thing rocking and rolling for sure. But, uh, just wanted to mention that. So, let's go ahead and rock and roll. >> What attracted you to this? What about Clint Kubak attracted you to come here to Las Vegas? >> Well, uh, I worked for his dad. His dad actually played for us in Denver when I first started. He was a quarterback there. Um [snorts] had a chance, you know, he asked me to uh come with him a couple other times and I wasn't able to go with him because I was under contract to a few other places, but uh [snorts] ton of respect for the family. Um and then I worked with Clint for a year uh when he was uh quality control in 16. So I'd already had a relationship with him. Uh it just worked out great. Um there's a lot of similarities between him and his dad, but there's some differences, too. He's uh both are very very detailed or detail oriented. Uh they they love ball which I think is huge and uh he's done a great job of organizing things since he's been here which I knew he would. So it's uh it's great to be with him for sure and the whole staff. I worked with a few guys that are on the staff also. >> Kirk Cousin said yesterday that Kubiaak comes into the building with a sense of urgency like he wants to get the ball rolling. Do you kind of sense that as well from him? >> Oh yeah. He's uh he's all ball man. I mean you know he's just very serious. Um he's uh he's a little bit like a lawyer, man. When you when you starts talking, he's you're billing hours right there with him for sure. You know, I mean, he it's all ball for him, which is uh which is great. That's nice to be able to work with and and he's a good person, too. I mean, that's that can't be uh you know, talked about enough because in our business, it's not always like that, but he's a great person. >> Joe, when you look at Dylan lobby, he's different position, but he's a Swiss Army knife like our friend Mike Furry, just sticks in the lead. Will you talk about Dylan and how you see him evolving in your schemes? >> Yeah. How do you know Mike Furry, by the way? >> He's the best, man. I love him. Make sure you tell him I said hello. >> Yeah. Awesome. Uh, no, I think uh he's done a great job throughout the OTAAS. Um, he's another one that really really sharp, gets the game, and um, you know, he knows the way he's going to make it is by the more he can do, and uh, he's he's accentuated that all the way through camp. And, uh, I really like him so far. you know, obviously OTAAS, we haven't put any pads on or any of that stuff, so you'll find out more as we go through it, but uh really like the kids so far for sure, and I think he's going to be a good player for us. >> What's it been like watching the the two the two kickers compete, the veteran Matt Matt Gay and and the rookie? Um what it's been like watching them uh go go at it? >> Well, uh first of all, I think um when they came in, the good thing about having Matt, uh you know, I've been with him before and Matt's really helped uh Special K quite a bit. you know, he's done a good job as far as getting him squared away with some of his technique and some of that, which is great for an older guy to be able to do, especially when you're competing for the job. But, um, you know, the competition's been good. Um, you know, hopefully we can get Matt back on the the same plane that he was when, uh, when I had him in LA. And I think, uh, I think Special K is going to be really good, too, down the road. So, should be a hell of a competition. >> I'm going to stick with Special K as well over here on the on the name. but um he was late to the game and and late to the technique and everything that goes into being a kicker. Have you ever worked with somebody that's kind of this new at this level um you know kind of learning on the fly? >> Yeah, it's it's hard to say you know that I've ever had anybody like him. I've had uh a guy named Jay Feelely who uh you know he was getting ready to get out of it went to a camp and he ended up you know kicking for about 14 more years after that. So it was kind of a different story but you know more selftaught. Um, but this guy's done a great job in college. Like he he had film to watch. It wasn't like he just came off the street and you know he's one of those try out guys that never kicked. I mean he had great film in college to watch and uh you know I think it's going to be a heck of a story and hopefully he's able to compete with Matt and and we picked the best guy. >> So follow on that with regards to the competition. Is it as black and white as who just makes more kicks, who's more accurate or are there other variables you're looking for for that spot? >> Other variables. I mean I think I think a lot of it um you know you want to see them like today we tried to put him in some pressure situations. is you want to try to get as many of those as you can because obviously end of the game kicks are more important than end of the game, end of the half kicks are more important than just the normal ball for sure. So, they have to be able to do both. But, uh, you know, there's a lot of things that go into play with all that stuff. I think the biggest thing that when you get a kicker and he's able to operate at a high level is because he's got a high operation level. Like the snapper and the holder are elite and uh that's the first thing that we got to make sure that we bring both of those guys every time. How much did you know about Matsuzawa's story before you guys signed him? Whereas did you learn most of it after he >> Yeah, I mean, when you go through all the draft process and all that stuff, you learn about it and talk to him. Maris, who uh is with us? Um he'll be one of our guys that's that's helping uh he tore his Achilles during uh during spring, but he'll be back here pretty soon. But anyway, he uh he had known his agent and then we got in touch with his agent and kept going from there and and uh it was very helpful to have that uh information from him, but then as you start watching the film, we had a a pretty good feel for what he was and how he's done things. >> We know it's early in the process, but when you're out there coaching, we see the attention to detail that you're putting into it. How have you felt the players have reciprocated that and taken that in? >> I think they've responded well. Um the one thing that I've noticed about this group that's that's impressive to me is their capacity for work. like when they work, they work and they roll. Um, but like you said, the details are the things that gonna make us to where we want to get to. We can't we can't be a team that just gives effort. In my opinion, like in the NFL, that should be part of your contract. When they say effort, you shouldn't have to coach effort. If you do, then it should be a breach of conf contract in my opinion. That's that's something that, you know, everybody should put out. And, uh, these kids have done that and they've they've really shown a really really good capacity to work so far. What does Sakuna Alooi add to your units? >> Uh he's a differencemaker type guy. You know, he's blocked punts in a league. He obviously had one against the Raiders last year. Um he's a guy that uh is twitchy. He's a guy that um has already shown what he can do on the field and he's and he's brought a lot to the to the group for us already. So, it's it's going to be good to coach him. I'm I'm excited we have him. >> Coach, early in the year, but the leadership you're seeing from Cousins and Crosby, so many leaders out there, what has impressed you so far? >> [snorts] >> Well, I mean, Max is he's a unicorn, man. I mean, you just don't see him like that. I mean, you know, I mean, I know the trade thing. Everybody's always talked about that. Um, I'm glad it didn't go through. I can tell you that much cuz I love the guy. I think he's one of the guys that that uh, you know, you're proud to be around for sure. He's got he's got an unbelievable love of the game and he's got an unbelievable passion for work, which I think will carry on to these other guys. And then Kirk, I told him the other day, I said, "I love the way you ball, man." because he's he's a guy that, you know, you watch around the league and you don't really unless you've worked with him, you don't know what kind of guy he is and he's he's exactly what you're looking for. No question why he's been as good as he's been. >> Anybody else? Cool. Thank you. Thank you. >> How excited you were to be teaming up with Nico Dean. Um, on the flip side of that, how disappointing has it been that you haven't really been able to take the field with him yet? >> Uh, I wouldn't quite say it been disappointing. I just know he here every day. So, uh, I still have a job to do myself. You know what I'm saying? You never know what happened or whatever the case may be. But he's still here every day. That's all I can really say as of now. >> Qu, you have an extremely high football IQ. I mean, at Georgia, three years waiting to get in that starting lineup, but when you did, you burst on. And that has helped you throughout your career. you're always getting better. >> Would you talk about where that drive comes from with you, please? >> Uh, honestly, I think it came from uh me not actually playing inside linebacker before I got to college. So, I had to learn it and it took me a little while, especially with being in the Kirby smart system. It was so much that he put on inside linebackers and it was new for me. I feel like football was new cuz I had to learn how to play inside. Um, sometimes it's easy for to let your instincts like just take over and play, but uh you can miss one assignment and it can be an explosive or a touchdown. And Kirby ain't really he much nicer than what he is now. I mean, he he wasn't as nice as he is now is what I meant to say. But, um, so anything I would do, uh, I know he would be real real hard on me. So, that kind of played a factor in it. And I remember trying to transition back to outside linebacker cuz that was kind of natural for me. And I feel like I could do that with dropping the coverage and doing stuff like that. But honestly, man, I just always try to attack every day and see how can I become a better player. I'm so hard on myself to the point where any little thing that goes wrong, uh, I kind of beat myself up about it. So, I'm just trying to give myself a little grace. That's what I've been working on this off seasonason. Anytime something go wrong, just give myself some grace and, uh, try to have a next play mentality so I can, you know, move forward cuz I know it's a lot to come. You know what I'm saying? I can make a play that nets that Nits play although I probably gave up something or whatever the case may be. So I'm just trying to move with the right mindset. >> I've been impressed watching you teach I specifically I watched you the other day the day you got the interception teaching Cody. What has been your impression? He's a young guy but sponge like you were when you were young. >> Uh honestly man Cody is a guy who's tremendously like smart. Um knows everything, know what everybody's supposed to be doing and stuff like that. Um um it's it's certain things that I feel like I can help him with as in uh being off the quarterback, whatever they may be. Uh just any little thing. So any advice I can give him, I try to just give it to him. And he's like a sponge. He soak up anything I give to him. Uh he don't feel any type of way. I don't try to be on him as much. I still allow him to be himself, but um if I can help in any way, I just try to do that and he always listen to me. So shout out to Cody for sure. What's been the benefit of having so many guys on the defense that can move play multiple spots on the >> Say it again for right here. >> What's been what do you think is the benefit of having multiple guys on the defense that can play multiple spots on the field like you? Honestly, man, it's a lot uh for offense going in that week um ahead of so in uh we're playing a safe in is week one and a team is just trying to get us together whatever the case may be and they present you know what I'm saying our defense know we have a lot of guys that played this play that you know what I'm saying they just move around in a lot of areas so now it's kind of hard to scout against us and tell what we are doing like say for instance I'm on the line you never know if I'm going to drop or I'm if I'm going to rush you know what I'm saying whether that's to the field or the boundary same same with Chin, Quiddy, no matter what the case may be, Matts, uh, it just whole lot, you know what I'm saying? It just, it kind of helps. And play hand in hand with the whole defense, I'll say. >> Qu, as one of the leaders on this defense, um, how satisfied are you with the progress that you guys have made this offseason as you wrap it up? And also, what's the message so that when you hit the pause button here, nothing gets lost and that you guys hit the ground running in training? >> I'm going to start with the the last question. Honestly, man, just standing in the playbook. You know what I'm saying? Because this is this is new. Uh, we've been challenged in different ways. I'm playing more positions that I probably ever played in my career, but this is a challenge that I'm willing to accept. This is what I've always wanted to do. I want I always want to be a guy who can move around and play multiple positions. And uh honestly, man, where we at right now? Uh we're growing each and every day. That's all you can ask for. Uh a lot of teams are preaching the same thing around this time. So, uh how are we going to separate oursel in order for us to get to what we want to get and to get what we can get out of, you know what I'm saying, the OTAAS and this offseason? So, we just got to stay locked in with it and just have the mindset. And as as a leader, it's my job. I feel as if coming in with the right mindset and make making sure that guys can match my energy, whatever the case may be. >> Qu, what's the difference in uh last year playing in a 4-3 defense in Green Bay and playing what's expected to be a 34? What's that preparation been like? And how do you think you you adapt to it? >> Uh, honestly, I think football is football at the end of the day. I think there's no system that I can't play in. Not that I'm just speaking so highly of myself, but um football is football at the end of the day. It's kind of similar because I played in three, four of my my first two years in the league. Not only that, at UG I did the same thing. Uh so just being comfortable with that. Um and that's kind of it. I don't really say it's a difference. I feel like uh scheme wise it kind of is, but at the end of the day, football is still football. You know what I'm saying? So that's all I can say. Kay, although uh you haven't been able to dress with Nico here in Las Vegas, you guys did spend some time together in Georgia, right? Just how what can you say about his presence just both on the field and in the locker room that he can still bring about? >> It's it's different. Um honestly, this is no knock on anybody who I played uh played with beforehand. Like I played with Edin Cooper who's a pretty pretty like tremendous guy. But me playing with the Kobe, this is a connection that I had with him way before, you know what I'm saying? We got to this level. It's been a minute since I played with him, but you know what I'm saying? It's kind of natural. So, I kind of know what he's thinking. I kind of know what he, you know what I'm saying? It may take a while cuz it's still been years, but I feel like um we just pick up well off one another. We can feed off each other real real well. And I know some days we all human. So, some days he may come in, he may not be feeling it a little bit or I may not be feeling it, but um we can like feel each other energy. We can just pick up and push one another. I know one day we [snorts] was in here working out in OTAAS and uh I kind of picked it up a little bit. You know what I'm saying? We was going at it a little bit and he fed off of that. So that kind of reminded me back to I don't want to keep talking about UG, but you know what I'm saying? Like that's what it is. You know, go dogs by the way. Sorry. >> What's been the mindset for you as an outside linebacker versus being off the ball as an inside linebacker each play? So you're going in and out of it. What's that mindset of what you or the checklist that you go through each play? >> Uh, honestly, I just had the same mentality, man. At the end of the day, you got to win your 101. Just got to stay physical. Anytime you physical and you can just beat the guy that kind of that cross everything out, you know what I'm saying? Just being relentless. That's all my mindset every play. How can I be relentless? How can I win this rep? Anytime I move down on the edge, first thing come to mind is all right. Um, my awareness kick in. I'm trying to rec I'm having pre- snap um awareness. Just trying to see what the formation is and see what I can recognize and see if it's going to be run or see if it's going to be passed or whatever the case may be. The run coming to me, make sure I set the edge and do my job. Not try to go one for one, but uh just try to be as physical as I can. Honestly, make you know what I'm saying? Making many plays as I can as well. So, uh it don't really change I'll say for sure. So, I just keep the same. >> Oh, you go. >> Uh Qu Rob Leonard told us that he wants the defense to play very fast and aggressive. Um what kind of freedom does that give you as a player? How does that match your style of play? >> Uh, I mean that's the that's kind of describe me. Uh, anytime I can be fast and be aggressive, I think I'm at my best. Anytime I got to sit right there and just think a whole lot. Not saying I don't want to do that, but playing inside linebacker, that's that's the kind of what it takes. You know what I'm saying? You have to think and react within two to three seconds, whatever the case may be. But anytime we can just play, line up and play and just react and play fast and be aggressive. Uh, that's the way I want to do it. And I think that's why my style fit uh this organization. You know what I'm saying? I think it's the right way. >> Going back to Georgia, you got to have a Brock Bower story and and Zeus told us a ton of them when he >> got here. What is >> talk about him early what you saw? >> Honestly, I knew Brock I think all of us kind of knew Brock was >> Brock. Well, I don't want to say that. I'm trying to see how I can word this. We know he was special soon as probably say fall camp came around and fall camp is is pretty hectic especially as a freshman you not knowing what to expect man it's hot whatever the case may be is tempo is very very high like it's hard you know what I'm saying but that that didn't like change his mindset at all uh he didn't fade away or do anything like that so um seeing him what he doing now uh it's it's not a surprise at all you know what I'm saying to see what he did his freshman year that was the only year I played with him so to see him just Bro, u man, it's uh it been tremendous just to watch, you know what I'm saying? Just to see even on Sundays when I wasn't here, just to see him. So, I'm not surprised at all cuz he's a hard worker. He don't say much. He kind of talking a little bit more. You know what I'm saying? Then I when I first met him. So, now he talking a little bit more. But, uh yeah, man. It's tremendous to see. >> What's the biggest piece of advice that you've been able to try to give to to Cody and Tommy in that room now kind of having some more years under your belt? What is the biggest thing you want to pass on to them? Uh honestly man just never forget uh this is an opportunity that all of us as we always pray to be in uh sometimes we can lose the train of thought of that like uh we kind of like focus on everything else instead of just being directly in the moment and just being thankful for where we are. So I just try to keep in keep them with the right mindset as in uh man this is everything you work for. Never lose the train the thought of that. Um anytime you out there man just play with confidence. You know what I'm saying? It's going to be challenges that comes but man just go out there and just play. It's the reason you here. You know what I'm saying? And it's a lot of people that's dying to be in our shoes. Uh a lot of people may say this or say that, but if everybody could do it, they'll be right here. But that's not the case. So we part of the 1% that's doing it. And so that's all I try to say. I just try to encourage people with those type of words. >> How would you describe Clint Kubak as a coach? >> Uh, tremendously. Uh, there's so much that I can say. Uh, some days he got high energy, some days he quiet. He kind of hard to read a little bit, but that's a good thing. I think I'm kind of hard to read, too. So, but you know, uh, he kind of he's a coach who wanted this team to be player le and that's the first thing when I first met with him that I pretty much enjoyed. uh I want to say that I enjoyed but that was the first thing that I kind of respected that stood out to me when I first had a conversation with him. He wanted to find out who the leaders were right away. You know what I'm saying? He didn't waste no days. Probably the first two to three days of OTAAS. He wanted this team to be player led. Anytime a team is player le that leads to wins and I just continue to build and be able to build. But I wish I can go more in tune like more in depth with it. But I'm still learning him as well. So, and I don't really talk I talked to him, but you know, he more so on the offensive side than the defensive side. But we talk as much as we can, but give me probably about two more week two more weeks and I can have a better answer for you for sure. >> Queen, Green Bay, you play for teams that qualify for the playoffs. >> And coming here to Las Vegas is a organization has been to the playoffs a lot over the last 10, 15 years. From that process, what do you take from Green Bay that you bring here for a lot of guys who don't understand that process of what it takes to get to the playoffs? >> Man, it's a day in and day out type of thing. Uh it's a certain mentality that you have to have. Uh you can't you really got to take it week by week. You know what I'm saying? You got to be you got to prepare the same way each and every day. You got to come in with the right mindset and like I said, it has to be a player le team and that'll leads to the wins and the victories, but it also leads to the sense of urgency uh that you have to have for otaas and lean up into the season. You know what I'm saying? Even when practice come, you have to the sense of urgency for the team has to be up. And so, uh for me as a leader, I just want to come in here with the right mindset because I know what it takes to win. Uh I I didn't win the big one when I was at Green Bay. Uh, I probably didn't get to, you know what I'm saying, close the game right before to the Super Bowl, however you want to put it. But, um, I still feel like I have a winning mentality. And, uh, I kind of just want to bring my leadership and just my presence and my energy to this to this organization. I feel like that's part of the reason why I actually came here cuz I wanted to be a part of a guy. I want to be a guy that can actually turn the organization around and get us back to where, you know what I'm saying, we used to be. So that's all I can say >> with your speed, strength, and everything without getting into scheme. You're a Swiss Army knife. You can play a lot of different places. How much do you like that in Robbie's plan? You could see you all over the place utilizing you, not just pigeon holing you to one spot. >> Yeah, that's kind of what I said. Uh honestly, I remember when I first signed here, um and we were doing an interview up here and I uh got back to I'm being used the right way. I think the last team I played for, I think kind of took it the wrong way. I wasn't saying it out of, you know what I'm saying? Just to be disrespectful towards the previous scene, which is the Packers, I was just saying like I'm moving around in different places. I feel like that's where my strength are. It's like you can move me down on the ball or you can bring me back. It's a lot that I can do. And uh I just feel like right now I'm being used the right way. I would never say uh it's more than I can chew. Uh but it's everything that I want. So, I won't sit right here and I complain or anything like that. Like I told Robbie, like I got his back. Um, so whatever the case may be, I can do it. So, I'm just happy that, you know what I'm saying? He can he view me as a player that can do multiple things and help me out. You know what I'm saying? So, that's what I'm happy for. >> You uh you played against Kirk obviously in the NFC North. What's it been like being his teammate in this short period? What have you learned about him? >> I don't learn a lot, man. We talk about everything and honestly I kind of like I always reflect back to when I did play on Minnesota cuz so I kind of know Kirk a little bit. I don't want to say too much right here in front of this podium but uh yeah so I kind of know him a little bit so I can like pretty much just reflect back to when I did play him in Minnesota what he might do uh anything like that. So it's kind of easy. I ain't going to say easy but I'm kind of used to it is what I'm trying to say. Kind of used to him. >> Were you on the field when he tore Achilles? >> Uh yeah I were. I was >> what's it like? You know, coming coming full circle. He talked about how much healthier he feels now. Like, are you seeing that? >> We actually talked about that. U because know that happened at at Lambo, I want to say. And uh we just talked about that. We talked about that. Talked about a play that I supposedly made. I think he I posted a pit. I dropped it. We talked about that. But uh honestly, man, I just think it's it full circle. Even when he was in Atlanta last year, just talking about how healthy he feel coming back on it. Uh, you know, that's a that type of injury can like challenge you mentally. You know what I'm saying? It's not easy to come back from, but I think he done all the right things to be back to, you know what I'm saying, who he to who he is and things of that nature. So, that's it. >> All right. Thanks, >> appreciate y'all. >> Hey, >> AJ, when you are obviously Daniel Carlson, what a wonderful person. one of your best friends leaves, but that's the business of the NFL. Will you talk about your role in teaching a young kicker and helping them who obviously they look up to your success and in all your longevity? >> Uh, yeah, definitely. I think it's been um it's been really interesting having rookies around, having Tyler and K around. we haven't had uh we haven't had rookies in training camp um in a while. So, it's interesting for me to be able to help them with their journey. There's so many things that you take for granted having known having played in this league for a little bit. And so, for me, getting to kind of relive my rookie year through them a little bit and get to tell them what my experiences were like going through OTAAS and training camp has been really fun. And uh I think there's a lot of learning that I've done as well, like reflecting back on my process because there's some questions that they ask me and I almost have some routines or habits that are just second nature at this point and I'm having to explain why I do what I do and I think that's helped me grow as well. So I think it's been a mutually beneficial situation, but they're both really talented young players and it's it's been fun to kind of work with them. >> What is the best way to describe Clint Kubak since you've gotten a chance to interact with him the past couple months? Yeah, I think he's all football. I think he's very genuine. What you see is what you get. Um and he just wants to win and he's going to do whatever it takes to to get that done here. Um but yeah, he's he's all football. Um and uh he's very very motivated and very driven. >> You've seen a lot of different coaching staffs, a lot of different regimes. Um what gives you the hope that this is the right one and this one's going to work? >> Yeah. Um, yeah, and I've seen a lot is my sixth head coach. Um, and I think the the main takeaways I have on what it takes to be successful as a head coach is you have to be authentically yourself. Um, and then you have to hire good people around you and trust them to do your job. And so far, that's all that he's done. And so, it's been really fun to see that. Um, I think he knows who he is. I think he's very confident and comfortable in his own skin. And that's a really impressive quality. um because I think that any kind of uh lack of authenticity is pretty easily sniffed out. Um and so I think that um it's been really cool to see the yeah just the confidence in who he is and uh I think he's hired a great staff and I think he really trusts the people around him and I think that's going to go a long way. >> Coach Zill was here a second ago and he he kept referring to Matazawa as special K. Is that the the name you guys have for him here? And where does that come from? >> Uh yeah, I think it uh it's what it's what Jod's been calling him a little bit. I've been trying to call him conc. But the first couple days I wasn't super confident in the pronunciation. So I was like, what? But I was also like, you can't just meet a guy and right off the bat start calling him the Tokyo Toe. It's kind of a mouthful, you know, like, hey, good morning the Tokyo Toe. It just doesn't exactly roll off the tongue. But I wasn't 100% sure in the pronunciation. So I also was kind of like I was either saying it like really quickly or kind of mumbling through it. I was like, "Hey, hey, what's going on, man?" Like, but then and then at some points too when he was at a distance and I had to say it loud, we were just calling him K. Now I feel really comfortable with the pronunciation. Um but uh yeah, I think that uh Special K maybe is a it's you know, it's not as it's not quite as good as the Tokyo Toe. The alliteration on that's pretty unbelievable, but Special K is a it's a good backup nickname. seems like a pretty high energy coach himself. Um, is that an adjustment for you at all or um is it is how interesting and is it hearing a new voice and maybe that new kind of level of intense? >> Yeah, I mean I'm in my eighth season and although I've had all these different um head coaches, it's only my third special teams coordinator full-time. Um, so yeah, it's been uh it's been a blast to work with him. I've really enjoyed it. I've really um appreciated his insight into, you know, the things that uh he thinks I do well, the things he wants me to improve on, and the things that I think we can do together. He's got such a unique approach. He's very creative, like you said. He's very energetic. Um and I think that for special teams at this level, I think that's very, very critical. Um because the reality is most people don't grow up wanting to play left tackle on punt team. They want to be the starting linebacker. Most people don't grow up saying, "Oh, I want to be the wing. They want to be the starting running back." But we need those guys to do that job at a high level. And so when he comes into the room with that energy and that fire and that passion, I think it lights it in a bunch of other people. And so hopefully, I mean, I'm confident that that will bring the best out of the group. >> Hey, for seven years, the elite operation of snap, hold, and kick was pretty similar play in and play out. It won't be that way this year with Daniel not being here. So, how do you build that chemistry with the guys that you have so far, Conc obviously and Matt, how do you continue to build that chemistry on how they may want that ball settled? >> Yeah, it's just reps. I mean, it's just doing the work. It's just showing up here every single day, getting the work in. Um, and then being really intentional about those reps and asking them, "Hey, how do you want this? How do you want that? How do you want this done?" And it's not just the technical aspect of them getting comfortable with me holding, me getting comfortable with knowing how they want the football. It's also the mental aspect of it of like I I see myself not only as the holder when I'm out there, but also as their caddy. So like what do you want from me in terms of communication? Do you want me to talk a lot? Do you want me to just shut up? Do you want me to just listen? Do you want me to ask questions different parts of the game? Do you want like advice? Do you want feedback? do you like what is it that you're looking for? Um end of game situation, we got a Mayday field goal. How much communication do you want from me on terms of where we are on the clock? And these are things that, you know, with Daniel and I, we worked together for so long. We we were completely speaking the same language. And so, uh, making sure that we can get to that level as quickly as possible is critical because I do think it affects their confidence. I think it affects their ability to make kicks, which affects us winning and losing football games. So figuring out all of those things, how they want me to treat them, how they want me to caddy for them, as well as how they want me to hold for them, I think is important. >> Are you reaching yourself? >> Yeah, I think a little bit. Yeah, like I was talking about earlier, there's some processes that I personally have that I they're so second nature to me, sometimes I don't even remember why I do the things that I do, the warm-ups or the mental routine or or these other things. And so when you get into some of the situational football, like when we're kicking field goals and some of the like finer details, there's some things that I'm like, yeah, for sure. Having to retach myself in terms of like, okay, this is why Daniel did it, how he did it. How do you want to do it? >> Daniel, I mean, AJ, you are very driven and my opinion and many others, you're the best punter in the NFL. How do you keep getting better? Because every year I've covered you, you do. How do you keep doing that when you're already elite? >> Yeah, I would say the biggest thing is I just have like a violent case of imposttor syndrome. I just constantly think I'm I'm uh I just don't think I stack up. I kick with other guys in the offseason constantly and I'm always uh only remembering their good punts and then deleting their bad punts. And then when I look back at my own session, I only remember my bad punts and I forget all the good ones. So if I have one bad punt in a day in a game, that's the only one I remember. And so I think part of it is um I just think that I have a little bit of that that I have to kind of work around and that's something that can potentially affect your confidence if you don't know how to properly manage it. Um and the other thing is is I don't think there's anything special about me. I think the reason that I've produced on the field the way I've produced is because of the work I've put in. It's because of the processes I have in place. And it's not like I have something different in my genetics that makes me predisposed to be better at punting because I remember what it looked like when I started. And so I don't think there's anything special or unique about me. I think what's special and unique is the work that I do. And so that's what keeps me going is because I want to be good at this game for a really long time. And I think that's what it's going to take. >> John Spitech um when he brought in all these new free agents, a lot of them are leaders and he was big on bringing in character guys. How have you kind of seen all these different leaders and different you know not just special teams but defense and as well as offense kind of come together so far? Yeah, that's a great question and we do really have a high character locker room right now and it's fun to see and I really do believe that leaders build leaders and so I think that's contagious and I think that um when you bring that quality of of person and that quality of character into the locker room it just rises the the level of everybody from a um leadership perspective from a production standpoint. Um, and so yeah, all the guys we bought brought in through free agency, through the last couple drafts, they're all really high character guys. And, um, it makes it easier to come to work with, too, when you've got less drama, less divas, people that show up excited to work, ready to go, and they don't have the, um, you know, just the droopy faces and the bad body language. Um, that's contagious as well. And so having as little of that as possible. And hopefully, you're never probably going to have a 100% buy in, but hopefully it becomes like the the cool thing or the normal thing to be excited to come to work and excited to practice and excited to do the little extra things and then it becomes um contagious in that way. And I think that's how you can kind of get the ball rolling and turn that into wins. >> Couple more guys. >> There there's first round picks and there's the first pick in the draft and on top of that a first pick quarterback. Um, Fernando walks into this locker room, walks into this building with a lot on his shoulders as a result of that. Um, were you curious what how he was going to handle that, how he was going to be, and how's your curiosity matched up with what you've seen so far? >> Yeah, I'm very impressed. I think he is just exactly what you see is what you get. Um, you know, he's it's kind of the funny thing of like in the off season when you're you're hanging out with people, friends, family, whatever, that's that's the question, right? Is like, oh, what's Fernando like? Oh, what's he like? You know, that's like the question I'm getting I'm fielding every weekend essentially from whoever I'm hanging out with. And that's just the answer I keep telling people is whatever you think he's like, that's exactly what he's like. It's not a bit, it's not an act. He's extremely genuine. He's extremely authentic. He's extremely motivated. Um, and uh I think that he's um done a fantastic job of not coming in here uh with like too much on his shoulders, just saying I want to be a great teammate. I want to help the team win. I want to learn. I want to do whatever I can. And um I think in any way that we can uh coaches, teammates, friends to take the pressure off of him, that's good. And he doesn't need to put the fate of the universe on his shoulders. We don't need him to be Superman. We just need him to be Fernando. >> Something that you uh said earlier is that you believe Klay Kubak has been his authentic self and has got a coaching staff that are also their authentic selves. when you, you know, think about Joe Damlis, you know, what's something in particular, you know, a situation that you think, you know, perfectly tells who's his authentic self? >> That's a great question. I think it's uh I think there's just you you'd have to be in the meeting room to really see it, but when he just starts going and he just starts rolling and it's just coming off um and he's going through the slides and he's just fired up that I think it's just that passion that that you can't really fake. Um, and when guys don't really love what they do, um, you can only hold on to it for so long. And we spend so much time with these coaches through practice fields, meeting rooms, etc. that, uh, it's just impossible to fake the passion that he feels for the game. And so, I don't have like a specific story for you necessarily. There's probably, uh, very few that I could share into a microphone, but uh, yeah, that that passion is just hard to replicate. >> Cool. Thank you guys. Thanks. Enjoy summer. Yesterday I flew out here in 2018 to interview you about going back to becoming one of our Spartans and the thing that's always stood out with you is everybody has speed >> but your brain, your football IQ, you're able to read things to adjust and it's just continued to get better for you at this level in your career. How do you continue to do that? >> You know, I'm just trying to find ways to improve, you know, no matter what it is. if it's seeing seeing things um that the younger guys are getting um seeing that type of stuff and I I just play that in my mind is like I'm taking a rep. So, I try to take those mental reps um and just build on that type of stuff to where once I do get in I see that coverage or I see how the defense is playing, you know, I can I can adjust and do what I got to do. >> You obviously have some experience playing with Kirk Cousins in Minnesota. Does that chemistry really kind of just pick back up where it left off when you get out here? >> Uh, pretty much. Pretty much if it feels like that. So, I mean, we just trying to grow grow as a group um as a whole offensive unit and um just just having that chemistry with Kirk. It's been great so far and um we're just trying to keep on building on that. >> You seen any differences in him kind of over that past two stops now getting here? You guys are together? >> Um, no. I wouldn't say I I would say Kirk's the same guy he was uh four years ago. um you know, he still has those dad jokes that he loves to bring and um just just the energy that he brings um to to the team and um when when guys are making plays, you know, he he's the first one celebrating and just being being happy for us to go out there and make plays. >> Obviously, the Raiders make an investment in you and on your part, uh there's a projection. How am I going to fit into this offense? What's my role going to be? Um it's been a couple months, I guess, now through OTA the offseason program. How do you see that developing? Um, you know, just trying to be be a guy that can play all over the field. Um, I think Coach Kubak does does a great job of just getting his playmakers the ball. You know, it's not just myself. Um, but has we got Trey, we got Brock, we got those guys that can do multiple things in the offense and that that's what's going to separate us as a as a unit, you know, just just to have guys just move around. You never know where they're going to be at on a single play. How much do you feel though uh if it is potentially an increased role than it was in Minnesota that you could flourish in a bigger role? >> Uh absolutely. I'm I'm looking forward to the challenge, you know. Um I I see myself as as a guy that can have that um jump from snaps um and just be be who I am, you know, and um just try to make plays when when I'm called upon and um try to bring guys with me. In 2018 when you were contemplating moving to Michigan, it was home, family, how much you love the valley. How special was it that now your journey was is bringing you back and where you get to be back? >> Uh it's a it's a blessing, you know. Um I I wasn't expecting to come back here, but you know, once I did get that call, you know, I just I just took it and um I'm just very grateful to h have this um beautiful city. You know, I have my family around me, things like that. So, um, it's it's a very it's just a blessing. >> What's your relationship been like so far with Trey Tucker? And how do you guys kind of bounce off each other and learn from one another? >> Uh, Trey Trey, yeah, he's my guy since day one, first day I got here, you know, he's been a dog, you know, with whether it's lifting, whether it's doing the extra things. Um, and you guys see it on the field like he he's always flying around. He can run all day like Coach Kubak has has expressed to you guys as well. you know, he he has a motor that is like what we what we need as as a receiver and as a receiver room, you know, just to have that type of guy that can just go and have that um examples being put out day in and day out. >> So many guys, >> so many guys keep talking about the attention to detail, eliminating the gray within this offense. >> What's been something that stood out to you about that? But then also your your role in blocking along the perimeter which we saw so many receivers in this offense create the opportunities for the running backs. >> Yeah, I mean it's no block no rock no block no rock mentality for us as receiving room. You know we got to be able to do the dirty work and um digs it. >> Who made a block no rock? Where that come from? >> Uh it came from uh my college coach, Coach Hawk. Um, so I mean just having that that mentality, it it it's not a you thing. It's it's more of a it's a team thing. We got to be a team. This is a team sport. So just just to have that type of mentality in the receiving room, you know, it's only going to make things easier for us in the pass game. And just marrying the running pass >> on the field. What's your early impressions of Fernando? >> Uh, he he he's very smart. I I would say that he's very smart. um very tall as well. You know, he can see over the offensive line. He can make those throws across the field and um very accurate things like that. So, I mean, he he's very eager to learn, which is very great for for a rookie like him being a first round pick. He's always trying to pick somebody's brain to, you know, improve. >> What uh Kurt mentioned yesterday about the s sense of urgency uh Kubak brings to the building every single day. What do you like about that that coaching style from him? >> I love it. I love it, man. You know, we we we we're trying to be an attacking team, you know, and um with with that sense of urgency, getting in and out the huddle, trying to catch the defense off guard or trying to move guys around on defense to not um dictate to the offense what coverage they're going to be in. So, just having that urgency, having that communication um is is playing a big role right now. Uh, Kubak mentioned this about having a player environment, letting the players make the decisions on certain thing where the quarterback decision or any other position groups. I was wondering what do you like about that philosophy from him? >> I feel like that that's what the the great teams do that when they win um they they're player le team. So, um just trying to take that um every day, you know, just trying to have guys like if if somebody's messing up like it's not going to be a coach that's saying something. We want players to correct each other and help each other out. That's how we're going to grow and get to where we got to be. >> Zach Azani was talking about how there's not really any established roles with this within this receiver room just yet and that's bred a lot of competition within the group. How have you guys kind of pushed each other through this offseason period? >> Um, you know, just we're just trying to be a whole complete room. You know, we got we want guys to be able to play all three positions inside, outside, be able to move around. So, just having that competition. Um, we're pushing each other. you know, if if somebody somebody's making a mistake, we want to help them out. And um if they're doing something right, we we we congratulate them. So, it's it's a we're just trying to build something something special here. And um going back to the player le thing like that, that's a that's a huge huge part part of this. >> I'm sure you're aware of Brock Bowers from afar, but what's your impressions now being able to share the same building with him and work with him every day? >> Uh he he's different. He's very different. Um just just the way he moves. He moves like a receiver, but he's big enough to be in the run game and um block the ends, things like that. So, like what he brings to the table is been nothing but amazing and seeing it firsthand and, you know, it's it's very great to see him and see how he works. >> What do you think is the most underrated trait about the receiver room as a whole that people you believe are just, you know, not picking up on from afar? >> Um, we we don't have egos in our room, I would say. you know, um we we all want to be um great. We all want to win. We want to do the right things on on the field, off the field, you know, so [snorts] we're just trying to be a complete room um to have guys go in like if somebody comes in for another player, we want the same expectations for for that player when they come in. So, just [snorts] having that that type of mindset and um just trying to build and just keep growing. I think that you look at Justin Jefferson obviously in Minnesota established himself as one of the best in the league and he's considered a number one and you draft Jordan in the first round he's considered the next tier wide receiver and then you had the opportunities but obviously less and far because of the guys in front of you. Now when you get here to the Raiders who sought you in free agency and people say hey they still need a number one wide receiver. What's the conversation like in that room about the need of possibly a number one wide receiver when you have so many guys who are proven that they can be a number one receiver? >> Um, I mean, I feel like we we don't even really think like that, you know, we we just try to go out and do do what we can when the play is called, you know, try to make the play and try to be in the right spot at the right moment. We we're not looking at it like, oh, we we need a number one wide receiver or or ex receiver, things like that. So, that that's not that's not our mindset. Our mindset is just focusing on each day and just growing together as a as a group. >> Is that unique? Is that sort of unique I guess in a way where there's not a set wider receiver one, wider receiver two? And is that Kubak wanting you guys as an offense to be so versatile? >> Uh I mean possibly. I couldn't couldn't really tell you uh his mindset on that, but I feel like we we have the guys to to do something um as a receiving room in this league. So, it's all about just putting the pieces together and just just growing and and just trying to compete every single day and um get each other better. >> All right, guys. Thank you. >> Thank you. Love that shirt.

title: Azeez Al-Shaair on the Texans Defense, Leadership and Minicamp | Full Q&A
text: CJ >> Hey. How y'all doing? >> CJ, as you compete against the offense, what differences do you see in their line of scrimmage? They talked about the offense being light years ahead of last season at this stage of the off season. >> Yeah, I think the biggest thing that just jumps out is when they breaking that huddle, like they're getting moving, the communication, all those guys is being on the same page. And obviously, you know, year two, same offensive coordinator, uh a majority of the same guys, even the guys that we brought in just kind of fitting right in what we're trying to do. Uh and you can just see it, you know, more confidence from everybody on that side of the ball, obviously starting with CJ, uh just commanding it. So, I think that's probably been the biggest thing that you'll see. >> Hey, Aziz, can you talk about um the group of linebackers you have? Is this one of the most competitive since you've been uh with the group that you currently have? >> Yeah, I think every year, you know, it's been competitive rooms for us and and groups. Um and I think this year is no different than the years prior, um even from my first year with the guys that we had in to last year to now. Um obviously losing EJ was a big blow to us. Um but just in general, the the guys that we have in there that that they brought in from free agency to the rookie class uh to the guys that were already here uh in the past, I think just continuing to make each other better, and that's something that I always like took pride in because in San Francisco, that's what we did, you know, me, Dre, Fred, you know, I played with Kwon Alexander, Malcolm Smith, and it was like all of us helping each other, but pushing each other to be as great as we wanted to be. >> CJ, some of the best steal kind of early in the draft, what have you noticed about Green Bay's defense as far as being in the league so far? >> Yeah, I think the thing that I love about Reed, it feels like having like just another linebacker on the field. Like the And I say that in the way that he communicates uh just urgency. You could tell like he's obviously done it at extremely high level. Already has, you know, Super Bowl to show for it and uh all the experiences and stuff like that. Uh so, I think the the number one thing that I like is just seeing that his communication even when he's not saying the right thing. Like me and him were were talking and communicating back and forth, but he's echoing everything and and talking to the defense, but there's been times where I might say a call and I was wrong and like he's yelling like the right thing like whereas other times maybe I I'll say it and maybe somebody might not hear it or whatever, but I just think like the biggest thing that I've enjoyed about uh Reed being here is just that communication piece. Obviously, I know the ability and the talent that he has, which is why he's here in the first place. Uh but I think that's something that I enjoy just about him so far. >> So, so today you made a big play. An interception was it? An interception? Um you know, what does plays like that mean uh not just to you, but to the team, especially at this point in the in the season, especially with you being a defensive leader? >> Yeah, I think obviously OTAs is is off-season training. It's that time of the year where you know, you can show up and kind of just get by or you can actually try to push yourself to be better. For me, coming into the NFL, every single day you got to show up and work and that's all I know. Um that's how I got to where I'm at in the first place. So, uh I think that's just a mentality of our team and obviously as a leader uh if you're not doing it, you know, nobody else is going really want to follow you. So, I think uh just trying to work my technique and keep getting better. It's been great competition, you know, all OTAs. Um and just excited for, you know, now putting a putting a end to OTAs and now getting ready for the 40 days away and then come back for training camp and, you know, go at it again. >> Season, unfortunately, A.J. got hurt and now you guys are looking for to someone to step up as the third linebacker. What do you see from some of the guys, the kind of stuff they're learning from you, the questions they're asking, and the way they're playing? >> Yeah, I think the the biggest thing is like whether E.J. was healthy or not, you know, it shouldn't change the mentality for any player. You know, you're you're preparing, you're treating yourself like a starter. Cuz in the NFL, we want the best of the best. We don't want the ones to be at this level and then the the drop-off to be drastic. Like the goal is that if I'm not playing, if Henry's not playing, if whoever's not playing, then whoever goes in there can seamlessly pick it up and and keep it moving. So, I don't think it changed anybody's mindset in our room. Obviously, just from the person that E.J. is and the player that he is, it sucks. He worked extremely hard and you know, all summer, you know, or all off season staying here with with all the guys and we've just been training and really just excited for what it was going to look like playing with him year two in the same scheme and everything like that. So, obviously, it sucks from that aspect, but have full confidence in all the other guys to continue to work like they've been doing and just whoever gets the opportunity is going to step up and make the plays. >> I see this is a semi-personal question for you, but I'm I'm curious how life has changed for you over the last couple of years since being here in Texas. Seems like you're a much more well-known player. You had a really good season last year being in the Pro Bowl. Just kind of a little contract year. So, I'm just curious how life has changed for you over the last couple of years since your success. >> Um I think end of day, nobody's paying you no money, nobody's giving you any accolades if you're not putting the work in and it's not, you know, you're not getting the results either. So, I've been blessed to, you know, have a lot of great coaches that have poured into me throughout my years from San Francisco to Tennessee to obviously coming here, Houston, and the work ethic that I've had and then a lot of blessings from God to be able to put me in the right positions and everything just kind of coming together. You know, I always try to humble myself cuz I know there's so many people in the world that work extremely hard that never get the results. So I just been blessed that the work that I put in and the results have showed for it. So I really couldn't even you know, say much as if it was on me, but just did my part trusted in God. My life is definitely changed for the better, but the mentality that I've had has really been consistent along the whole way. >> Can you tell me about the difference that you've seen as far as leadership is concerned when it comes to players like Kamari and Nelson and Ka'imi and Will and Dameon Pierce. I mean they're still young in their careers, but I mean they have some experience in the league. >> Yeah, 100%. I think the thing that's so funny cuz I mess with those guys all the time. You know, Will already see Will he's like a little big brother. So already we already have our back and forth all the time. And a weird wrinkle that's probably not going to be a huge issue, but something that will need to be ironed out is uh that if Harrison Smith does return, they are going to have to get him under contract. And what that actually costs could be, you know, part of the math here. But before getting into any of that, he did like Flores did also say, you know, hey, I have told him a bunch of times that I want him back. And that's kind of what everybody has said. We have made it very clear how we feel about him, that we really want him back and we would love it and he knows that and then we're going to leave him alone. And to me, they are not talking like people who know what's going to happen and are just like keeping it secret until it's actually real because we don't want anybody to, you know, get we don't want to get out ahead of our skis in case something goes wrong, but we really know what's going to happen and we're just keeping it a secret from you. They're not doing that. They really seem like they don't know. Like they just don't have any idea where this guy's head's at. I don't think anybody does. I think he's like out in the woods and the only two things that know at all what he is thinking are the deer and the hummingbird that he's been talking to for the last two months. Um the we just don't know. So we don't know how to deal with and and then like dealing with that you basically just have to make the assumption that you're not going to get Harrison Smith back. And if you do get Harrison Smith back what a beautiful problem to have. Now we have to figure out what who who we're going to brush to the side so that Harrison, you know, when Harrison Smith wants to come in. Okay, cool. happy with that. Um, I am still of the opinion that Harrison Smith would be wise to hang him up. I don't think that what he does is still like I think he's becoming more and more of a liability. And I think that ages, you know, time is coming for all of us. And so I'm kind of the opinion that if he comes back, I mean, we're not expecting 2018 Harrison Smith. We're not even expecting 2024 Harrison Smith. You know, this is a different guy now. But even whatever we get from 2026 Harrison Smith isn't a net negative, right? Like there still would be some positive there. We just to be realistic about what we would expect him to contribute and then you got to figure out the cap numbers and all that alongside the Brian O'Neal extension and those two things could end up even being related. So uh I will talk to you tomorrow. Plus we got locked on Vikings after dark that happened uh Monday Tuesday night. You can check those out. Tyler Forness subbed in on Tuesday or a little under the weather. He is alive, I promise. Uh we'll do the same thing on Thursday, 10 p.m. Central. Catch us live.
