title: Aaron Glenn OTA Press Conference (6/10) | New York Jets
text: All right. Good morning. >> [clears throat] >> So, since this is the last week of our OTAs, I want to give you guys just some insight on how this week is going to go about. So, yesterday was really an extension of what we did last Thursday, which was a number of reps in the red zone. And that was a good practice for us yesterday. Going to today, today will be heavy heavy special teams. We'll have a walk-through with base down offense and defense, but for the most part special teams will be emphasized today. So, today is one of the days I really like because for the rookies and first-year players, man, this is where they start to get like really understand exactly where their role can be when it comes to special teams. So, that'll be good for those guys. And then tomorrow will be heavy third down day. All right. So, that's how the week will be planned out. When it comes to injuries, no injuries up to date. The only one that I will say that you guys will not see until today will be Cade. And Cade has back tightness, but he'll be fine. He'll be fine. The thing is that since it's special team practice, we want to make sure we just hold him out for the day, and he'll be fine going to to vet mini camp. So, any questions going forward? >> Is it Cade York? >> Say it again. >> Cade York. >> Oh, Cade quarterback Cade. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Got it. Got it. Got it. >> You do have a new kicker, Cade Sanders. Just talk about that for a little bit and just what he brings. >> Yeah. Yeah. Obviously, he did a really good job in in Miami. And I've said this this last time we spoke is anytime we can get a good player that can create competition, we want to bring the player in to be able to create that. So, um those guys will battle it out. Um I'm sure we'll see exactly how far this goes, but um it's just creating competition. >> What happened with Quinton Skinner? I know you guys liked him last year. >> Yeah. Well, Quinton had um he had some injuries and uh at this point we want to make sure that he can get himself healthy and see how that goes going forward. >> Has anyone stood out to you during these sessions? PJ Hall >> What kind of improvement on >> Yeah. Yeah. Here's the hard thing about um about OTAs because the physical part of it is not really a huge part, you know, so uh I would say this. I'd say the mental part um in all three phases like I I've been impressed with our guys have really understanding learning what what the scheme is about. And the one thing that I talk about more than anything is just really understanding the details of the scheme. Understanding the why because once once you understand the why of the scheme, it allows you to make plays within the scheme. So, uh I think the players been on top of that. They've been doing a good job of that. Listen, we still have a ways to go and we understand that. Um but man, we're really the execution, the details and the discipline about what we're doing, that's been the focal point um on every day of what we're what we're trying to create. >> We We haven't We haven't asked you much about it at all is Savion Red Sweat. >> Yeah. >> And I'm wondering how he's coming along. That is one large person right there. >> Yeah. He He's um He's um He's easy to pick out. You know, he's easy to pick out. Uh but he's doing a really good job. Again, he's no different than any other guy that I talk about as far as uh really trying to understand exactly how we do things. Um obviously this is his first year here. Uh but going through phase one uh really focusing in on the the strength conditioning part, then going through phase two where we really uh emphasize strength conditioning, but now he's starting to understand exactly what the scheme uh the details of the scheme and exactly what his job would be. Obviously in phase three, the physical part is not where things that we can actually just emphasize for the most part, but he's doing a really good job and he's starting to understand exactly how he fits in the scheme. Again, another guy that that we know have to has a ways to go, but for the most part I I like exactly where he's at. >> Is his weight where it's supposed to be? >> His weight's where it needs to be. It is. >> And just to follow on that in a larger sense, it seems like you added some big players like him and Darrell Jackson. >> Was there an emphasis in the off season to add size to your front? >> Um It It was. It's a big man's game. It will always be a big man's game. And for us to be able to add large men that has the ability those guys have, the agility those guys have, uh it only makes us better as a team and that's across the board. O-line, D-line, at the linebacker spot where Demario Demario's about 242 lb, something like that. Um even our guys on the edges with JJ and and Osa, those guys are big men. Even Bailey, he's a 255 lb man with with with long arms, so to your point, yes, we we that was an emphasis for for us. But not only big men, but big men that can move. >> Coach, we had we had saw Josh Myers about him a week or two last week saying that he said >> Yeah. He had a chance to be one of the greats. Is that kind of what you're seeing from him this spring as he enters his second year? There's a sense of urgency with him as far as how do I take my game to the next level and >> [snorts] >> um the things I have to do to be able to to be one of the top offensive linemen in this league and a lot of that has to do with the technique part of it, which he's really getting that from his coach. a lot of it has to do with the mentality part of it of everyday, man, I am chopping wood to be the best that I can be. Um and then physically making sure that he's in a he's in shape, physically making sure that he's strong. Uh physically making sure that he's conditioned to be able to play a number of plays. So, all those things he's putting in line to be able to be one of the better O-line players in this league, but um Listen, he's keeping everything in perspective though. To make sure that, man, this is a team game and I want to be good not just for myself, but I want to be good for the team, if that makes sense. >> All right, you you guys drafted tight ends the last 2 years for like pass catches. >> Yep. >> And and you have Jeremy on the on the roster and I know you talked about how you can bring more get more out of him. >> What do you see his role? How do [snorts] you see him progressing? >> It's a little different than than what I talked about last year and he's um he's a versatile player. Um and when I say that, he's a guy that can play in line at the Y tight end. He's a guy that actually we can actually flex out um and use him in pass patterns. Um but I think we have a really good mix when it comes to the tight end room. Somebody that's versatile like he has, then you got Mason um man who's really growing in in that aspect of being versatile. We know what he can do in the passing game. Um then with Sedeeq, we know that he's a he's just a matchup nightmare. So, um I'm happy about that room. I think those guys I think they'll do a good job for us. I'm excited to see how they operate during training camp. >> AG, um Carl Dunbar, he has a history of developing guys into really talented like Zach Line. So, [snorts] I'm curious like what was your relationship like with him before he came here? >> What does he do that he's able to get the most out of? >> So, um I was a scout here when he was coaching here. And this just over time um I call him Dundee, so if you hear me say Dundee, that's what I'm talking about. So over time uh we've met up at the combine a couple of times just to talk D-line play. And I was always intrigued about his um the techniques that he taught. I was always intrigued about the drills that he had. Um I was always intrigued about the mentality that he brought to the position to where uh I knew at some point if I had the opportunity to hire him as as my D-line coach that I would jump at the chance to do it. So um there's no secret to why the guys that he's coached end up playing at a high level. It's because of what he brings to the table and the mentality he has himself. Uh and I think those guys really buy into who he is and that shows on the field for the most part. >> His technique um surely would probably be the first one to say he didn't have a great year last year. >> seen from him this spring and what are your expectations for him in year two with you? >> W- I will say this, it's um it's always good when a person when a player is self-aware. And it's always good when a player is his own toughest critic. and for him to say that and for him to for what I know about what we've talked about for him to do the things that he's been doing this off season to get himself into a position where listen, I want to be one of the top linebackers. It's no different what we just talked about with Membo. Um the way these dudes are going about their business in all three phases has been unbelievable for the most part and listen, I'm going to support that player. Um I'm going to continue to help that player. Um even when you have a down year, man, you try to look at the things that that like what can I do to pick myself up? And I think with DeMario being next to him, that's going to help him out a lot cuz he's still a young player. And he is a player that came from being a safety to being a linebacker. So, having somebody that's been in this league for a long time as DeMario sitting right beside him, it can only help him. So, um any player that's self-aware and will critique themselves that on the year-to-year basis always good. >> Hey, coach. How has Braelon Allen looked, you know, coming off the Yeah. Yeah, that's um to see him out there to see him run around, to see a big man that's as agile, uh that obviously you know you can use him in the run game, but to be able to use him in the passing game, um that was the vision, you know, with him, Breece, and Isaiah last year. And obviously that didn't come to fruition. So, um man, I'm just looking forward to seeing him get out in camp and uh and and be a part of that that three-headed monster I call them um as far as running back. So, um it's good to see him moving around. Um obviously we hate to see him go down with the injury, but man, it's um it's good to see him out there with us. >> Hey, coach. It seems like this time of year doesn't translate quite as well for the line of scrimmage players as it does for DBs or receivers. For a player like David Bailey, what can you tell about what he's done so far and how he's growing and what can you not tell? >> Yeah. Yeah. It it the the first-step quickness is something that pops off the tape like immediately. obviously you already said the physical part of you you you just can't get um as much as you want in that aspect, but uh you do see the hand usage. You do see the the moves that he's trying to create. And this is the time when you want to work on some things that, you know, you might not feel as comfortable with. Uh this is time to work on those things. So, he is he's working on some of his weaknesses, uh but you do see the strong points of what he has and um and I don't ever want him to lose sight of that. You know, of of of the things that we know that he can do, but um this is the time to work on things that you want to get better at, and that's what we're focused on with him is, man, let's make sure we use that that that speed rush that you have, but also understand that you can rush with power, and you have a spin move that can be pretty deadly um in his arsenal. >> Thank you, everyone. >> All good. >> Thank you.

title: Kaden Elliss on OTA practices, upcoming minicamp | New Orleans Saints
text: Caden, I guess let's let's talk uh first of all, OTAs last week, wrapping it up here. How's it been going so far? >> Uh it's been fun. Uh good to get with the guys and coaches and I'll get on the field and play uh at least a little bit of football out there. >> How How's it been for you, you know, being back in in New Orleans, you know, for the first time? >> It's been a lot of fun. It's been special. Um really excited to be back. Really excited to have the gold back on and get to go out there and and play some ball with these guys. >> What What did you learn about the organization the the first time uh back in New Orleans here? >> Uh the first time I was here? >> Yeah. >> Uh it's just well-run. Um you know, Mickey and Spencer and like all of them do a really good job from top to bottom. Um and it permeates obviously. I wasn't sure uh fully what the culture would be like without Sean. Um but I've been uh you know, more than impressed and I really thankful to how Kellen um has uh really built a a special culture here that I think's ready to take off. >> So So when you signed here, the Saints were your first team you said, "Yeah, I'm going back." >> [laughter] >> Not in a negative way. You just didn't think like that just happens so rarely, you know? Um so uh for it to happen like it you didn't think it was going to. Um and then all of a sudden calls go the way they they go and all of a sudden it's like, "Hey, might be New Orleans." And then uh all of a sudden when you do realize it's a possibility um the thankfulness for uh something familiar, uh the thankfulness for such an awesome city and and well-run organization um permeated the the entire thoughts from there. >> I'm sure you've been asked this question many a time, but the linebacker room is a little bit different this time. There's There's no Demario Davis. I'm sure you learned a lot from him. >> Yeah, I learned a lot from him. He's uh you know, like big brother of the league. He uh um feel like he takes kind of everybody he has under his wing. Um and I was no different. So, to be able to learn behind him for uh for all those years was really special. To get to play beside him was really special. Um now I get to uh come back and and also uh you know, come come be me is is special as well. >> As we wrap up OTAs here and then you got mini camp, what do you want to accomplish here in the next week and then little time off for training camp? >> Yeah, for me it's really I guess building relationship, earning the trust of the guys around me. Um I think the the special teams, everybody that's been on a special team, you can attest to the camaraderie that you guys had. So, right now for me it's it's trying to build that as best I can with the guys in this locker room, earn the trust on that field and then all of a sudden training camp comes, preseason, season. We're five steps ahead of someone that that just started off, so that's what I'm trying to do.

title: Kellen Moore talks Saints OTAs Day 7 | New Orleans Saints
text: All right, guys. Um, third down day today. We'll be outside uh nice and warm and uh should be a really fun day. So, we've had a good week so far. Had a practice on Monday. Monday we had a little team activity/competition with bow fishing which was a ton of fun um for a lot of guys. For myself, first time going south for a fishing excursion. So, that was a lot of fun. And no surprise, Brian Young was the uh top uh fisherman and Oscar Delp had the biggest fish. So, those are some highlights. So, I'll open up for questions. >> Is today the last is today the last day or tomorrow? >> Four >> for the OTAAS. >> Uh, tomorrow will be the last day of OTAAS and then next weekend will be our uh veteran mini camp. >> What have you kind of learned about this team so far? >> Competitive, connected. I think those are the two things we've just spent a lot of time on and uh these guys have put a ton of work in and um to see the attendance we've had each and every day and the investment these guys have put into it has been awesome. >> Speaking of uh Del, how's he doing? when we noticed he was observing last week. >> Yeah, doing well. Doing well. Just uh had a little hamstring thing pop up uh you know the other day in practice and he's been doing well though. >> Do you expect him back on the field today? >> I think he'll do something at today at some point. Yeah. >> Any attendance of that? >> Uh I'm guessing uh probably no Shep, no Alvin, no CO today just based off of meetings today. So >> we talked to you last week obviously before practice. Alvin said he talked to you at practice. How would you say that relationship and that situation with Alvin stands right now? >> Yeah, good. I love Alvin. Um it was good to see him and u you know obviously uh it was it was a great opportunity to spend a little bit of time with him. Anticipate veteran mini camp seeing him uh next week and so uh it'll be good to see him again. >> Would you say you expect him to be part of your team this season? >> Yeah, I think that's how you always prepare. you know, he's on he's on the roster and we're excited about him and keep preparing the right way and I'm excited to get him into the fold with uh Travis and um I think he'll be a great opportunity. >> Does his contract still need to be addressed or anything like through the process or >> I think that's a fair discussion on the business side for for him and uh Mickey at times, but uh you know that'll be taken care of and our job is to prepare for for football. >> Was he here at all this week or did he leave after we saw him at the open practice last? >> Um he was not. It was the day that he was here last week though. Was it just the one day or did he stay for? >> Yeah, he was here for that day. Yeah. >> Is Chris dealing with anything? >> Um I mean he hasn't been able to do the team activities obviously throughout OTAAS and so uh he's not here today. I mean we'll uh we'll check in on that but uh you know he's done a ton of work this offseason and so you know he'll be in a good place. >> Is that injury related or related to blood clot? >> Um the blood was blood clot was related to just not participating in the team and some of those things. I get your thoughts on third year players. They have their rookie season in second year and third year. Is that a pretty good gauge for you, you know, after the third year to see, hey, you know, he's pretty fluid and and you start thinking about maybe sec, you know, second contract is that third year. >> Yeah, I think that's a fair assessment. You know, when you're in your coming into your third year, your rookie year, there's a lot. You basically play two seasons in one. you go right from your college season right into the NFL season. The second year, I think, is always a big jump for these guys just because it's their first time having a full NFL off seasonason and they can kind of find their rhythm and routine. Certainly that third year, it's kind of you're transitioning to more of a veteran status. You should know the expectations, know the roles, and u you obviously there's a business component of that. Once you're entering your third year, we all we all know where these contracts go. And so, um, you know, we got a lot of guys who've earned their opportunity to play early and they're kind of in a really good spot right now to keep going. >> Two starting quarters from the end of last year, both really young guys for second last year. Um, what did you see from them in that kind of closing stretch that that made you kind of comfortable going into it with them still in those roles? >> I think just the confidence that showed up and then as a result the steadiness. Um, you know, I thought our back end just did an excellent job throughout the season as it progressed. Um, you can look at our third down numbers, the way our third downs were handled. Um, the explosive plays. I think those things are credit to the way our back end was playing, playing at a really high level, communicating at a high level. And you just saw the confidence growing. And I think even out here in OTAAS, you can see these guys confidence. U, I think our guys have a lot of confidence in the scheme, but also what they're doing individually. >> And with Kool-Aid in particular, um, is confidence a big part of his game? like in and you obviously just mentioned it. Did you see that grow as you kind of got more kind of time on tap? >> Yeah, I think you can definitely see the confidence. Uh corner is a hard position. You play some really hard downs in this league in the NFL and uh you play against these premier receivers and uh the guys that are really special are obviously really talented, but they also can respond to plays that don't go their way because inevitably there will be a play that doesn't go your way. And the way these guys can quickly respond, I think, you know, Kool-Aid and Quincy are great examples of those guys that if something happens and doesn't go their way, they just hop right in. They just keep going. >> What What have you liked about Travis Han getting to work with him, see him, see the way you can use him and things like that. >> Yeah, I love his work ethic. Love what he's put into this entire off seasonason. I mean, he's here every day just training, doing everything he can. I think the cool thing is um he's a really smart player. we've seen the explosiveness, but because of his smarts and his football IQ, I think he's, you know, truly any down, every down, um, he can play a really valuable role in that situation where you're not rotating as much. And so, um, you know, I'm excited. Obviously, running backs are a little bit of a challenge assessment right now just because the run game is fairly limited uh, to walk through and, you know, a couple team things here and there. So, u, I'm excited for him, though, but he's he's done an awesome job. I know there could be a tendency to think running backs can be plugged into any system that that a team wants to run, but like knowing the system you guys wanted to run this year and then going out and targeting him, what what fits best that >> Yeah, I I think if you look at his exposure, you know, certainly what he ran last year uh with Liam there, I thought he did a phenomenal job in that system. And so, um I think there's some similarities, you know, from from what he was asked to do and from a run game perspective. I think his suddenness, his one cut, his vision uh shows up and then you know the pass game components you know that he was able to utilize there uh will certainly continue to utilize. We've used that historically. Obviously we know the running backs who we've been a part of other places but also here. So uh I think it fits in really well. >> How big is bringing a guy in like that for Tyler's development? Like what what are some of the biggest benefits for a second quarterback to bring in a weapon like that? Yeah, when you have the threat of the run game, obviously it's it's extremely valuable. And so, um, you know, there's times where you're going to want to run the ball and just run it. And then at times, at least having the threat and the potential of the run game, you know, creates those play action opportunities. And, uh, you know, forces defense to at least play in a little bit more conflicting situations. And, uh, Travis's done a great job and, you know, I think he's, you know, steadily improved each and every year in the NFL and you've seen that and certainly last year is a really good of indication of where he's going when he's healthy. Coach, after years of being an assistant, what were your biggest takeaways of being a head coach for the first time? Anything that surprised you, you learned or interesting to share? >> It's a good question. I think uh you know, time management becomes important. Uh you know, trusting trusting guys to kind of uh you know, we have a really awesome staff and sometimes, you know, building that trust and just, you know, letting guys do their job I think is a a really important part of this. you know, we we've got an awesome staff and, you know, they're more than qualified to handle a lot of the obligations and I think that's that's been something you get more and more comfortable with as you go and uh once we've kind of created our rhythm and expectations, I think it's been really good. >> Whether you win or lose, it seems like your demeanor stays the same. Is it important for a leader to maintain that kind of composure? >> Yeah, I think consistency is important. Obviously, uh, hey, we all have emotions. I have highs, I have lows. Uh, but the team doesn't always need to see those. And I think that's an important part of it. And um the NFL season, no matter how talented of a season or successful a season you have, there's going to be good moments. There's going to be, you know, moments you got to navigate. And so you can look at even all these teams that win Super Bowls each and every year. Um they all have a tough stretch at some point. And so you got to navigate that the right way. >> What you guys did tight end, um was getting that position um or is that position more of a priority for you like just getting more involved in the offense? I think it's a fair assessment just looking at what we've done. Obviously tried to hire sign Noah last year and uh yeah, timing wasn't right. We're able to acquire him this year which was awesome. Uh Oscar was a fun surprise in the draft just being available at that that status or situation. And so uh and then we got some young guys that we had last year on the back end that we thought really took strides through their development through the season. And so um I think it's a great group. Exciting to see that group just expand those roles. And I think that's what's training camp's gonna be all about. >> What the Rams did with like 13 personnel and hear about teams trying to copy them. How can you tell if like a trend is worth pursuing as a trend versus like uh everyone else is doing it, but what was that? >> Yeah, it's a great question. I can talk about that for a long time. I mean, the trends are important in this league and we're always trying to find, you know, edges and opportunities for your football team. And so, you're naturally going to look at the teams that have the most success in this league. Um, you know, you have to match ultimately these things with your personnel and make sure it fits them. And so, um, multiple tight ends obviously has increased in this league. It's certainly something that everyone's probably going down the same road. Um, you got to make sure it becomes a valuable thing because, um, you know, LA is a great example and the 13, it was a really successful thing for them. There's other teams last year who really dug into 13 personnel wasn't as successful and, you know, everyone's kind of leaning in the Rams theory. Well, there's plenty of other teams that try to go down that road and it maybe was, you know, the EPA, those plays aren't necessarily pretty. So, uh, you got to understand the why and make sure it all connects. >> How how do you feel like you've like evolved as a play caller? Like, where are some of the things that like as you look back, make you better, make you grow, make you make you think and change? >> Yeah. Um, every place is a different environment, different situation. And I think I've always really enjoyed trying to build a system around um what our roster looks like and what our quarterback certainly plays like. And so um you know certainly going from Dallas to LA to Philly, three very different styles. Um you know, from a pass game, run game. And then from a system standpoint, I think this offseason was a really important one for us to really clean it all up and really identify and narrow our focus from an offense perspective. Um, you know, there's a lot of plays you can run in this in this world and uh they're all good. You know, there's plenty of good stuff, but we really got to narrow and get good at certain things that we feel really confident about and then have the presentation and the design and the versatility on our roster to be able to continue to evolve that as a season goes. >> Last year, you talked about how it was going to be a little bit of a blend of all of those Yeah. >> different places that you've been. Is that still the way that you view it this year, or have you sort of now started to hone in more on maybe something different? Yeah, I think you know those are all exposures. I think really the focus now is you know building a system around these guys and feel like we got a great group of guys. We got really versatile players who can do a number of things and so I think that's going to be a benefit to us and you know now is really the focus is you know we're finishing up kind of this core installation of core concepts and core systems that we believe in and then it's about taking that through the summer and into training camp and we're not going back to step one. We just got to keep building and that's a really important aspect of this. Is Jordan Tyson still kind of the same? >> Yeah, you won't see much difference now. >> Same. Yeah. >> The point of taking some pressure off of Tyler as a former quarterback, where do you kind of land on like is that something that you had to learn? Do you naturally want to, you know, call shots for Tyler or to the pass game or have you always felt that maybe it's better to take the ball out of his hand sometimes? Yeah, I think I think it really comes down to every week's a different battle, a different game plan, and you just have to have the versatility to play different styles through a season. Um maybe a game that Tyler has to throw it 50 times or maybe a game we got to run it 50 times. I mean, whatever in between those two, you know, variables. And so, I think it's important that you can play different styles because every matchup's different. Every defense has their strengths and has their things you want to attack. title: Saints CB Kool-Aid McKinstry on stepping into a leadership role, improving as a defense
text: As a squad, as a team, with the coaching staff, we're doing a good job of connecting, building a brotherhood, building chemistry with one another, and it's bringing us together. I feel like the locker room have more energy than it has since I've been here, for sure. >> Quincy talked about your your confidence and your comfortability. How do you translate that from last year to this year and build on that? >> Oh man, I feel like rule number one is growth. So, you know, coming into this year, I definitely want to show growth. I definitely want to show my maturity year in and year out as a player and mentally as a leader. >> And all different types of ways, for sure. >> What do you think you What do you think are the biggest strides from last year to this year? >> Um I'll say first, um just, you know, being a leader. And um not just being a leader with my position group or with the secondary or with just even with the defense, just, you know, being a leader like all the way around um with the team. Um also, just, you know, just being here for these guys in any type way I can, just, you know, inviting them to the house, just finding different ways that we can make that we can connect because that's something that the coaches have been harping on. So, you know, just >> Yeah, right there. You and Quincy, how have y'all been kind of building off each other, feeding off each other? >> Um me and me and Quincy, man, we like best friends, man. We hang out. We hang out together. We eat together. Um we kind of do everything together. We talk every day. Um I send him plays, he send me plays. Like, "Hey, if you'd have played this play like this, it would have So, you know, me and him got that bond that, you know, we we looking at each other to feed off each other to definitely make plays and bring energy to the team. >> [laughter] >> Yeah, just having walked in here, so much has that kind of been, you know, I know it doesn't get you wish you guys could play together. And I know he's one of your closest guys on the team here. Kind of how's How's that it's just been being in that kind of giving this side of the net spot? How you guys doing so far? >> Oh man, first I'll say I'm going to say he's a great player, man. That's Slot Roll. He knows this thing, man. He works hard, and that's how he got to the position that he's in right now, you know. Yeah, we got safety on him. He's a young player. He's very athletic, and I feel like, you know, we got him there because we feel like he can learn this spot. We feel like he's a guy that can, you know, step into this role and do what he needs to do. So, you know, my job is to play. So, if coach got the confidence in him to put him in the game right there, I'm going to have the same confidence and make sure I'm behind him in the same exact way. >> I know it's a it's kind of a weird question, but just that second year under, you know, Brandon Staley's defensive scheme, do you feel like just because you guys are now a little bit more familiar, kind of knowing where each piece is going, how kind of you want to run that thing, do you feel like now like this defense can make another step in front of what you guys did last year? >> Um yes, definitely. Um towards the end of the year, I feel like we was one of the best defenses in the league, and I feel like um we still have growth, and we know we still can grow as players, and we still can grow from things that teams are trying to do with us based off any scheme, you know what I'm saying? So, um I feel like coming into this year, um as me, Derwin, Drue Tranquill, um Q, we'd be back there talking and going over things, and it's kind of like we're so connected, it's kind of like I've been playing with these guys for a minute. Like I like I've been here with them long enough to say too much. Like we're already on the same page, and we don't have to make too many signals to say too many words. It's just lucky and >> Is that also cool just the versatility of how guys can play different you know like you can move different pieces in this defense? >> I feel like as a as a defensive back, that's why they say "Get the best you got to be able to move and play different roles and be able to make yourself valuable by being able to move into different roles, you know?" So, um you can't just be a corner, you can't just be a safety. You know, you got to be able to move. >> Cor uh shout out to the Alabama baseball team. >> Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, I seen them. Um well, it's crazy. I just was watching them on the TV like maybe Monday. They played Monday? Yeah, so yeah, I watched them on Monday and I was trying to figure it out. I'm not really a baseball fan, a baseball guy. So, I seen them win and celebrated jumping the crowd and stuff. I did get to witness that, but I don't I don't know where they going or if it's a championship now or any of that. Yeah, but salute to those guys. >> Just going into your three, do you do you put pressure on yourself to be a more vocal leader? Like is that something that a role that you feel comfortable stepping into? Like what does that look like for you? >> Um yeah, I feel like I'm I'm definitely comfortable in being a leader. Like I said, I was around Coach Saban for years and I feel like he's one of the ultimate leaders and I was around this guy so I feel like I picked up a lot of leadership qualities and I'm kind of a vocal leader. I'm kind of a lead by example type guy so I fit right into that role, man. It's I feel like it's not too big for me. Like I said, I want to be a leader for the whole team, man. With the O-line, you know, O-line players can come talk to me, not just be a defensive guy. >> And with so many young players, is that is that kind of a cool feeling to know, you know, this group, this kind of core group is is leading this team, kind of bit into the new uh future, if you will? >> Um yeah, man. I feel like as young guys, man, all we got to do is keep leading by example, keep making plays and keep doing things the right way. And I feel like everything will take care of itself. >> How would you Sorry, you probably got this already. How would you describe your confidence in year three heading into your third year? >> Oh man, I feel like confidence is number one at corner. I feel like I'm right where I need to be. With the confidence side thing, man, I feel like I'm locked in. I've seen a lot. I've been around this game a lot. Diving into film with coaches, just trying to fill out little kinks about different little things. So I feel like, you know, I'm I'm ready to see some new things, you know what I'm saying? Like if I've seen a lot so I feel like I'm right where I need to be confidence-wise. >> How do you feel like you you finished last year? Like the second half of the season it seemed like everything really kind of came together and like you feel like you just been leveling up like >> Yeah, definitely. I definitely feel like I've been leveling up, man. You know, I feel like I've been I've been training hard, been working my ass off in my off-season and you know, just going back into the film, watching my good and my bad plays, learning from those and you know, making sure that I don't make the same mistake twice. You know what I'm saying? That's kind of been my focus point. Just, you know, just trying to grow, man. Growth has definitely been number one. And I say definitely going into a new year, growth is something that the coaches want to see. It's something that everyone want to see. It's something that I definitely want to see within myself so, you know, growth is definitely a major thing. >> What what's been the biggest change for you? Just like off the field, with the preparation and review and and all that stuff. >> Uh, you know, just you know, just growing up, man. I would say, you know, just doing all the small things. All the things that you hear as a rookie. All the things you hear going into your two that you should be, you know what I'm saying, and what you shouldn't do as a player. Just living right, basically. Just, you know, just going to get in the hot tub. Going to get in the cold tub. Just doing everything in my body. Just staying after for treatment. Just doing little things where I feel like it'll make me a better >> person, better player. >> Do you feel like it's paying off? Like last week we were out here, looked like you had two pass breakups. Today you guys are clamping down and stuff like that. Like you feel the work like right now like paying dividends? >> Yeah, I definitely feel my work paying uh paying dividends, so, you know, I'm a challenge with myself. I like to challenge myself, and my challenge is to keep on working. Like never get too comfortable with myself. Never get too too satisfied with where I'm at now, you know, cuz I feel like I'm still I still got a ceiling to reach. I feel like I still got a high ceiling, so, you know, I'm just trying to get to where I need to be for for this team. >> How close are you to the to the ceiling? >> I don't know. Um, only God knows that. All I can do is keep my head down and work, you know, and just whenever I get there, I'll know, you know what I'm saying? And hopefully I can keep growing growing growing till year 15 or however, you know what I'm saying? So, you know, the ceiling is there. My job is to keep my head down till I'm there.

text: nice and warm and uh should be a really fun day. So, we've had a good week so far. Had a practice on Monday. Does his contract still need to be addressed or anything like that through the process or >> I think that's a fair discussion on the business side for for him and uh Mickey at times, but uh you know that'll be taken care of and our job is to prepare for for football. >> Was he here at all this week or did he leave after we saw him at the open practice last? >> Um he was not. >> It was the day that he was here last week though. Was it just the one day or did he stay? >> Yeah, he was here for that day. Yeah. >> Is Chris still dealing with anything? Um, I mean, he hasn't been able to do the team activities obviously throughout OTAAS and so, uh, he's not here today. I mean, we'll, uh, we'll check in on that, but, uh, you know, he's done a ton of work this off seasonason and so, you know, he'll be in a good place. >> Is that injury related or related to blood clot? >> Um, the blood was blood clot was related to just not participating in team and some of those things. Yeah. >> Thoughts on thirdyear players, they had their rookie season in second year and third year. Is that a pretty good gauge for you, you know, after the third year to see, hey, you know, he's pretty good and you started thinking about maybe second, you know, second contract. Is that third year? >> Yeah, I think that's a fair assessment. You know, when you're in your coming into your third year, your rookie year, there's a lot. You basically play two seasons in one. You go right from your college season right into the NFL season. The second year I think is always a big jump for these guys just because it's their first time having a full NFL off seasonason and they can kind of find their rhythm and routine. Certainly that third year it's kind of you're transitioning to more of a veteran status. You should know the expectations, know the roles and um you know obviously there's a business component of that once you're entering your third year. We know we all know where these contracts go and so um you know we got a lot of guys who've earned their opportunity to play early and they're kind of in a really good spot right now to keep going. the two starting quarters from the end of last year, both really young guys for second last year. Um, what did you see from them in that kind of closing stretch that made you kind of comfortable going into it, but again, I'm still in those roles? >> I think just the confidence that showed up and then as a result, the steadiness. Um, you know, I thought our back end just did an excellent job throughout the season as it progressed. Um, you can look at our third down numbers, the way our third downs were handled. Um the explosive plays, I think those things are credit to the way our back end is playing, playing at a really high level, communicating at a high level, and you just saw the confidence growing. And I think even out here in OTAAS, you can see these guys confidence. Um I think our guys have a lot of confidence in the scheme, but also what they're doing individually. >> And with Kool-Aid in particular, um is confidence a big part of his game and like in you obviously just mentioned, did you see that grow as he kind of got more kind of time on task for us? Yeah, I think you can definitely see the confidence. Uh corner is a hard position. You play some really hard downs in this league in the NFL and uh you play against these premier receivers and uh the guys that are really special are obviously really talented, but they also can respond to plays that don't go their way because inevitably there will be a play that doesn't go your way. And the way these guys can quickly respond, I think, you know, Kool-Aid and Quincy are great examples of those guys that if something happens and doesn't go their way, they just hop right in. They just keep going. What have what have you liked about Travis Han getting to work with him, see him, see the way you can use him and things like that? >> Yeah, I love his work ethic. Love what he's put into this entire offseason. I mean, he's here every day just training, doing everything he can. I think the cool thing is um he's a really smart player. We've seen the explosiveness, but because of his smarts and his football IQ, I think he's, you know, truly any down, every down um he can play a really valuable role in that situation where you're not rotating as much. And so, um, you know, I'm excited. Obviously, running backs are a little bit of a challenge assessment right now just cuz the run game is fairly limited, uh, to walk through and, you know, a couple team things here and there. So, uh, I'm excited for him, though. But, he's he's done an awesome job. I know there could be a tendency to think running backs can be plugged into any system that that a team wants to run, but like knowing the system you guys wanted to run this year and then going out and targeting him what what fits best that >> Yeah, I I think if you look at his exposure, you know, certainly what he ran last year uh with Liam there, I thought he did a phenomenal job in that system. And so, um I think there's some similarities, you know, from from what he was asked to do and from a run game perspective. I think his suddeness, his one cut, his vision uh shows up and then you know the pass game components you know that he was able to utilize there uh will certainly continue to utilize. We've used that historically. Obviously we know the running backs who we've been a part of other places but also here. So uh I think it fits in really well. >> How big is bringing a guy in like that for Tyler's development? Like what what are some of the biggest benefits for a secondyear quarterback to bring in a weapon like that? Yeah, when you have the threat of the run game, obviously it's it's extremely valuable. And so, um, you know, there's times where you're going to want to run the ball and just run it. And then at times, at least having the threat and the potential of the run game, you know, creates those play action opportunities. And, um, you know, forces defense to at least play in a little bit more conflicting situations. And uh Travis's done a great job and you know I think he's you know steadily improved each and every year in the NFL and you've seen that and certainly last year is a really good of indication of where he's going when he's healthy. >> Coach, after years of being an assistant, [snorts] what were your biggest takeaways being a head coach for the first time? Anything that surprised you or you learned or interesting to share? >> It's a good question. I think uh you know time management becomes important. uh you know trusting trusting guys to kind of uh you know we have a really awesome staff and sometimes you know building that trust and just you know letting guys do their job I think is u a really important part of this. You know we we've got an awesome staff and you know they're [clears throat] more than qualified to handle a lot of the obligations and I think that's that's been something you get more and more comfortable with as you go and uh once we've kind of created our rhythm and expectations I think it's been really good. >> Whether you win or lose it seems like your demeanor stays the same. Is it important for a leader to maintain that kind of composure? >> Yeah, I think consistency is important. Obviously, uh, hey, we all have emotions. I have highs, I have lows. Uh, but the team doesn't always need to see those. And I think that's an important part of it. And, um, the NFL season, no matter how talented of a season or successful a season you have, there's going to be good moments. There's going to be, you know, moments you got to navigate. And so, you can look at even all these teams that win Super Bowls each and every year, um, they all have a tough stretch at some point. And so, you got to navigate that the right way. with what you guys did at tight end. Um, was getting that position um or is that position more of a priority for you like just getting more involved in the offense? >> I think it's a fair assessment just looking at what we've done. Obviously tried to hire sign Noah last year and uh yeah, timing wasn't right. We're able to acquire him this year which was awesome. Uh Oscar was a fun surprise in the draft just being available at that that status or situation. And so, uh, and then we got some young guys that we had last year on the back end that we thought really took strides through their development through the season. And so, um, I think it's a great group. Exciting to see that group just expand those roles. And I think that's what's training camp's going to be all about >> what the Rams did with like 13 personnel and hear about teams trying to copy them. How can you tell if like a trend is worth pursuing as a trend versus like, uh, everyone else is doing it, but what was that? >> Yeah, it's a great question. and I can talk about that for a long time. I mean, the the trends are important in this league and we're always trying to find, you know, edges and opportunities for your football team. And so, you're naturally going to look at the teams that have the most success in this league. Um, you know, you have to match ultimately these things with your personnel and make sure it fits them. And so, um, multiple tight ends obviously has increased in this league. It's certainly something that everyone's probably going down the same road. Um, you got to make sure it becomes a valuable thing because, um, you know, LA is a great example on the 13, it was a really successful thing for them. There's other teams last year who really dug into 13 personnel wasn't as successful and, you know, everyone's kind of leaning in the Rams theory. Well, there's plenty of other teams that try to go down that road and it maybe was, you know, the EPA, those plays aren't necessarily pretty. So, uh, you got to understand the why and make sure it all connects. >> How do you how do you feel like you've like evolved as a play caller? like what are some of the things that like as you look back make you better make you grow make you make you think and change and >> yeah um every place is a different environment different situation and I think I've always really enjoyed trying to build a system around um what our roster looks like and what our quarterback certainly plays like and so um you know certainly going from Dallas to LA to Philly three very different styles um you know from a pass game run game and then from a system standpoint I think this offseason was a really important one for us to really clean it all up and really identify and narrow our focus from an offensive perspective. Um, you know, there's a lot of plays you can run in this in this world and uh they're all good. You know, there's plenty of good stuff, but we really got to narrow and get good at certain things that we feel really confident about and then have the presentation and the design and the versatility on our roster to be able to continue to evolve that as a season goes. >> Last year, you talked about how it was going to be a little bit of a blend of all of those Yeah. >> different places that you've been. Is that still the way that you view it this year or have you sort of now started to hone in more on maybe something different? >> Yeah, I think you know those are all exposures. I think really the focus now is you know building a system around these guys and feel like we got a great group of guys. We got really versatile players who can do a number of things. And so I think that's going to be a benefit to us.
