And now you as a young guy, you're trying to tell these grown men kind of how to operate and you got to kind of be a certain certain kind of way. You gotta be a standup guy and you got to be able to demand certain things. And you know, for a rookie, that's that's hard sometimes. And there are guys that have done it. I've coached rookies that have done it. But it takes a lot. And so you have to show up and keep your mouth shut early and and earn the respect. And once you got the respect, you can kind of kind of guide guys and get guys to do the things you need them to do. >> Yeah. KT KT is a smart uh KT is a smart person and he he knows a lot about the world. So we have we have some uh we have some great conversations, you know, and as long as the football is the football and we're we're meeting what we have to there, I I I like it. It's good conversation for sure. How much has he grown in the time that you're here just as a person and as a leader? >> Kavon. >> Yes, >> man. A lot. Um I will say though the since the day I've got here um you know his the the way he's worked has always been really strong. Um and he's he his play speed and effort has been uh by far the best of the group this offseason. I mean he just that's just how he plays. um you know looking at his film um when I had got here you know I didn't I wouldn't have said that I wouldn't have thought that about him as a player just he was a young player and there was some consistency areas that he could improve in um so when I you know got to meet him and started working with him I was just blown away at how hard um and how intentional he does work. Um and that's been the same for you know two going on three years that you know that I've been here with him and it's it's a joy to be around because he brings it every day. He mentioned it was sort of like a wing style defense and he had success right that that one year double digit sacks and that. >> How much is it similar to that and like why do you think maybe that could be advantageous to him? >> Well, he's been there the the Baltimore roots obviously were we're in Wink's defense. I wasn't with it but just it is what it is. And then obviously here so familiarity will help him. He does have familiarity with some of the the verbiage and and things that exist in the systems. Um, but I think sacks are a funny thing, man. You know, like he he did have a great year. I look at the quality of the rushes, whether it's a sack or not, you know, and um, you know, sometimes you have big years and and sometimes you don't, you know, so I I don't I wouldn't say that that was necessarily a system thing. I wasn't here for it, so I'm not attached to it. I don't know. Um, but, you know, I I just think he he had a good year and was playing good defense and he's been playing good defense. So, you know, where those numbers go this year, we'll see. Um, >> you know, but I'm just I just I just think the way he's been working and playing, you know, that stuff will take care of itself. >> Arell Arell is not in your room. Right. Right. >> Arll, but he looks like he should be. Like Burn said, they all look like us. You know what I mean? Um, can you see or do you, you know, when there's any pass rush opportunities? Do you work with him or see what he might be able to offer? >> Yeah, for sure. Um, just right away, obviously, you see the physical traits, the length, the strength, and all that. Um, and the little bit that he has pass rushed, you know, I I just he or even looking at his college film, his mindset is right. You know, I always say if you can't win with power, you can't win consistently at any level of football. We have, you know, in our room, you know, which I know we have the the the three players that get a lot of the notoriety, but I I consider our room to be a sevenheaded dragon with everyone that's in there, right? But whatever skill set you're looking at, we have a lot in that room, but the the the three frontline guys are are, you know, by and large athletic rushers. But it's no different for them. They have to rush with power in order to have consistent success. And sometimes for guys with movement traits, that can be a challenge. Like they're chasing edges. They want to throw moves and they think pass rushing is just throwing moves and winning on the edge and venting the corner and turning the corn. But the tackles are too good at this level. They can just set hold their hands and wait for you to take the edge and wash you up the field. So if you never, you know, you know, put a put a post in the fence, so to speak, you know, they're they're they're just going to play for that. Arll naturally is a power rusher and he has the length and strength to do that. So I think you know as his role expands and he gets more rush opportunities because his mentality is the right way as a starting point you know the sky's is the limit for him. >> How does how does Brian Burns not take Brian Burns for granted and how does this team and this coaching >> I think it's because >> he's a great he's a great player. It could be an easy thing to do, but I think it's a testament to him. You don't take Burns for granted because you you feel him and you feel his greatness every day. I mean, the guy has been a great player. He's going on year eight, but he comes out every day, whether it's meetings or practice, >> puts the work in, engages teammates, coaches, participates in meetings, asks questions, works his ass off on the field. So, you you it's a testament to him. You feel him. He he he is a he is a pro. He is a leader. So every day you you you can appreciate how great he is because he operates like that which is you know all great players don't have that mode of operation but but he does and it's we don't take it for granted because it's so obvious on a daily basis. >> What's this group for you? >> You know they um from the day we got here they've been excellent. Uh like the buyin, the attendance um the want to you know they want to be coached hard. They want to do the right thing. Uh it's a great group of guys. I tell them like I love the room in the sense of it's a mix of young guys, old guys, guys that have played a lot of ball, guys that maybe haven't played a lot of ball, but they all want each other to do well. Like there's competition, but they're all cheering for each other and if you guys have been at some practices, you see the excitement from the DBs like the ball. So, it it's been good. It's been a really good room and uh excited to coach them. >> How do you divvy up the responsibilities between you guys? I mean, is it kind of on a daily basis? >> Uh, no, it's it's all hands- on deck. we all meet together. Um, so, uh, all the DBs are hearing the same thing. The corners are hearing what the safeties are being taught. The Nickels are hearing what the corners are being taught, vice versa, because we are a flexible defense in the sense of safeties are going to play nickels, corners are going to play nickels, nickels can play safety. Um, so it it's all of us. Um, I deal mainly with the safeties and the nickels. Addison handles the corners, you know, we're on the grass and everything, but we do do a lot together because of the way our defense is wired. Gota. >> How do you size up that uh competition opposite Pollson? >> You know, it's been good. All of those guys um all of those corners opposite Pollson have have done a good job. You know, since Hood's got here, he's came in eager. We spent a lot of time with them obviously in the draft prep of uh just getting to know who he was and who he is and what kind of player he is. So, since he's got here, he's been the guy that that we thought he was going to be. And then Tay's taken a ton of strides. And then Newsome, you know, we signed him for a reason. Obviously, the tape speaks for itself on what he's done in this league. So, it's good. And in this in this league, you can't have enough corners. So, as many as we can have, that's as many as we want that are good. So, it's been good. It's been a healthy competition for all those guys. >> Do you think that has the traits to start as a rookie? >> I do. I do. You know, we um we take it one day at a time, but you know, what he put on tape in college and since he's gotten here, um you know, he has that makeup in him. And the beautiful thing about Hood is his mind is wired the right way, too. Like he knows what it's going to take. Uh he knows he's got to stack days, stack reps and things like that. But the makeup's there. And you know, um that's why he's playing at this level. >> Yeah. Where would you like to see him in particular polish his game a little bit in camp before you say he's the guy? >> Yeah. Yeah. You know, um there's a lot every all of those guys, everyone's working on a lot. Um right now he's strong. You got to learn how to play strong. And I think it's the strength of the wide outs that he's going against. And we have some veteran guys, especially as of late, that we just signed that are more savvy and know kind of the tricks of the trade. And so as he gets reps and gets more comfortable, I think that's going to come with it for him. But he's starting to pick it up. He's he's a fast learner. >> Odell got him twice on that yesterday. >> Yeah. Yeah. He got him with hoods, hand placement, got him in trouble one time. So things like that is is what he is learning. Yeah. where Odell, you know, a savvy guy that's run a lot of routes. And it's funny when when Odell came, Hood was like, "Dang, that's Odell." You know, it's kind of like he grew up watching Odell play and now he's going to cover him. And we we kind of joked about it in the room with with Hood. So, >> seeing you sprinkle Greg inside a little bit. Uh is that something that is uh >> uh you know, we're just working everybody at that position, especially in our defense. Like the nickel position is super valuable. And we always tell our guys like the more you can do the better. Uh Dinard's deal too is we're positionless defense. So we do a lot of things whether they think Greg's going to go in there and play man, play zone. It's something he's done also in his past. So we're just kind of sprinkling in guys and experimenting with which best 11 we can get out there and some maybe situationally and things like that. But it it was just to see him go do it again because it was in Cleveland when he did it. So um it was just a thing that we were working with with him. >> And so I'm along those lines. Where's our Darius fit? He just seems like a guy. >> Yeah. Uh so yeah, my time obviously with AD last year, uh he's a chess piece. Yeah. He's going to play safety, he's going to play nickel, he can play dime if we needed to him. That's a beautiful thing about our Darius, like in a pinch, he can go play any position on the back end that we would need him to. His mind's kind of wired that right way. He's been in the system obviously for a number of years. So that's kind of how we see a Derry is just he's going to play where we need him to play when we need to. Sorry, but um one thing Addison was talking about was you guys have get better tapes, right? And so you looked at what the guys did last year and wanted to improve on. When you looked at Javon Holland, how would you assess what maybe didn't go great last year that you wanted to see him and where is he at right now? >> Yeah, uh Javon is playing Javon is doing a excellent job right now. Um he is moving well. He's confident. Everything that we want Javon to be, he is being right now. um he's super comfortable in the system. He's super comfortable with what he wants to accomplish and and he knows there were plays he had last year that he wants back and uh we talk about it. We talk about how he's going to improve it, how we're going to work on it and he's in a really good spot right now. >> What did you want to what stood out on the tape? >> I just little fundamental technique stuff and and Javon will tell you there's sometimes he tries to do too much. >> Yeah. and then doesn't end up doing what he's supposed to do, you know, and that and that comes from wanting to make plays and you want guys to want to make plays, but then it's like when the plays come, you make those plays. So, that's more kind of just keeping him in the reigns and then when he has the freedom to do what he wants to do, that's when he can go. >> What's the biggest um part of his learning curve with learning this particular offense? >> I don't think there's much other than just the it's new new language. It would be best I could liken it is, you know, if you speak Italian, you got to learn French. you know, it's really what ultimately what it is. So, he's done a really good job. It's been really fun. It's been a stimulating process, I think, for for everybody involved. >> Thanks, Willie. Uh, and he's he's taken to it really quickly. He's really smart. He studies at it, works at it. So, it's been great. >> You talk about um you start from the ground up. Did you make any just mechanical changes with him or just say do what you're comfortable with? How do you manage that? >> Uh, it's always a conversation. You know, it's you guys get to this level and they got things that they feel good about and comfortable with. um I have things that I think are helpful in that work and it's just a it's a back and forth. It's just like any coaching, you know, working relationship where you're trying to um share thoughts and ideas and hey, sometimes things work for for one guy that don't work for another and you just work through that. So, that's been really good. Uh he's very open and honest and we kind of come from some similar places in terms of what we believe in and what what we think works. So, it's been really pretty easy. Jackson had said, you know, back at the start of the offseason program that, you know, you guys had sat down and, you know, looking over like quarterbacks that you've coached in the past and the idea of rookie pick. How much do you dive into that? He's obviously an eager guy to talk about other guys, but how much do you also want to kind of break away from that and kind of treat this as its own, you know, situation? He's Jackson. He's not any of the guys that >> I think that's exactly what it is is, uh, every quarterback's unique. They have their own strengths. They have their own weaknesses. They have their own things. they need to work on. Um, they all have perspectives that are different. Um, they see the game differently. So, anytime you you're comparing or or trying to make somebody look like somebody else or do something that's that's not just unique to the to the quarterback, I think you get yourself in trouble. So, try really hard to let Jackson be Jackson. He's got a skill set that's unique to him and and he's done a lot of really nice things so far early in his career. And his ability to improve on things, I think, is important. And we had some very direct conversations about what those things are and very specific plan that we had for the spring, what we wanted to get better at and how we wanted to get better at it, what drills we were going to do, how it was going to integrate with what we're going to do, the teamwork. So, it was planned out and and we talked about one of our early meetings, but very very um strategic in that regard and he did a really nice job with it and I think he's gotten better over the course of the spring. I'm looking forward to getting training camp. >> Speaking of a Jackson being Jackson, Jackson ran a lot last year, right? And >> well, yes. Yes. Um, right. Not just ran ran well, but there was a lot of discussion here about riskreward and blue tents and all those things. So, I mean, in an evolution of a young quarterback, does the pocket and throwing out of the pocket become more important or do you let Jackson be Jackson and, you know, if he can run for nine touchdowns, he'll do it again? >> I think there's guys that can use their feet in the league are weapons. Um, his running ability is something that makes him unique, makes him hard to prepare for, makes him hard to defend. That's always going to be a part of his game. I think there's an awareness of when uh when to put yourself at risk, when to when to get out of bounds or when to get down on the ground and not take a hit and when to be smart with the football, too. And those are the things you just point out and you watch them and you watch all the things that that went on over the course of the year and and you maybe get to a point where, hey, look, it's a it's a first and 10. I don't need you to lower your shoulder and try to run through somebody. Just get on the ground or get out of bounds and we'll move on to the next play. Um, but I never want to take that ability for him to affect the game with his legs because it's something that makes him a really dangerous player in the league. So, >> did you see a lot of cases of that when you studied all these things where it's like, okay, I want to talk to him about that one, that one, that one. And did he agree with you that, you know, because last year he could be a little headstrong about, you know, I need to get the first down here. >> Yeah, that yes, I we you just you're honest about it. You approach it pretty straightforward and when you have a chance to point something out like that, you point it out. um you know, we don't always have to agree on on every situation and the best thing is is those are all now in the past and um you know, it's more about what he does moving forward at this point. I think what was really great for him last year uh from a toughness perspective is I think he proved to all of his teammates and the people in this league that he's he's a really tough player um and that there's a time and a place and he's already proved that. So, you know, we can kind of move on from that. I think uh and he's done a really good job of of taking that coaching. He's incredibly coachable. Um he's very open-minded and I think he understands that uh for us to to be the team we want to be, we need him on the field and I think that's really important. >> Much was made about this coaching staff having so many former coaches or people with coaching head coaching experience. So I'm curious when you guys are putting this offense together, how does those personalities mesh where you guys can all be on the same page and have our system as Harbaugh said, >> it's been awesome. I mean I've talk about growth and being stimulated and being excited to come to work every morning. Uh, you know, I I've always been a fan of of coach Naggie from what his his and and what they've done in Kansas City and that system of offense. I mean, I think everybody in the league studies that team every year. You know, we studied that offense for years. Um, I've got a unique perspective on some of the places I've been is different than his. Um, and then you add in Gro and then uh TK and and we got a really really experienced coaching staff and the best part about it is it's there's no ego. And I and I really mean that and that's what's made it so fun. um is is we get all these different ideas and how do we make it ours and what do our players do best and I think we put together a pretty sweet uh starting point to our system and and I'm really excited about it. I think the players are too but we got some really really smart coaches. It's probably the most experienced from top to bottom offensive staff I've been around. Um and it's it's it's stimulating. It's it's exciting. >> Harbs has talked about Jackson wanting every play to be perfect and that's understandable. I would imagine I would I would also think that coaching is about growing pains and figuring out what goes right, why it went wrong, that kind of thing. How have you seen him handle that knowing that, you know, going into year two, he's kind of taken a lot on his shoulders, even more so than what he did last year now with all the newness involved? >> That's a that's a good question. I think the position of in and of itself is is always going to be one of struggle. There's going to be moments where you play really well. always there be moments where you don't make the play and and the spotlight's always on the quarterback um particularly in this city and I think he does a great job of understanding uh his role and what that means for our football team um but also understands how to handle the pressures that come with it and inevitably there's going to be hard times. There's going to be adversity. It's it's not a quarterback play is never linear. It's never you're just consistently doing this all the time. there's es and flows and ups and downs and um that's part of a maturation process for young quarterbacks is learning how to handle those failures, learning how to grow from those moments. Um and that's something that I think he's done a really good job of and he's so poised. Um he's got such a great feel and awareness for his his team and his teammates and and he's so coachable that he's got the makeup to handle all those things really really well. I'm excited to see where he goes from here when it comes to that stuff. But um his ability to take coaching, make corrections, uh make mistakes and then fix them, I think has been really fun. It's been a fun coaching journey this spring. Um you know, as for an example, you know, yesterday we in practice had a very specific, very, very challenging period where we did all fourth downs, so fourth and six to 10. Obviously, not a very high conversion percentage down. Um defense is giving us all kinds of different looks and pressures. It's really hard uh for the quarterbacks. they don't like it. It's very tilted in the favor of the defense. Um, but those are the moments that you can actually, I think, get the most growth in those particular situations because there's there's failure involved and there's there's really hard challenging things that come up that we're doing now that hopefully when we get to those moments in the season, uh, we can nail them and I think that's been a really cool part of the process is he takes that coaching really well. >> Did he nail any of them? >> We had one or two that were pretty dang good. So, that was good to see. The defense nailed a few, too. So, that's usually the way it goes. >> When we asked him, "What do you want to improve?" He he signal like in the pocket getting his reads faster. How do you how do you go about coaching that? >> Uh there's a I think everything is a is a there's a timing and footwork element to everything in the passing game. >> Um if you're if your feet are in rhythm with what the the play design is, whether it's a five step or a seven step or a play action, whatever that timing is for the routes and the route depth with the footwork is I think really really important. Um, along with that is where your eyes are and that and that eye discipline and where you're supposed to look and what you're looking at and why you're looking at it uh also helps that decision-m process and that timing and that that tempo that you want to play with the rhythm in the passing game. So >> the footwork is always is always always always where it's going to start. >> Um, and everybody has their own unique rhythm to their footwork. Not every quarterback is the same. And so you work within those those things. Um, and then you marry that up as as best you can to to how the concepts work. So, I think for him it's it's really been an eyes discipline and footwork consistency have been the two things that we focused a lot on and I think he's he's really answered the bell over the course of the spring. It's been good. >> How in particular would you assess his footwork and his eye discipline right now where he's where he at with us? >> Uh, really pleased where he's at. Um, I think he's he's made some strides and and he did some good. I mean, he naturally does some good things. I mean, it's not >> uh I'm not going to sit here and say that what he did last year is was bad. I mean, there's a lot of good things he did uh and how he did them. So, just trying to build on that and then try to refine it. And to me, the biggest mark for the quarterbacks in this league is how consistent are you with those things and like a snap- to snap basis. Um, and that's what you work on is just how that it never changes. And so your rhythm and timing for whatever the concept requires of you is is consistent over the course of uh of of plays and games and series and weeks and months. That's what you hope for. So that's what we're that's what we're drilling on pretty hard right

title: John Harbaugh on Gearing Up for Training Camp in West Virginia | New York Giants
text: I heard something about a big game. So, we'll be we'll be watching from afar from our TV. No ticket. No ticket. Man, it's going to be crazy down there. It's going to be exciting. So, good luck to the Knicks. Can't wait to see it. >> What questions you have? >> What are you looking for? What do you How do you view the whole away training camp in West Virginia? >> Uh, yeah. I'd look at it like a real opportunity. You know, it's going to be a chance to get locked in. It's a simple place to be. You know, you don't have to deal with coming back and forth from a hotel. Uh you get we obviously we'll get away from the the World Cup stuff and the construction here, which is a plus, too. But for us, but uh that that bonding opportunity, you know, guys aren't going home. Uh they're going to be uh you know, with each other into the evening and stuff like that. Go to dinner together. I think I think it's a real plus for us. I'm excited about it. How beneficial is it to see a New York team having success and how it's treated so your players can see what that's going to be like as you go forward? >> Yeah, I think it's a good thing. It's a good thing, you know, they all the things that those those players are saying there are all the things that our guys are saying, you know, and and they're experiencing the success at the highest level, playing really at the highest level as a team. You know, the best team is the team that plays the best as a team. That's something we said from the beginning and then you see it play out with the Knicks. It's uh it's just really good to see. >> John, when you were hired, you talked about the New York Giants looking like the Giants, right? And and and you like bigized players. Do you like some of the additions you've made? And why is it important to have a big physical team? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, that's uh it's part of it. It's uh you got to have I think Bill Parcell said that these guys are just rare people on the planet, right? along those lines. And uh to me that always stuck with me when I saw that way back when, you know, and they have to have to be successful as a football player in this league, you have to have certain traits. So being big is a trait, being long is a trait, being athletic is a trait, being physical, you know, having strong hands, those are traits. Being fast is a trait, having be able to change direction, being fluid, being extremely coordinated. You know, some people just have a knack, you would say. It's there's an athleticism to that as well. quarterback traits. All the quarterback traits, off platform throws, touch throws, layered throws, those are things that are are are past arm strength, you know. So the players come in all different shapes and sizes, but they have to have traits, you know, toughness is a trait, you know, endurance is a trait, resilience is a trait. So kind of looking for all those things and hopefully it's wrapped up in the best player, you know, and who's the best player? The best player is a player who plays the best, you know, and that's what you look for in the end. >> Healthwise, maybe aside from the league, any of the guys we didn't see all spring, anything that was a concern could linger into camp. >> I can never think off the top of my head. >> Cam Jones, and Sam Roberts, we didn't really see after >> Cam Jones had a had a an incident moving his uh moving his house up here. He should be fine like in a week. >> Uh Clayton, Lucas, Patrick, >> Collins. Well, yeah. Give me one at a time. I won't be able to remember them all. >> Fedoni had is still coming back from the foot thing. He had a little deal with that thing in there. Uh, it's uh it's it's going to it got cleaned up, I think, yesterday or today. It's like a twoe cleanup. So, he should be good for training camp. Fingers crossed on that one. >> Who else? >> Sam Roberts. >> Sam Roberts is just on track. He uh he's on track. He should be in there in training camp. Start training camp to a degree, then ramp up from the start of training camp. Bo Collins >> Bo was dealing with hamstring that he's working through just he's he should be fine. Kubas Lucas Patrick Slen >> Lucas Patrick yeah he had he's got he's got old guy stuff old guys have stuff as you well know >> calling me old it's fine >> what's the old thing I resemble that remark >> talking to me about this >> what about Malik like what's the what's the plan for him now like what does he do the next three months to try to not three months sorry six weeks to get himself ready three months for the season that's what I was thinking to get himself ready for you know the summer >> well I think he does everything he And uh from what he told me, he said his plan is to be here most of the time. Almost all the time he'll be here. Uh I believe I'm sure he'll do he won't be here all the time, but he's going to be here a lot working really hard. He's making really good progress right now. So, you know, I'm very hopeful that uh that he'll be he'll be back soon. But I also understand, you know, you come back from a knee, there's going to be he could be he'll be back and then he'll still be building his way back to where he's, you know, his ultimate full strength self. So, but uh he's doing great. He's doing a great job. Obviously made some real good progress in the last few weeks. >> Are you any more optimistic now about Malik as far as the beginning of the season? >> I wasn't less optimistic before, you know, just it's like I said, I said it's it's a slog. It's a grind. You know, he's he's he's still in the middle of it. It's still he's probably not in the middle of it now. He's probably maybe 70% through. I don't know, something like that. But he's 80% through. But he's uh he's still grinding. You know, it's going to be a grind. He starts playing again, too, to get to get it back right. the news this spring. I don't think we ever asked you about Joe getting the extension. Just curious what your reaction was to that. >> Yeah, I was happy. You know, uh I think he's he's he's a good guy. Enjoy working with him and looking forward to what uh you know, what we all can do together, you know, and uh that's that's a that's a good thing. >> What if any input did you have on that? >> Uh they asked me, you know, if I like Joe and I thought he did a good job, I said, "Yeah, you know, but it's it's it's uh it's it's the decision of the the people I respect. I respect, you know, the the ownership group, you know, that's that's their call and uh that's their call and they made it and I respect it. I think it's a good decision. I agree with it. But uh you know, I think I think that's uh it's good. I'm excited. >> Two more. When you assemble this coaching staff, you talked about, you know, making it our system. So, I'm curious as you look at what Na and Callahan and Tagger and these guys have done with this offense. How would you assess what they've done, how the team's responded so far getting adjusted to it? Yeah, I like the system that we're building. I think the system is really good. I think it's it's continues to be built. Uh the next step is going to be honing in a little bit in training camp about our identity, you know, and how we you know what we're going to be really best at, especially the first, you know, three to five games and and really getting good at those things. But, uh great system, great coaches, great teachers. I feel really good about it. >> Anything more that you learned about the leadership of this team and the players as you camp? >> Well, yeah, I learned a lot over the course of the whole, four months, five months. title: Nick Emmanwori: "I'm Just Trying To Evolve My Game" | Seattle Seahawks
text: You guys see a lot of work with the edge guys here, especially today. How big of a priority is that for you now going into year two, adding more versatility to your game? >> Uh, yeah. I'm just trying to evolve my game just like how the NFL game is evolving, you know? So, I'm trying to just be the front runner and uh lead in that way. So, I'm working with, you know, the edge edges and uh y'all seen laws out there giving me tips and just, you know, trying to get me going in that in that uh lane. >> You always hear, you know, talk about the big league players can make year one, year two. Your year one was obviously really good. What are you looking to improve upon? >> Uh I think I'm looking to just be more of a complete player. like, you know, a lot of the stuff last year as a rook, I was like, you know, maybe like after like week eight or nine, I started like noticing formations and stuff. So, I'm trying to, you know, week one, I'm trying to notice stuff and be be ahead of the game so I can just play fast and uh make more plays and uh just more just finish more and just uh more impactful plays every drive. >> How much more how much better equipped do you feel to be able to handle all these different roles? Like last year, Coach McDonald talked about how just throwing so much at you during the week. How much better equipped do you feel for that? I feel I feel really equipped uh you know in the practices and the film and stuff. I'm kind of like ahead of the plays and the coaches are coming to me like yeah you know you're ahead of that play keep going uh keep building on that track but uh I wouldn't say it's night and day you know I think I did a really good job last year but I'm definitely ahead of the curve now and starting to feel the game way more. What kind of teachers Demarcus Warren, what's he teaching you in particular? >> Uh, just how to win. Uh, you know, especially with my gifts and my ability, just how to win easy, not making it too complicated. Uh, with a guy like him, he's done it for so long. So, like, you know, anything he says is kind of like green and and good to go. So, I'm just uh soaking up as much game as I can from him and uh learning. So, he's just he's just giving me what what what he got. So >> when you think think back on maybe where you were this time last year to now you're Super Bowl champion, played a key role on a Super Bowl champion, all that. Does it seem does it seem like yeah, I kind of expected all that to happen or does it seem really like >> Oddly enough, yeah, it kind of feels like you know this is how things were supposed to be. So I'm not I don't wake up surprised about what position I'm in or what we did as a team. Like it feels good like looking back on the past like you know we had a great season and it was fun like you know just great ball top to bottom. But you know I'm not surprised. I don't wake up surprised. >> Looking back at the Super Bowl, what was it like playing? >> It was it was a little, you know, my mind I kind of made my mind up about playing because it was like, you know, for me personally, it probably would have sucked just to go throughout the whole season, all the ups and downs, uh, everything we done been through just to not playing the Super Bowl. So, I made my decision to play that night and uh it felt good going out there and playing like uh you know uh had my teammate support and uh I mean you know we we dominated out there so it's pretty pretty pretty easy for me to just be out there and just do what I can do. >> How limited were you that night? >> Uh honestly I was full go. So when I went out there I did pregame warm-ups and I I went a little hard in pregame warm-ups. I think I went a little too hard and I was like really pushing my ankle and it was like you know it was holding up. was good and uh we're all we're all good now. So >> So you weren't limited post Super Bowl or had to shut it down or anything? >> Nah, you know, I mean, of course, after the Super Bowl ended, just had to recover uh you know, stayed in Seattle for a little bit while everybody left back to the East Coast, recovered, did what I had to do uh in the offseason. Did did rehab a lot just to fortify my ankle, make sure there was no problems right now. So >> what did this offseason look like for you? Last year you had draft prep and everything was crazy kind of way it is after the college season ends. what did you kind of do to kind of set an offseason plan for yourself and what would you kind of try to take care of? >> Honestly, yeah, this first offseason, you know, they kind of say you have so much time on your hands, you don't really know what to do with it. And, you know, I kind of understood that, but since he went so far, it was kind of like the weeks were kind of like just just get what you can from it. So, uh, honestly, I know my next offseason I'll be way more better equipped and like move with better pace and stuff, but this offseason was a little little not crazy. It was it was a good offseason, but you know, just being my first offseason, it was a little little little extra. >> Anything else? >> Thanks, D. >> All right. Appreciate it. Jack.

title: Drew Allar PROGRESS UPDATE, sleeper CB, Riley Nowakowski role | Steelers Reward
text: What's going on, everybody? Steelers' OTAs, last week here before the Steelers break, and that is a 7-week break between now and training camp. It will not start until late July. Pittsburgh Steelers didn't have a lot of veterans here. There were still some here, guys like Chukwuma Okorafor, Troy Fautanu, most of the O-line was here. Um but a lot of guys weren't here. So, you got a lot of younger players getting more and more reps. Um we see a lot of Drew Allar and Will Howard today, and that was a big topic. Mike McCarthy saying, you know, the QB school stuff is being built out. They showed Tom Arthurs, Steelers' quarterback coach, his progression throughout the year with Green Bay. They showed Aaron Rodgers' from when he was young and where he went. And now they show Drew Allar's and Will Howard's, and Drew Allar is starting to already see some change in his footwork, some change in his mechanics. He also is working with John Beck, uh QB trainer, for about a year or so. Mike McCarthy's worked with him in the past. Um and they are really focused on that footwork. And And Drew Allar said the biggest difference for him right now, he feels like he's not thinking as much. He thinks that, you know, the mental side of his game, eye manipulation, uh understanding post-snap reads and rotations from teams, is becoming a lot more crisp. Um and just becoming a lot easier to kind of all process down and parse. Um and then the footwork stuff, obviously staying in a rhythm, very, very important. But he feels like it's going to be something that's going to continue to grow. The accuracy part still isn't necessarily there, but it doesn't need to be when you're starting to get down the accuracy and rebuilding from the base. But a lot of progress, Mike McCarthy feels like has been made over the last uh few weeks with him in there. I continue to say, you know, Daylen Everett is sticking out. But another corner I want to shout out that maybe you guys don't know. De'Nico Slaughter. They signed this guy as a futures deal, but he can play slot, he can play outside, he can play safety. He can do a little bit of everything. They have him playing the slot right now. Has a very quiet confidence about him. He's been getting some first-team reps um as part of that young guy crew with Everett. And he's made some real plays in this spring period. So, definitely someone I didn't have on my radar coming into OTAs and mini camp, but someone that has come on. I talked to him today, and he seems like a guy that is really calm, collected, and is ready to prove himself. Even if he doesn't make the team, a sure fire practice squad candidate to me. Also talked to Riley Nowakowski today for a little bit. You know, playing fullback, playing tight end, playing H-back. He feels like he can do more than just fullback. He feels like he can be flexed out and you know, run seam routes and do different things like that run wheel routes, be a real red zone threat. So, there's more to his game that he believes can be unleashed, and we'll see. I think he's going to be somebody that gets used a lot among this rookie class. All right, folks.
